# Neon Design System Components

This document provides comprehensive documentation for components of the Neon Design System, including props, slots, and usage examples.

## Component Index

### NeonAccordion

collapsible content container that allows users to show and hide sections of related content.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonAccordion component when you need to:
- Display content that can be collapsed and expanded to save space
- Organize related information into sections that can be viewed independently
- Create FAQ sections with questions that expand to show answers
- Implement progressive disclosure of complex information
- Reduce visual complexity by hiding secondary content until requested
- Group form sections that aren't all required at once
- Create expandable/collapsible sections within a drawer or modal
- Present a list of independently accessible content sections in a compact format
NeonAccordion is ideal for presenting multiple sections of content in a limited space, allowing users to focus on specific sections as needed. For navigation between completely separate views of content, consider NeonTabs instead. For very simple toggle visibility, a basic show/hide button might be more appropriate.


### NeonAiChatLauncher

component that provides a user-friendly interface for interacting with AI assistants, featuring speech-to-text capabilities and customizable visual styles.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonAiChatLauncher component when you need to:
- Create an entry point for AI chat functionality within your application
- Provide users with a simple way to ask questions or request assistance
- Implement a modern, accessible interface for AI interactions
- Collect user input before launching a more comprehensive AI experience
- Add speech-to-text capability for hands-free interactions
- Create a branded AI launcher that matches your application's theme
- Provide suggestions based on user input to guide interactions
- Handle error states and loading indicators for AI functionality
- Integrate AI capabilities in a user-friendly, unobtrusive way
- Create consistent AI interaction points across your application
NeonAiChatLauncher is designed to serve as the primary entry point for AI interaction within your application. Its clean, focused interface is optimized for capturing user input and integrating with AI processing systems.


### NeonAppHeader

top-level navigation component that provides consistent header styling and functionality across an application.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonAppHeader component when you need to:
- Create a consistent application header with branding elements
- Provide primary navigation at the top of your application
- Display a header with a logo and application title
- Add utility elements like search, notification icons, or avatar menus in the header
- Implement a header with customizable center and right sections
- Create a header with optional subheading text
- Provide a clickable home link functionality
- Establish a professional and unified application branding
NeonAppHeader is the primary header component in the Neon Design System. It provides a consistent and accessible way to implement application headers with branding and navigation elements.


### NeonAppNavIcon

specialized icon component designed specifically for application navigation with pre-defined navigation icons.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonAppNavIcon component when you need to:
- Display navigation icons specifically designed for application menus
- Create consistent navigation icons throughout your application
- Use specialized icons for common application sections like overview, calendar, gradebook, etc.
- Implement navigation icons that are part of the Neon Design System's app navigation
- Maintain visual consistency in application navigation elements
- Use application-specific icons that are optimized for navigation contexts
NeonAppNavIcon is designed specifically for application navigation contexts and provides specialized icons for common application sections. For general icon usage, consider using the standard NeonIcon component instead.


### NeonAppNavSwitcher

dropdown component for switching between entities such as users, schools, or classes within an application navigation system.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonAppNavSwitcher component when you need to:
- Allow users to switch between different entities or profiles in an application
- Provide a consistent entity selection interface across various applications
- Display user profiles with names, avatars, and metadata
- Group related entities like schools, classrooms, or users in a selectable dropdown
- Integrate with NeonAppNav for a complete application navigation experience
- Present entity information with optional images, avatars, and metadata
- Support multiple entity types with consistent visual presentation
- Enable quick switching between different contexts within the same application
- Display entity lists with pagination for larger collections
NeonAppNavSwitcher is designed to work with the NeonAppNav component to provide a complete navigation experience. It's particularly useful for applications that require users to switch between different contexts like schools, classrooms, or user profiles.


### NeonAppNav

navigation component that provides a hierarchical, collapsible navigation structure for applications, including support for multi-level navigation items, user information, and app switching functionality.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonAppNav component when you need to:
- Create a consistent, accessible application navigation structure
- Display a hierarchical navigation system with support for multiple levels
- Provide user information and user-specific menu options
- Allow users to switch between different applications or contexts
- Implement a standard navigation pattern across your application
- Support both desktop and mobile navigation experiences
- Create a navigation system with icons, text, and optional visual indicators
- Enable users to navigate between different sections of your application
NeonAppNav is the primary navigation component in the Neon Design System, designed to provide a consistent navigation experience across applications with support for multiple navigation patterns and responsive behaviors.


### NeonAvatarButton

button component designed to display user avatars and initials, providing a clickable interface for profile menus and user actions.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonAvatarButton component when you need to:
- Create a profile or user menu trigger in your application
- Display a user's avatar as a clickable button element
- Implement user account navigation in headers or navigation bars
- Provide an accessible, clickable avatar for user profile actions
- Create a visual representation of the current user with interactivity
- Implement dropdown menus attached to an avatar
- Add user-related actions to navigation areas with limited space
- Create a compact user interface element that represents the logged-in user
NeonAvatarButton is often used in application headers, navigation bars, and settings panels to provide quick access to user-related actions. It's commonly paired with NeonMenu to create dropdown menus containing options like account settings or logout functionality.


### NeonAvatarStack

component that displays a collection of avatars in a visually compact grouping with automatic handling of overflow.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonAvatarStack component when you need to:
- Display a group of users or participants in a visual format
- Show multiple user avatars in a compact, space-efficient way
- Represent team members, collaborators, or participants in a project
- Display a list of users where seeing their profile pictures is helpful for recognition
- Create a visually appealing representation of group membership
- Show user involvement in discussions, tasks, or shared content
- Save horizontal space when displaying multiple user avatars
- Automatically handle the display of many users with an overflow mechanism
NeonAvatarStack is ideal for situations where you need to visually represent multiple users in a space-efficient way. The component automatically handles overflow when there are more users than can be displayed, providing a count and optional menu to see additional users.


### NeonAvatar

versatile avatar component that displays user representation through initials or profile pictures with various styling options.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonAvatar component when you need to:
- Display a visual representation of a user or entity within an application
- Show user profile pictures or generate visual representations using initials
- Create consistent user identification across the user interface
- Provide visual cues for user-related content or actions
- Represent users in comment sections, user lists, or messaging interfaces
- Add user identification to headers, profiles, or navigation components
- Display user presence in collaborative applications
- Create visual hierarchies of users with different sizes of avatars
- Implement user-focused UI elements with consistent styling and behavior
NeonAvatar is a foundational component for representing users throughout the Neon Design System. It supports displaying either profile pictures or automatically generating visual representations using user initials. For situations requiring user interaction with avatars, consider using NeonAvatarButton or NeonAvatarStack for displaying groups of users.


### NeonBadge

small, versatile status indicator component for displaying counts, notifications, or status indicators.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonBadge component when you need to:
- Display a notification count or numerical indicator
- Show the number of items in a collection or category
- Indicate the presence of new or unread content
- Create a small visual indicator with color coding
- Add status indicators to interface elements
- Highlight that an element has associated notifications
- Show a small count indicator next to navigation items or buttons
- Display alerts or notifications that require minimal screen space
- Create a small visual marker in different colors to indicate status
- Show numerical values in a compact, visually distinct way
NeonBadge is designed to be a lightweight visual indicator that can be used in various contexts throughout your application to provide quick status information or numerical counts.


### NeonBreadcrumbs

navigation component that displays a hierarchical trail of links showing the user's current location within the application.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonBreadcrumbs component when you need to:
- Provide users with context about their location within the application hierarchy
- Allow users to navigate back to previous levels in the navigation hierarchy
- Create clear navigational paths for deep or complex application structures
- Help users understand their current position relative to the overall site structure
- Enable quick backward navigation to parent pages
- Implement SEO-friendly navigation patterns
- Support users in understanding the relationship between different sections
- Improve overall user orientation within multi-level navigation systems
- Allow users to quickly jump to previously visited sections without using browser controls
NeonBreadcrumbs is a standard navigation pattern that enhances user orientation and provides efficient navigation options in multi-level applications. It works especially well when an application has clearly defined hierarchical levels or when users need to navigate between related sections.


### NeonButtonFooter

versatile button footer component that provides a standardized way to display action buttons in containers such as cards, dialogs, drawers, and layouts.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonButtonFooter component when you need to:
- Display primary and secondary actions at the bottom of a container
- Create a consistent layout for action buttons across your application
- Group related buttons with clear visual hierarchy
- Provide a tertiary action (like delete) that should be visually separated
- Present complex button patterns like button menus or split buttons
- Implement responsive button layouts that adapt to mobile screens
- Create a clear separation between content and actions
NeonButtonFooter is primarily used inside container components like NeonCardStandard, NeonModalDialog, NeonModalDrawer, and NeonLayoutDetail, typically placed in their footer slots.


### NeonButtonGroup

component that displays a group of related buttons in a unified, selectable control with either horizontal or vertical layout.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonButtonGroup component when you need to:
- Create a set of related toggle buttons that function as a single control
- Provide users with a visual way to select one option from a set of choices
- Implement filtering or sorting controls that allow users to switch between different views
- Display multiple related actions in a compact and organized layout
- Create segmented controls for toggling between different states
- Provide a user interface for single-selection from a small set of options
- Implement tabs-like navigation in space-constrained areas
- Display mode switchers (like view modes or display options)
NeonButtonGroup is ideal for situations where radio buttons would be too formal or take up too much space, but a clear selection from multiple options is needed.


### NeonButtonSplit

split button component that combines a primary action button with a dropdown menu of additional options.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonButtonSplit component when you need to:
- Provide a primary action with related secondary actions
- Save screen space by combining multiple related actions in one component
- Present a default or most common action prominently with additional options
- Group related actions where one action is performed more frequently than others
- Implement a primary call-to-action with contextual alternatives
- Create a hierarchical button that clearly distinguishes between main and secondary actions
- Provide quick access to a set of related commands without navigating to a new page
- Reduce cognitive load by keeping related options accessible but not immediately visible
NeonButtonSplit is ideal for situations where there is a primary action users will perform most often, but there are additional related actions that should be accessible when needed. It combines the clarity of a standard button with the flexibility of a dropdown menu.


### NeonButton

versatile button component that serves as the primary interactive element for user actions in the Neon Design System.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonButton component when you need to:
- Trigger an action or event when clicked
- Submit a form
- Navigate to another page or external link
- Provide user controls for interactive features
- Create primary call-to-action elements
- Provide affordance for user interactions
- Create a visually consistent set of action controls
- Implement accessible interactive elements
NeonButton is the foundational button component in the Neon Design System and supports various styles, states, and configurations. It can be used standalone or as part of button groups, forms, cards, and other container components.


### NeonCardAction

clickable card component for navigation or selection that features icons, tags, headings, and interactive elements.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonCardAction component when you need to:
- Create interactive cards that navigate to different views or activate actions
- Display a visual representation of an action or option that users can select
- Group related action information with visual indicators like icons and tags
- Implement clickable navigation tiles or action cards in your application
- Create selectable option cards with consistent styling
- Present action options with supporting text and visual elements
- Add user avatars or selection dropdowns to action cards
- Create AI action cards with distinct styling
NeonCardAction is designed for interactive card experiences that lead to further actions. It features a prominent chevron icon to indicate its actionable nature and supports various interactive elements like selection dropdowns and avatar stacks.


### NeonCardHeader

versatile header component for cards that provides consistent styling with support for colors, icons, tags, and avatars.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonCardHeader component when you need to:
- Create visually distinct headers for card components
- Apply consistent branding or category colors to card headers
- Include icons, avatars, or tags in card headers to provide additional context
- Create cohesive section headers within a card-based interface
- Highlight different content categories with color-coded headers
- Add visual hierarchy to card elements
- Group related information with a distinctive heading element
- Enhance card components with a professional, branded appearance
NeonCardHeader is designed to be used as a header element within NeonCardStandard or other card components. It provides a standardized way to display headings with visual enhancements like colors, icons, tags, and avatars.


### NeonCardMedia

specialized card component designed for displaying media content (images, illustrations, or icons) with accompanying text and interactive elements.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonCardMedia component when you need to:
- Display content that prominently features visual media alongside text
- Create cards with images, illustrations, or icons as a focal point
- Implement media-rich interactive cards for selection or navigation
- Present content in both vertical (media above content) or horizontal (media beside content) layouts
- Create visual navigation elements that require imagery
- Display media content with consistent aspect ratios across your interface
- Build selectable card interfaces that include visual elements
- Present media content with optional header, body content, and footer actions
NeonCardMedia is ideal for creating visually engaging content cards that feature images or other media prominently. It extends the functionality of the standard card component with specialized features for media display and layout control.


### NeonCardSelectable

selectable card component that provides interactive selection functionality with checkbox or radio button controls, while maintaining a consistent card design pattern.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonCardSelectable component when you need to:
- Allow users to select one or more options from a set of visually rich choices
- Create a more engaging and visually appealing alternative to standard radio buttons or checkboxes
- Display selectable items with supporting content, icons, or illustrations
- Implement a visually consistent selection pattern for complex content
- Group related information in a selectable container
- Create an interactive card-based selection experience
- Offer users radio button functionality (select one from many) in a card format
- Provide checkbox functionality (select multiple) in a card format
- Create a card that can be clicked/tapped as a whole to trigger selection
NeonCardSelectable extends the functionality of standard card components by adding selection capabilities, making it ideal for scenarios where users need to choose between visually rich options rather than simple text-based choices.


### NeonCardStandard

versatile card component for displaying content in a contained, styled container with consistent elevation and spacing.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonCardStandard component when you need to:
- Group related content or information together in a visually distinct container
- Create clear visual separation between different sections on a page
- Display content that belongs together in a logical unit
- Implement a consistent container design throughout your application
- Present content in a clean, bordered container with optional header and footer
- Create layouts with multiple content cards that need consistent styling
- Implement content containers with consistent elevation and shadow effects
- Display information that should be visually separated from the page background
NeonCardStandard is the foundational card component in the Neon Design System and serves as a versatile container for various types of content. Use it whenever you need to visually group related information. For more specialized card use cases, consider NeonCardSelectable for making selectable cards or NeonCardMedia for cards with media content.


### NeonCheckboxField

group of checkbox options that allows users to select multiple values from a list of choices.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonCheckboxField component when you need to:
- Allow users to select multiple options from a list of choices
- Present a list of related, non-mutually exclusive options
- Create toggleable settings or feature selections
- Implement multi-select functionality within forms
- Create hierarchical selection interfaces with parent-child relationships
- Allow users to enable/disable multiple features or options
- Create selection lists with additional helper text for each option
- Implement toggle switches for multiple related settings
NeonCheckboxField is ideal when users need to select any number of options from a group (including none, one, or many). For single selection from a list of options, use NeonRadioField instead. For a single checkbox option, use NeonCheckboxSingle.


### NeonCheckboxSingle

versatile standalone checkbox component that supports multiple display styles, states, and customization options.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonCheckboxSingle component when you need to:
- Allow users to make a binary choice (yes/no, true/false)
- Create a standalone checkbox control for a single option
- Implement a toggle switch for enabling/disabling a feature
- Display a checkbox in an indeterminate state (partially selected)
- Create customized checkbox controls with special icons
- Display a checkbox that needs to be larger and more prominent
- Create a standalone clickable icon that behaves like a checkbox
- Add a checkbox to a form with consistent styling and behavior
- Create an accessible checkbox control with proper labeling
NeonCheckboxSingle is intended for individual checkbox controls. For multiple related checkboxes, consider using NeonCheckboxField instead.


### NeonChipMultiSelectField

form field component that allows users to select multiple options from a set of choices, displaying each selection as a chip (tag).

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonChipMultiSelectField component when you need to:
- Allow users to select multiple options from a predefined list
- Display selected options as interactive chips/tags that can be toggled on and off
- Present a more visual and space-efficient alternative to standard checkboxes
- Show selected options in a compact, scannable format
- Allow users to quickly toggle selections with minimal clicks
- Provide a visually engaging multi-selection interface
- Create a form field that clearly indicates multiple selections are allowed
- Present options in a horizontal layout that can wrap to new lines when space is limited
- Support selection of multiple items from categories, tags, filters, or attributes
NeonChipMultiSelectField is ideal for scenarios where you need a more visually appealing and compact alternative to checkbox lists or multi-select dropdowns. It's especially useful when the selected items benefit from being immediately visible and interactive.


### NeonChipSelectField

component that displays selectable options as interactive chips with dropdown functionality, allowing users to make a single selection from a group of choices.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonChipSelectField component when you need to:
- Present a set of options as interactive chips that users can select from
- Allow users to choose a single option from multiple choices
- Display selectable options in a compact, visual format
- Provide selection functionality in a space-efficient manner
- Create a more engaging selection interface than standard radio buttons or dropdown menus
- Show options that benefit from visual recognition and selection
- Implement a modern, chip-based selection pattern in forms
- Conserve space while maintaining clear option visibility
- Present categorical options that work well with the chip visual metaphor
NeonChipSelectField is particularly effective when the options are relatively short labels that can fit well within chips, and when you want to make all options visible at once rather than hidden in a dropdown.


### NeonChipSelectSingle

toggleable chip component that displays as a selectable, contained element with an optional icon and label text. It provides a visually distinct way to make boolean selections.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonChipSelectSingle component when you need to:
- Create a visually distinct toggle control that appears as a chip/pill
- Provide a checkbox-like functionality with a more prominent visual treatment
- Allow users to select/deselect a single option
- Present a compact, contained selection control with clear visual feedback
- Show selection state with a more engaging visual treatment than a standard checkbox
- Create space-efficient toggle controls that don't require traditional checkbox styling
- Implement selections that benefit from the chip/pill visual metaphor
- Display toggles with custom icons or indicators
NeonChipSelectSingle acts as a specialized selection control that combines checkbox functionality with a chip/pill visual appearance. It's particularly useful when you need a more visually prominent selection mechanism that provides clear state indication in a compact format.


### NeonChipSet

component for displaying and managing a collection of chips, handling overflow and clear-all functionality.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonChipSet component when you need to:
- Display a collection of related items as compact, interactive chips
- Allow users to view and remove selected items or filters
- Manage multiple selections in limited space with automatic overflow handling
- Show selected options from multi-select fields
- Present filter selections or tags with the ability to remove individual items
- Create token-based input interfaces with removable elements
- Display multiple selected items in a compact, scannable format
- Provide users with the ability to clear all selections at once
- Represent complex hierarchical selections as simple, manageable tokens
NeonChipSet is designed to manage groups of chip elements efficiently, with smart overflow handling that automatically creates a menu for chips that don't fit in the available space. It's an excellent choice when you need to display multiple selections or filters in a limited space.


### NeonChip

compact, interactive component used to display discrete information, represent selected items, or trigger actions.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonChip component when you need to:
- Display selected items or values in a compact format
- Create removable tags or labels
- Indicate the status of an item
- Display contact or user information with an avatar
- Create interactive filters or categories
- Present multiple discrete values in a limited space
- Show items that can be individually removed from a collection
- Represent selected options in multi-selection interfaces
NeonChip is ideal for representing discrete data points, selected values, or options in a compact, visually distinctive format. For multiple chips, consider using NeonChipSet to manage collections of chips.


### NeonDateField

form field component for selecting and inputting dates with an accompanying calendar picker.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonDateField component when you need to:
- Allow users to select a specific date from a calendar interface
- Collect date information in a standardized format
- Validate that user input conforms to date requirements
- Enforce date constraints such as min/max allowed dates
- Create form fields that require date selection
- Implement date input with a visual calendar picker
- Present date selection in a localized format
NeonDateField is ideal for forms requiring date selection with visual confirmation. It combines text input with a calendar UI to ensure accurate date selection. If you need to collect a date range instead of a single date, consider using NeonDateRangeField instead.


### NeonDatePicker

versatile date picker component that allows users to select dates from a calendar interface with support for single date, multiple dates, or date range selection.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonDatePicker component when you need to:
- Allow users to select a specific date from a calendar view
- Enable selection of multiple individual dates
- Allow users to select a date range with start and end dates
- Provide an intuitive calendar interface for date selection
- Validate dates against custom business rules
- Restrict date selection to specific ranges (min/max values)
- Allow selection of only weekdays
- Create interactive date selection interfaces within forms or dialogs
- Provide a consistent date selection experience across your application
NeonDatePicker is the core date selection component in the Neon Design System and offers flexible modes to handle different date selection requirements. Use it when you need a full calendar interface for date selection. For simpler date input with text fields, consider NeonDateField.


### NeonDateRangeField

form component that allows users to select a date range with start and end dates through a visual calendar interface.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonDateRangeField component when you need to:
- Collect a range of dates from users (start date and end date)
- Allow users to select date ranges for reservations or bookings
- Create date filters with start and end parameters
- Define date ranges for reporting or analytics
- Set scheduling periods with clear start and end points
- Create event planning interfaces that require duration selection
- Implement date-based search functionality with range parameters
- Define term dates, enrollment periods, or any time-bounded activity
- Collect date ranges where the relationship between start and end dates is important
- Provide a user-friendly alternative to entering two separate dates manually
NeonDateRangeField is built on top of NeonDateField and NeonDatePicker components. It combines two date inputs with calendar pickers in a single, cohesive interface that ensures the start date logically precedes the end date.


### NeonEllipsis

component that truncates text with an ellipsis when it exceeds a specified number of lines, and displays the full text in a tooltip on hover.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonEllipsis component when you need to:
- Display text that might overflow its container in a clean, controlled way
- Limit text to a specific number of lines with an ellipsis at the end when truncated
- Show the full text content in a tooltip when the user hovers over truncated text
- Maintain a consistent text layout when dealing with variable-length content
- Prevent text overflow from breaking your UI layout
- Present lengthy text content in a space-efficient manner
- Enhance readability in UI elements with limited space
- Implement responsive text behavior across different screen sizes
NeonEllipsis is an essential utility component for managing text overflow in the Neon Design System. It provides a clean solution for displaying content that might be too long for its container while still making the full content accessible via tooltip.


### NeonErrorCardContent

component for displaying error states and empty states with an illustration, message, and optional action buttons.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonErrorCardContent component when you need to:
- Display errors in retrieving or processing data within a card or section
- Create user-friendly empty state messages with visual indicators
- Provide error feedback with options for users to retry or take other actions
- Show a standardized error presentation within your application
- Create consistent error states across different components and pages
- Present error messages with supporting illustrations for better user comprehension
- Implement empty state messaging for when content is not available
- Guide users with clear actions to resolve error conditions
NeonErrorCardContent is designed to be used both standalone and within container components like NeonCardStandard. It combines an illustration, error message, and action buttons to create a comprehensive error or empty state display.


### NeonErrorPageContent

component for displaying error pages with consistent styling and customizable content for various HTTP error codes and custom error states.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonErrorPageContent component when you need to:
- Display standardized error pages for common HTTP error codes (403, 404, 408, 500)
- Create custom error states with your own heading, subheading, and body content
- Provide users with clear information about an error that has occurred
- Include visual illustrations or custom media with error messages
- Add action buttons for users to retry operations or navigate elsewhere
- Present errors in a consistent, branded format across your application
- Ensure error messages are accessible and user-friendly
NeonErrorPageContent is part of the Neon Design System and provides predefined content for common error codes while allowing for complete customization when needed. Use it to display errors in a consistent, professional manner that aligns with your application's design language.


### NeonFilePicker

component for uploading files with various display options, including a button interface and a drag-and-drop zone.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonFilePicker component when you need to:
- Allow users to upload files to your application
- Provide a simple button interface for file selection
- Offer drag-and-drop functionality for easier file uploads
- Display a list of selected files with optional thumbnails
- Restrict uploads to specific file types or extensions
- Validate files based on custom requirements
- Create form fields that accept file uploads
- Display visual feedback for uploaded files
- Support both single and multiple file selection
- Create a user-friendly file upload experience
NeonFilePicker is the primary file upload component in the Neon Design System. It offers flexible configuration options for different upload scenarios and integrates with form validation systems.


### NeonFloatingActionButton

floating action button (FAB) component that provides a persistent, circular button typically used for primary or assistive actions, with optional expanding content panel.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonFloatingActionButton component when you need to:
- Provide easy access to a key action across various screens
- Create a persistent chatbot or AI assistant interface
- Allow users to quickly access help or support functionality
- Implement a collapsible panel for information or interaction
- Display a notification indicator for new messages or updates
- Create a consistently positioned interactive element
- Provide an assistive interface component that remains accessible across different screens
- Implement a floating chat or feedback mechanism
NeonFloatingActionButton is designed to provide quick access to important functions while minimizing screen real estate usage. It's especially useful for AI assistants, support chats, or other features that should be persistently available but not intrusive.


### NeonFooter

standard footer component that displays copyright information, navigation links, and optional address details.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonFooter component when you need to:
- Display consistent footer information across your application
- Include standard legal links such as privacy policy and terms of service
- Show organizational address information
- Provide copyright attribution at the bottom of your pages
- Implement a standardized page footer that matches the Neon Design System
- Create a clear visual separation between page content and footer information
- Add required legal and policy links to comply with regulations
- Display contact information for an organization or institution
NeonFooter should be used at the bottom of your application pages to provide consistent footer information and navigation links. It's designed to be part of your overall page layout and works best when used with other Neon Design System components.


### NeonFullPageSkeleton

loading state component that displays placeholder content while data is being fetched or processed, providing visual feedback to users during loading operations with various layout options.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonFullPageSkeleton component when you need to:
- Indicate to users that content is loading without showing a blank screen
- Maintain user engagement during data fetching operations
- Provide a visual preview of the page structure before content loads
- Improve perceived performance by showing content placeholders
- Create a smooth transition between loading and loaded states
- Display appropriate loading states for different types of content layouts (tables, calendars, grades, assignments, etc.)
- Reduce user frustration during network delays
- Implement a consistent loading experience across your application
NeonFullPageSkeleton is designed to mimic the layout of various content types, showing placeholder elements that match the expected content structure. This helps users understand what kind of content to expect while waiting for actual data to load.


### NeonGradeBlock

simple component for displaying grades or scores in a colored block with optional percentage value.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonGradeBlock component when you need to:
- Display academic grades or scores in a visually consistent way
- Show performance metrics with both a letter grade and percentage
- Create visual indicators of status or performance levels
- Display grades in a compact, color-coded format
- Indicate assessment results in education or evaluation contexts
- Provide quick visual feedback on performance metrics
NeonGradeBlock is designed to display simple grade data with optional percentage values in a colored block. It's ideal for dashboards, report cards, assessment summaries, or anywhere you need to display grades or performance indicators visually.


### NeonIconCustom

component for registering custom SVG icons that can be used with the Neon Icon system.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonIconCustom component when you need to:
- Add custom SVG icons to your application that aren't available in the standard icon set
- Integrate product-specific or app-specific iconography into your application
- Use branded or specialized icons that follow your design system
- Create a custom icon library for use within your micro frontend
- Register SVG icons that can be referenced by NeonIcon and other Neon components
- Support Right-to-Left (RTL) language displays with custom icons
- Display SVG icons with complex paths or specific styling requirements
- Create namespaced icons to prevent collisions between different micro frontends
NeonIconCustom is a container component that registers SVG content with the Neon icon system. Once registered, these icons can be used by NeonIcon and other components by referencing them with the "|custom" suffix.

- Provide visual categorization through color-coded icon backgrounds
- Draw attention to specific icon elements

- Add a decorative element to simple iconography
NeonIconStack combines a background shape with a foreground icon to create a layered effect. It's useful for creating visual interest and drawing attention to specific functionality in your interface.

### NeonModalDialog

dialog component that presents content in a layer that appears above the application, requiring user interaction before returning to the main interface.

- Present a self-contained workflow that must be completed or dismissed
- Create a temporary overlay that blocks interaction with the underlying page
- Request user confirmation or decision while maintaining context of the current page
NeonModalDialog is ideal for important interactions that require full user attention and should interrupt the normal workflow. For less disruptive interactions or side panels, consider using NeonModalDrawer instead. For simple notifications that don't require user action, NeonToast would be more appropriate.

- Allow users to perform secondary tasks while maintaining their current context
- Implement progressive disclosure of complex interfaces
NeonModalDrawer is designed for displaying content that complements the main page. For modals that should appear centered on the screen, consider using NeonModalDialog instead.

- Implement email address inputs with built-in validation
- Create fields with character limits and constraints
- Add icon indicators to text inputs for better context
NeonTextField is the fundamental text input component for forms and should be your default choice for collecting short textual data from users. For multi-line text input, consider using NeonTextareaField instead.


### NeonTextareaField

flexible textarea component for capturing multi-line text input with built-in validation and formatting options.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonTextareaField component when you need to:
- Collect longer text responses from users that might span multiple lines
- Allow users to enter descriptions, comments, feedback, or other free-form text
- Create form fields where users need more space than a standard text field provides
- Implement text areas with character counts, validation rules, or formatting requirements
- Display multi-line text input with consistent styling and behavior across your application
- Capture text input that requires validation (minimum/maximum length, regex patterns)
- Provide users with a resizable text area for variable-length content
NeonTextareaField is the primary multi-line text input component in the Neon Design System. It extends the functionality of standard text inputs with additional features like character counting, validation, and integration with the form system.


### NeonTimeField

form input component that allows users to select or enter time values in a standardized format.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonTimeField component when you need to:
- Collect time input from users in a consistent format
- Allow users to select a time value from a dropdown picker
- Capture appointment times, meeting times, or schedule information
- Enforce time format validation automatically
- Set minimum or maximum time constraints for inputs
- Implement accessible time selection in forms
- Create time-based filtering or search inputs
NeonTimeField is designed to handle time data specifically, ensuring proper formatting and validation while providing an intuitive user experience. It integrates with the Time type from the MFE utils library to handle time values consistently.


### NeonTimePicker

component that allows users to select a time using an interactive time picker interface.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonTimePicker component when you need to:
- Allow users to select a specific time
- Provide an intuitive interface for time selection
- Standardize time input across your application
- Include time selection in forms or data entry interfaces
- Ensure consistent time format handling
- Enable precise time selection with hours and minutes
- Create accessible time selection interfaces
NeonTimePicker is the standard time selection component in the Neon Design System. For simpler time input needs or when you need a form field with a label, consider using NeonTimeField which incorporates this time picker with additional field capabilities.


### NeonToast

toast notification component for displaying brief, non-disruptive messages to users with optional actions and automatic dismissal.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonToast component when you need to:
- Provide brief, non-blocking feedback to users about an action or state change
- Display notifications that don't require immediate user attention
- Show success, warning, error, or informational messages
- Present timely information that can be auto-dismissed after a period of time
- Provide quick actions related to the notification content
- Communicate status updates without disrupting the user's workflow
- Display transient messages that should appear temporarily and then disappear
- Show notifications with consistent styling across your application
NeonToast is designed for lightweight, temporary messaging that doesn't interrupt the user's current task. For more critical messages that require immediate attention, consider using NeonSystemMessage instead.


### NeonTooltip

lightweight tooltip component that displays helpful text or content when users hover over or focus on an element.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonTooltip component when you need to:
- Provide additional context or explanation for UI elements without cluttering the interface
- Explain the function of icons, buttons, or other interactive elements
- Display supplementary information that doesn't require constant visibility
- Enhance accessibility by providing text descriptions for visual elements
- Show keyboard shortcuts or hints for power users
- Provide definitions or clarifications for abbreviated terms or technical concepts
- Display warnings or important notes about specific functionality
- Label elements that don't have visible text labels to improve usability
NeonTooltip is designed for brief, contextual information. For more complex interactions or content that users need to interact with, consider using NeonPopover or NeonModalDialog components instead.


### NeonTree

hierarchical tree component for displaying structured data with support for navigation, selection, and expandable/collapsible nodes.

**When To Use:**

Use the NeonTree component when you need to:
- Display hierarchical data with parent-child relationships
- Create a file/folder structure interface with expandable folders
- Implement a navigational tree menu with clickable links
- Create a multi-level selection interface with checkboxes
- Show organization charts or other nested data structures
- Present categories and subcategories in a collapsible format
- Create an expandable table of contents
- Implement a site navigation with expandable sections
- Visualize nested data structures like file systems, taxonomies, or organization charts
- Support lazy loading of large hierarchical datasets
NeonTree is versatile and can be configured in three primary modes: basic (for display only), navigation (for clickable links), and selectable (for checkbox selection).




## Component Details

# NeonAccordion

A collapsible content container that allows users to show and hide sections of related content.

## When To Use

Use the NeonAccordion component when you need to:

- Display content that can be collapsed and expanded to save space
- Organize related information into sections that can be viewed independently
- Create FAQ sections with questions that expand to show answers
- Implement progressive disclosure of complex information
- Reduce visual complexity by hiding secondary content until requested
- Group form sections that aren't all required at once
- Create expandable/collapsible sections within a drawer or modal
- Present a list of independently accessible content sections in a compact format

NeonAccordion is ideal for presenting multiple sections of content in a limited space, allowing users to focus on specific sections as needed. For navigation between completely separate views of content, consider NeonTabs instead. For very simple toggle visibility, a basic show/hide button might be more appropriate.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the component |
| dataHeading | string | Yes | - | The heading for the accordion |
| dataSubheading | string | No | - | The subheading for the accordion |
| dataSize | string | Yes | - | The size of the accordion. Options: 'small', 'large' |
| dataIcon | string | No | - | The name of the icon that shows up next to the header |
| dataBorderType | string | No | 'none' | The border type for the accordion. Options: 'none', 'bottom', 'full' |
| dataExpanded | boolean | No | false | When true, the accordion will be expanded |
| dataInjectionSpacing | boolean | No | true | When false, removes the spacing class around the injected content |
| dataContentPreview | boolean | No | false | When true, shows the first two lines of content when collapsed |
| dataAvatarFirstName | string | No | - | First name for avatar in header |
| dataAvatarLastName | string | No | - | Last name for avatar in header |
| dataAvatarProfilePictureSrc | string | No | - | Image source for avatar |
| dataAvatarBackgroundOption | string | No | 'default' | Background style for avatar. Options: 'default', '0', '1', '2', '3', '4', 'high-contrast', 'theme' |
| dataAvatarSize | string | No | 'medium' | Size of the avatar. Options: 'extra-small', 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'extra-large' |
| dataIconStackIcon | string | No | - | The icon name for Icon Stack |
| dataIconStackColor | string | No | 'gray' | The color for Icon Stack. Options: 'magenta', 'red', 'orange', 'yellow', 'green', 'teal', 'cyan', 'purple', 'gray' |
| dataIconStackShape | string | No | 'circle' | The shape for Icon Stack. Options: 'circle', 'square', 'hexagon', 'diamond' |
| dataIconStackSize | string | No | 'large' | The size for Icon Stack. Options: 'x-small', 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'x-large', 'xx-large', 'xxx-large' |
| neonAccordionExpandedStateChange | function | No | - | Event handler called when accordion is toggled: (isExpanded: boolean) => void |
| children | ReactNode | No | - | Content to display when the accordion is expanded |

## Examples

Basic accordion with conditional content loading:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonAccordion } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AccordionConditionalExample() {
  const [showContent, setShowContent] = useState([]);

  const accordionContent = [
    {
      id: 'item-1',
      heading: 'heading 1',
      subheading: 'subheading 1',
      getContent: () => {
        return <p className="__neon__text">This is the section 1 content.</p>;
      }
    }, {
      id: 'item-2',
      heading: 'heading 2',
      subheading: 'subheading 2',
      getContent: () => {
        return <p className="__neon__text">This is the section 2 content.</p>;
      }
    }, {
      id: 'item-3',
      heading: 'heading 3',
      subheading: 'subheading 3',
      getContent: () => {
        return <p className="__neon__text">This is the section 3 content.</p>;
      }
    }
  ];

  return (
    <div>
      {
        accordionContent.map((obj, idx) => {
          return (
            <NeonAccordion
              key={obj.id}
              id={obj.id}
              dataHeading={obj.heading}
              dataSubheading={obj.subheading}
              dataBorderType="full"
              dataSize="large"
              neonAccordionExpandedStateChange={(isExpanded) => {
                const clone = [...showContent];
                clone[idx] = isExpanded;
                setShowContent(clone);
              }}
            >
              <div>
                {showContent[idx] && obj.getContent()}
              </div>
            </NeonAccordion>
          );
        })
      }
    </div>
  );
}
```

Accordion with full width content and custom spacing:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonAccordion } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AccordionFullWidthExample() {
  const [showContent, setShowContent] = useState([]);

  const accordionContent = [
    {
      id: 'item-1',
      heading: 'heading 1',
      subheading: 'subheading 1',
      getContent: () => {
        return <p className="__neon__text">This is the section 1 content.</p>;
      }
    }, {
      id: 'item-2',
      heading: 'heading 2',
      subheading: 'subheading 2',
      getContent: () => {
        return <p className="__neon__text">This is the section 2 content.</p>;
      }
    }, {
      id: 'item-3',
      heading: 'heading 3',
      subheading: 'subheading 3',
      getContent: () => {
        return <p className="__neon__text">This is the section 3 content.</p>;
      }
    }
  ];

  return (
    <div>
      {
        accordionContent.map((obj, idx) => {
          return (
            <NeonAccordion
              key={obj.id}
              id={obj.id}
              dataInjectionSpacing="false"
              dataHeading={obj.heading}
              dataSubheading={obj.subheading}
              dataSize="large"
              neonAccordionExpandedStateChange={(isExpanded) => {
                const clone = [...showContent];
                clone[idx] = isExpanded;
                setShowContent(clone);
              }}
            >
              {/* 
                Adding the class __neon__accordion-content gives you the same spacing you get but now you can change things with the flush classes.
                Add the classes __neon__flush-left __neon__flush-right __neon__flush-bottom to zero out spacing where you don't want it.
              */}
              <div className="__neon__accordion-content __neon__flush-left __neon__flush-right __neon__flush-bottom">
                {showContent[idx] && obj.getContent()}
              </div>
            </NeonAccordion>
          );
        })
      }
    </div>
  );
}
```

# NeonAiChatLauncher

A component that provides a user-friendly interface for interacting with AI assistants, featuring speech-to-text capabilities and customizable visual styles.

## When To Use

Use the NeonAiChatLauncher component when you need to:

- Create an entry point for AI chat functionality within your application
- Provide users with a simple way to ask questions or request assistance
- Implement a modern, accessible interface for AI interactions
- Collect user input before launching a more comprehensive AI experience
- Add speech-to-text capability for hands-free interactions
- Create a branded AI launcher that matches your application's theme
- Provide suggestions based on user input to guide interactions
- Handle error states and loading indicators for AI functionality
- Integrate AI capabilities in a user-friendly, unobtrusive way
- Create consistent AI interaction points across your application

NeonAiChatLauncher is designed to serve as the primary entry point for AI interaction within your application. Its clean, focused interface is optimized for capturing user input and integrating with AI processing systems.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the component |
| dataPlaceholder | string | No | - | The placeholder text for the input field |
| dataMaxLength | number | No | 10000 | The maximum number of characters allowed in the input field |
| dataDisableSpeechToText | boolean | No | - | If true, the speech to text functionality will be disabled |
| dataDisplaySpeechToText | boolean | No | true | If false, the speech to text button will not be displayed |
| dataIsLoading | boolean | No | - | If true, the component will be in a loading state |
| dataIsLoadingText | string | No | 'Loading' | The text to display when the component is in a loading state |
| dataErrorText | string | No | - | The error text to display if the component is in an error state |
| dataAriaLabel | string | No | 'PowerBuddy prompt launcher' | The aria label for the component |
| dataInputAriaLabel | string | No | 'Ask PowerBuddy' | The aria label for the input field |
| dataMicAriaLabel | string | No | 'Activate microphone' | The aria label for the microphone button |
| dataSubmitAriaLabel | string | No | 'Submit question' | The aria label for the submit button |
| dataType | string | No | 'ai' | Visual style type. Options: 'white', 'ai' |
| neonValueChange | function | No | - | Callback fired when the user submits a message |
| onInput | function | No | - | Callback fired when the user types in the input field |
| children | React.ReactNode | No | - | Content to use in the component slots |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| ai-chat-launcher-error | No | For buttons or other elements to display when the component is in an error state |
| ai-chat-launcher-suggestion | No | For buttons or other elements to display based on the value submitted |

## Examples

Simple AI Chat Launcher:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonAiChatLauncher } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AiChatLauncherExampleSimple() {
  const [value, setValue] = React.useState(undefined);

  return (
    <NeonAiChatLauncher
      id="ai-chat-launcher-simple"
      neonValueChange={(value) => {
        setValue(value);
        console.log('value', value);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

AI Chat Launcher with suggestions:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonAiChatLauncher, NeonButton } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AiChatLauncherExampleWithSuggestions() {
  const [value, setValue] = React.useState(undefined);

  return (
    <NeonAiChatLauncher
      id="ai-chat-launcher-suggestions"
      neonValueChange={(value) => {
        setValue(value);
      }}>
      <div data-slot="ai-chat-launcher-suggestions">
        {value?.split(' ').slice(0, 4).map((word) => {
          return <NeonButton
            key={word}
            id={'suggestion-' + word}
            dataText={word} />;
        })}
      </div>
    </NeonAiChatLauncher>
  );
}
```

AI Chat Launcher in error state:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonAiChatLauncher, NeonButton } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AiChatLauncherExampleError() {
  return (
    <NeonAiChatLauncher
      id="ai-chat-launcher-error"
      dataErrorText="PowerBuddy could not be accessed at this time. Try refreshing the launcher.">
      <div data-slot="ai-chat-launcher-error">
        <NeonButton
          id="refresh-button"
          dataText="Refresh"
          dataIcon="refresh"
          dataType="primary"
          onClick={() => {
            console.log('Refresh clicked');
          }}
        />
      </div>
    </NeonAiChatLauncher>
  );
}
```

AI Chat Launcher in loading state:
```jsx

  return (
    <NeonAiChatLauncher
      id="ai-chat-launcher-loading"
      dataIsLoading={true}
      dataIsLoadingText="Processing your request..."
    />
  );
}
```

AI Chat Launcher with white theme:
```jsx

  return (
    <NeonAiChatLauncher

    />
  );
```

# NeonAppHeader

A top-level navigation component that provides consistent header styling and functionality across an application.

## When To Use

Use the NeonAppHeader component when you need to:

- Create a consistent application header with branding elements
- Provide primary navigation at the top of your application
- Display a header with a logo and application title
- Add utility elements like search, notification icons, or avatar menus in the header
- Implement a header with customizable center and right sections
- Create a header with optional subheading text
- Provide a clickable home link functionality
- Establish a professional and unified application branding

NeonAppHeader is the primary header component in the Neon Design System. It provides a consistent and accessible way to implement application headers with branding and navigation elements.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | No | - | Unique identifier for the header |
| dataHeading | string | Yes | - | The heading text to display in the header |
| dataSubheading | string | No | - | Optional subheading text to display below the heading |
| dataHomeLinkUrl | string | No | '/' | The URL to navigate to when the header logo/title is clicked |
| neonAppHeaderHomeLinkClick | function | No | - | Event handler for customizing home link click behavior |
| children | ReactNode | No | - | Child elements to render in the header slots |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| app-header-center | No | Content to display in the center section of the header |
| app-header-right | No | Content to display in the right section of the header |

## Examples

Basic header with heading:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonAppHeader } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AppHeaderBasicExample() {
  return (
    <NeonAppHeader dataHeading="My Application">
      <div data-slot="app-header-right">
        <p>Right side content</p>
      </div>
    </NeonAppHeader>
  );
}
```

Header with avatar button:
```jsx

          <NeonAvatar
            dataSlot="avatar"
            dataFirstName="First"
            dataLastName="Last"
            dataAvatarSize="small"
            dataBackgroundOption="high-contrast"
          />
        </NeonAvatarButton>
```
```jsx
      </div>
    </NeonAppHeader>
  );
}
```

Header with custom home link click handler:

```jsx
export function AppHeaderHomeLinkExample() {
  function customRouteFunction() {
    console.log('Using alternative routing');
  }

  return (
    <NeonAppHeader
      dataHeading="Click Me"
      neonAppHeaderHomeLinkClick={(event) => {
        event.preventDefault();
        customRouteFunction();

      <div data-slot="app-header-center">
        <p>Center content</p>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="app-header-right">
        <p>Right content</p>
      </div>

  );
}
```

```jsx
              dataSlot="avatar"

              dataLastName="Last"
              dataAvatarSize="small"
```

# NeonAppNavIcon

A specialized icon component designed specifically for application navigation with pre-defined navigation icons.

## When To Use

Use the NeonAppNavIcon component when you need to:

- Display navigation icons specifically designed for application menus
- Create consistent navigation icons throughout your application
- Use specialized icons for common application sections like overview, calendar, gradebook, etc.
- Implement navigation icons that are part of the Neon Design System's app navigation
- Maintain visual consistency in application navigation elements
- Use application-specific icons that are optimized for navigation contexts

NeonAppNavIcon is designed specifically for application navigation contexts and provides specialized icons for common application sections. For general icon usage, consider using the standard NeonIcon component instead.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the icon component |
| dataIcon | string | Yes | - | The icon to display. Valid values include: 'app-nav-forms', 'app-nav-gradebook', 'app-nav-overview', 'app-nav-assignments', 'app-nav-calendar', 'app-nav-trophy', 'app-nav-payments', 'app-nav-grad-cap', 'app-nav-attendance', 'app-nav-users', 'app-nav-newsfeed', 'app-nav-megaphone', or any standard icon name |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles for the component |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |

## Examples

Simple app navigation icon:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonAppNavIcon } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AppNavIconExampleSimple() {
  return (
    <NeonAppNavIcon id="simple-app-nav-icon" dataIcon="app-nav-overview" />
  );
}
```

Using app navigation icons in a list:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonAppNavIcon } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AppNavIconExampleList() {
  const navIcons = [
    'app-nav-overview',
    'app-nav-calendar',
    'app-nav-assignments',
    'app-nav-gradebook',
    'app-nav-forms'
  ];

  return (
    <div className="app-nav-icon-list">
      {navIcons.map((icon, index) => (
        <div key={index} className="app-nav-icon-item">
          <NeonAppNavIcon id={`app-nav-icon-${index}`} dataIcon={icon} />
          <span>{icon.replace('app-nav-', '')}</span>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

Using a standard icon as fallback:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonAppNavIcon } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AppNavIconExampleFallback() {
  return (
    <div className="app-nav-icon-examples">
      <div className="app-nav-icon-example">
        <NeonAppNavIcon id="app-icon-1" dataIcon="app-nav-overview" />
        <span>App Navigation Icon</span>
      </div>
      <div className="app-nav-icon-example">
        <NeonAppNavIcon id="standard-icon-1" dataIcon="settings" />
        <span>Standard Icon Fallback</span>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Styled app navigation icon with additional styling:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonAppNavIcon } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AppNavIconExampleStyled() {
  const iconStyle = {
    transform: 'scale(1.5)',
    margin: '16px',
    display: 'flex',
    alignItems: 'center',
    justifyContent: 'center'
  };

  return (
    <NeonAppNavIcon
      id="styled-app-nav-icon"
      dataIcon="app-nav-gradebook"
      style={iconStyle}
      className="custom-app-nav-icon"
    />
  );
}
```


# NeonAppNavSwitcher

A dropdown component for switching between entities such as users, schools, or classes within an application navigation system.

## When To Use

Use the NeonAppNavSwitcher component when you need to:

- Allow users to switch between different entities or profiles in an application
- Provide a consistent entity selection interface across various applications
- Display user profiles with names, avatars, and metadata
- Group related entities like schools, classrooms, or users in a selectable dropdown
- Integrate with NeonAppNav for a complete application navigation experience
- Present entity information with optional images, avatars, and metadata
- Support multiple entity types with consistent visual presentation
- Enable quick switching between different contexts within the same application
- Display entity lists with pagination for larger collections

NeonAppNavSwitcher is designed to work with the NeonAppNav component to provide a complete navigation experience. It's particularly useful for applications that require users to switch between different contexts like schools, classrooms, or user profiles.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the component |
| switcherOptions | Array<AppNavSwitcherItem &#124; "DIVIDER"> | Yes | - | An array of entities to select from |
| currentSwitcherOption | AppNavSwitcherItem | No | - | The currently selected entity |
| dataAppNavCollapsed | boolean | No | false | Flag indicating if the app nav is collapsed |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |

## AppNavSwitcherItem Interface

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the item |
| heading | string | Yes | - | Main title text for the item |
| subheading | string | No | - | Secondary text displayed below heading |
| menuSubheading | string | No | - | Subheading that appears in select menu (falls back to subheading if not provided) |
| imgSrc | string | No | - | URL for the top image |
| placeholderImage | 'classroom' &#124; 'school' &#124; 'district' | No | - | Predefined placeholder image type |
| firstName | string | No | - | First name for avatar or initials generation |
| lastName | string | No | - | Last name for avatar or initials generation |
| profilePictureSrc | string | No | - | URL for avatar profile picture |
| metadata | Array<{ key: string, value: string }> | No | - | Key-value pairs displayed with the entity |
| initials | string | No | - | Custom initials override (defaults to first letters of firstName and lastName) |

## Examples

Basic usage with user profiles:

```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonAppNavSwitcher } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { type AppNavSwitcherItem } from '@neon/interfaces';

export function AppNavSwitcherExampleSimple() {
  const switcherOptions: Array<AppNavSwitcherItem> = [{
    heading: 'Mason Parker',
    id: 'user-mason-parker',
    firstName: 'Mason',
    lastName: 'Parker',
    profilePictureSrc: 'example-files/avatars/Mason Parker.jpg'
  }, {
    heading: 'Noah Smith',
    subheading: 'PowerSchool Middle School',
    id: 'user-noah-smith-middle-school',
    firstName: 'Noah',
    lastName: 'Smith',
    profilePictureSrc: 'example-files/avatars/Noah Smith.jpg'
  }];

  const currentSwitcherItem: AppNavSwitcherItem = switcherOptions[0];

  return (
    <NeonAppNavSwitcher
      id="app-nav-switcher"
      currentSwitcherOption={currentSwitcherItem}
      switcherOptions={switcherOptions} />
  );
}
```

With placeholder images:
