# NeonAppNav

A navigation component that provides a hierarchical, collapsible navigation structure for applications, including support for multi-level navigation items, user information, and app switching functionality.

## When To Use

Use the NeonAppNav component when you need to:

- Create a consistent, accessible application navigation structure
- Display a hierarchical navigation system with support for multiple levels
- Provide user information and user-specific menu options
- Allow users to switch between different applications or contexts
- Implement a standard navigation pattern across your application
- Support both desktop and mobile navigation experiences
- Create a navigation system with icons, text, and optional visual indicators
- Enable users to navigate between different sections of your application

NeonAppNav is the primary navigation component in the Neon Design System, designed to provide a consistent navigation experience across applications with support for multiple navigation patterns and responsive behaviors.

## Props

NeonAppNav doesn't accept direct props in the conventional sense. Instead, it relies on a service-based approach where navigation data is set through the AppNav service.

## Service Methods

The NeonAppNav component is controlled through the AppNav service, which you can access using the `getAppNav()` function:

| Method | Parameters | Description |
|--------|------------|-------------|
| setNavItems | Array\<NavItem\> | Sets the main navigation items to display |
| setUser | NavUser | Sets the user information displayed in the navigation |
| setSwitcherOptions | Array\<AppNavSwitcherItem \| "DIVIDER"\> | Sets the options for the app switcher dropdown |
| setCurrentSwitcherOption | AppNavSwitcherItem | Sets the currently selected app switcher option |

## Key Interfaces

### NavItem

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
|----------|------|----------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | Unique identifier for the navigation item |
| name | string | Yes | Display name for the navigation item |
| description | string | No | Optional description that appears beneath the name |
| iconName | string | No | Name of the icon to display (for primary links or categories) |
| iconColor | IconColor | No | Color to apply to the icon |
| iconColorWeight | NeonColorWeight | No | Color weight to apply to the icon |
| imagePath | string | No | Path to an image associated with the link (ignored for primary items or items with children) |
| children | Array\<NavItem\> | No | Child navigation items, when defined makes this item a category |
| isDisabled | boolean | No | When true, disables the navigation item |
| disabledTooltipText | string | No | Text to display in tooltip when item is disabled |
| url | string | No | URL to navigate to when item is clicked (required for navigation items) |
| isNewTab | boolean | No | When true, opens URL in a new tab |
| isLeavesApp | boolean | No | Controls whether to display the "leaving site" icon |
| avatar | AvatarUser | No | User avatar information associated with this item |
| onUserClick | (navItem: NavItem, event: Event) => void | No | Custom click handler for the item |
| isCurrentRoute | (navItem: NavItem) => boolean | No | Function that determines if this is the active route |
| isActiveOverride | (navItem: NavItem) => boolean | No | Function to highlight additional nav items beyond the current route |

### NavUser

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
|----------|------|----------|-------------|
| firstName | string | Yes | User's first name |
| lastName | string | Yes | User's last name |
| profilePicture | { src: string, alt?: string } | No | User's profile picture information |
| userMenuOptions | Array\<NavItem\> | Yes | Menu options for the user dropdown |

### AppNavSwitcherItem

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
|----------|------|----------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | Unique identifier for the switcher item |
| heading | string | Yes | Main text displayed for the item |
| subheading | string | No | Secondary text displayed beneath the heading |
| menuSubheading | string | No | Subheading that appears in select menu (falls back to subheading if not specified) |
| imgSrc | string | No | URL for the top image |
| placeholderImage | 'classroom' \| 'school' \| 'district' | No | Predefined placeholder image to use |
| firstName | string | No | First name used to generate initials when collapsed |
| lastName | string | No | Last name used to generate initials when collapsed |
| profilePictureSrc | string | No | URL for avatar profile picture |
| metadata | Array<{ key: string, value: string }> | No | Key-value pairs displayed in the switcher |
| initials | string | No | Custom initials to display (overrides default first/last initial) |

## Examples

Basic navigation setup:

```jsx
import React, { useEffect } from 'react';
import { NavItem } from '@neon/interfaces';
import { NeonAppNav, getAppNav } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function BasicAppNavExample() {
  useEffect(() => {
    // Define navigation items
    const navItems: Array<NavItem> = [
      {
        id: 'dashboard',
        name: 'Dashboard',
        iconName: 'dashboard',
        url: '/dashboard'
      },
      {
        id: 'courses',
        name: 'Courses',
        iconName: 'school',
        children: [
          {
            id: 'course-math',
            name: 'Mathematics',
            url: '/courses/mathematics'
          },
          {
            id: 'course-science',
            name: 'Science',
            url: '/courses/science'
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        id: 'settings',
        name: 'Settings',
        iconName: 'settings',
        url: '/settings'
      }
    ];

    // Set up navigation when component mounts
    getAppNav().then((appNav) => {
      appNav.setNavItems(navItems);
    });
  }, []);

  return <NeonAppNav />;
}
```

App navigation with user information:

```jsx
import React, { useEffect } from 'react';
import { NavItem, NavUser } from '@neon/interfaces';
import { NeonAppNav, getAppNav } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AppNavWithUserExample() {
  useEffect(() => {
    // Define navigation items
    const navItems: Array<NavItem> = [
      // ... navigation items
    ];

    // Define user information
    const user: NavUser = {
      firstName: 'Jane',
      lastName: 'Doe',
      profilePicture: {
        src: '/path/to/profile-image.jpg',
        alt: 'Jane Doe'
      },
      userMenuOptions: [
        {
          id: 'profile',
          name: 'My Profile',
          iconName: 'person',
          url: '/profile'
        },
        {
          id: 'logout',
          name: 'Sign Out',
          iconName: 'logout',
          url: '/logout'
        }
      ]
    };

    // Set up navigation and user info when component mounts
    getAppNav().then((appNav) => {
      appNav.setNavItems(navItems);
      appNav.setUser(user);
    });
  }, []);

  return <NeonAppNav />;
}
```

App navigation with switcher options:

```jsx
import React, { useEffect } from 'react';
import { AppNavSwitcherItem } from '@neon/interfaces';
import { NeonAppNav, getAppNav } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AppNavWithSwitcherExample() {
  useEffect(() => {
    // Define switcher options
    const switcherOptions: Array<AppNavSwitcherItem | 'DIVIDER'> = [
      {
        id: 'school-1',
        heading: 'Central High School',
        subheading: 'School Admin',
        firstName: 'Central',
        lastName: 'High',
        profilePictureSrc: '/path/to/school-logo.png',
        metadata: [
          { key: 'District', value: 'Springfield USD' },
          { key: 'Type', value: 'High School' }
        ]
      },
      'DIVIDER',
      {
        id: 'school-2',
        heading: 'Lincoln Elementary',
        subheading: 'School Admin',
        firstName: 'Lincoln',
        lastName: 'Elementary'
      }
    ];

    // Set up switcher options when component mounts
    getAppNav().then((appNav) => {
      appNav.setSwitcherOptions(switcherOptions);
      appNav.setCurrentSwitcherOption(switcherOptions[0] as AppNavSwitcherItem);
    });
  }, []);

  return <NeonAppNav />;
}
```

Complete app navigation setup with router integration:

```jsx
import React, { useEffect } from 'react';
import { NavItem, NavUser, AppNavSwitcherItem } from '@neon/interfaces';
import { NeonAppNav, getAppNav } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { useNavigate } from 'react-router-dom';

export function CompleteAppNavExample() {
  const navigate = useNavigate();

  useEffect(() => {
    // Helper function to connect navigation items to the router
    const connectRouterToNavItems = (items: Array<NavItem>): Array<NavItem> => {
      return items.map(item => {
        if (item.children) {
          // Process children recursively
          return {
            ...item,
            children: connectRouterToNavItems(item.children)
          };
        } else if (item.url && !item.isNewTab) {
          // Add click handler for router navigation
          return {
            ...item,
            onUserClick: (navItem: NavItem, event: Event) => {
              event.preventDefault();
              navigate(item.url);
            },
            isCurrentRoute: (navItem: NavItem) => {
              return window.location.pathname === navItem.url;
            }
          };
        }
        return item;
      });
    };

    // Define and process navigation items
    const navItems = connectRouterToNavItems([
      {
        id: 'dashboard',
        name: 'Dashboard',
        iconName: 'dashboard',
        url: '/dashboard'
      },
      {
        id: 'students',
        name: 'Students',
        iconName: 'people',
        children: [
          {
            id: 'student-roster',
            name: 'Student Roster',
            url: '/students/roster'
          },
          {
            id: 'student-reports',
            name: 'Student Reports',
            url: '/students/reports'
          }
        ]
      }
    ]);

    // Define user information
    const user: NavUser = {
      firstName: 'Jane',
      lastName: 'Doe',
      profilePicture: {
        src: '/path/to/profile-image.jpg'
      },
      userMenuOptions: [
        {
          id: 'profile',
          name: 'My Profile',
          iconName: 'person',
          url: '/profile'
        },
        {
          id: 'logout',
          name: 'Sign Out',
          iconName: 'logout',
          url: '/logout'
        }
      ]
    };

    // Define switcher options
    const switcherOptions: Array<AppNavSwitcherItem> = [
      {
        id: 'school-1',
        heading: 'Central High School',
        subheading: 'School Admin',
        profilePictureSrc: '/path/to/school-logo.png'
      },
      {
        id: 'school-2',
        heading: 'Lincoln Elementary',
        subheading: 'School Admin'
      }
    ];

    // Set up all navigation components
    getAppNav().then((appNav) => {
      appNav.setNavItems(navItems);
      appNav.setUser(user);
      appNav.setSwitcherOptions(switcherOptions);
      appNav.setCurrentSwitcherOption(switcherOptions[0]);
    });
  }, [navigate]);

  return <NeonAppNav />;
}
```


# NeonAvatarButton

A button component designed to display user avatars and initials, providing a clickable interface for profile menus and user actions.

## When To Use

Use the NeonAvatarButton component when you need to:

- Create a profile or user menu trigger in your application
- Display a user's avatar as a clickable button element
- Implement user account navigation in headers or navigation bars
- Provide an accessible, clickable avatar for user profile actions
- Create a visual representation of the current user with interactivity
- Implement dropdown menus attached to an avatar
- Add user-related actions to navigation areas with limited space
- Create a compact user interface element that represents the logged-in user

NeonAvatarButton is often used in application headers, navigation bars, and settings panels to provide quick access to user-related actions. It's commonly paired with NeonMenu to create dropdown menus containing options like account settings or logout functionality.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the avatar button |
| dataAriaLabel | string | Yes | - | Accessible label for the avatar button |
| children | React.ReactNode | Yes | - | Avatar component to display (must include a NeonAvatar with dataSlot="avatar") |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles |
| onClick | function | No | - | Function to call when the avatar button is clicked |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| avatar | Yes | Place for a NeonAvatar component |

## Examples

Basic avatar button:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonAvatarButton, NeonAvatar } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AvatarButtonExample() {
  return (
    <NeonAvatarButton id="user-profile-button" dataAriaLabel="User Profile">
      <NeonAvatar
        dataSlot="avatar"
        dataFirstName="John"
        dataLastName="Doe"
        dataAvatarSize="medium"
      />
    </NeonAvatarButton>
  );
}
```

Avatar button with profile picture:
```jsx

      <NeonAvatar
        dataSlot="avatar"
        dataFirstName="Jane"
        dataLastName="Smith"
        dataAvatarSize="medium"
        dataProfilePictureSrc="path/to/profile-image.jpg"
      />
    </NeonAvatarButton>
  );
}
```

Avatar button with menu:
```jsx

      text: 'Account Settings',
      iconName: 'settings'

      id: 'logout',

            dataSlot="avatar"
            dataFirstName="Alex"
            dataLastName="Johnson"
            dataAvatarSize="medium"
            dataProfilePictureSrc="path/to/profile-image.jpg"
          />
        </NeonAvatarButton>
      </div>

  );
}
```

# NeonAvatarStack

A component that displays a collection of avatars in a visually compact grouping with automatic handling of overflow.

## When To Use

Use the NeonAvatarStack component when you need to:

- Display a group of users or participants in a visual format
- Show multiple user avatars in a compact, space-efficient way
- Represent team members, collaborators, or participants in a project
- Display a list of users where seeing their profile pictures is helpful for recognition
- Create a visually appealing representation of group membership
- Show user involvement in discussions, tasks, or shared content
- Save horizontal space when displaying multiple user avatars
- Automatically handle the display of many users with an overflow mechanism

NeonAvatarStack is ideal for situations where you need to visually represent multiple users in a space-efficient way. The component automatically handles overflow when there are more users than can be displayed, providing a count and optional menu to see additional users.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the avatar stack |
| users | Array<AvatarUser> | Yes | - | An array of AvatarUser objects to be displayed in the stack |
| avatarSize | string | No | 'medium' | Size of the avatars within the stack. Options: 'extra-small', 'small', 'medium', 'large' |
| showOverflowMenu | boolean | No | true | Set to false if using with neonAvatarStackOverflowButtonClick event to not render the menu |
| neonAvatarStackOverflowButtonClick | function | No | - | Callback function triggered when the overflow button is clicked |

## AvatarUser Interface

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| firstName | string | No | - | First name of the user |
| lastName | string | No | - | Last name of the user |
| profilePicture | object | No | - | Object containing the source URL for the profile picture |
| profilePicture.src | string | Yes (if profilePicture is provided) | - | URL to the profile picture image |
| initialsBackgroundOption | string | No | - | Background style for avatar when displaying initials |
| tooltipText | string | No | - | Text to display in tooltip when hovering over the avatar |
| tooltipPlacement | PopperPlacement | No | - | Placement of the tooltip |
| id | string | No | - | Unique identifier (required when using tooltipText) |

## Examples

Basic avatar stack with many users:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonAvatarStack } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AvatarStackExample() {
  return <NeonAvatarStack
    id="avatar-stack-example"
    users={[...Array(30)].map(() => {
      return {
        firstName: 'Cory',
        lastName: 'Matthews',
        profilePicture: {
          src: 'example-files/cory-matthews.jpg',
        }
      };
    })}
  ></NeonAvatarStack>;
}
```

Avatar stack with tooltips:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonAvatarStack } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AvatarStackTooltipExample() {
  return <NeonAvatarStack
    id="avatar-stack-tooltip"
    users={[...Array(30)].map((value, index) => {
      return {
        id: 'avatar-' + index,
        firstName: 'Cory',
        lastName: 'Matthews',
        tooltipText: 'Cory Matthews',
        profilePicture: {
          src: 'example-files/cory-matthews.jpg',
        }
      };
    })}
  ></NeonAvatarStack>;
}
```

Avatar stack with custom overflow button click handler:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonAvatarStack } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AvatarStackButtonEventExample() {
  return <NeonAvatarStack
    id="avatar-stack-button-event"
    users={[...Array(30)].map(() => {
      return {
        firstName: 'Cory',
        lastName: 'Matthews',
        profilePicture: {
          src: 'example-files/cory-matthews.jpg',
        }
      };
    })}
    showOverflowMenu="false"
    neonAvatarStackOverflowButtonClick={(): void => { alert('Now thats a lot of Cory Matthews\'s!'); }}
  ></NeonAvatarStack>;
}
```

Avatar stack with different size:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonAvatarStack } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AvatarStackSizeExample() {
  return <NeonAvatarStack
    id="avatar-stack-size-example"
    avatarSize="large"
    users={[...Array(10)].map(() => {
      return {
        firstName: 'Cory',
        lastName: 'Matthews',
        profilePicture: {
          src: 'example-files/cory-matthews.jpg',
        }
      };
    })}
  ></NeonAvatarStack>;
}
```




# NeonAvatar

A versatile avatar component that displays user representation through initials or profile pictures with various styling options.

## When To Use

Use the NeonAvatar component when you need to:

- Display a visual representation of a user or entity within an application
- Show user profile pictures or generate visual representations using initials
- Create consistent user identification across the user interface
- Provide visual cues for user-related content or actions
- Represent users in comment sections, user lists, or messaging interfaces
- Add user identification to headers, profiles, or navigation components
- Display user presence in collaborative applications
- Create visual hierarchies of users with different sizes of avatars
- Implement user-focused UI elements with consistent styling and behavior

NeonAvatar is a foundational component for representing users throughout the Neon Design System. It supports displaying either profile pictures or automatically generating visual representations using user initials. For situations requiring user interaction with avatars, consider using NeonAvatarButton or NeonAvatarStack for displaying groups of users.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | No | - | Unique identifier for the avatar (required when using tooltip) |
| dataFirstName | string | No | - | The first name of the user |
| dataLastName | string | No | - | The last name of the user |
| dataProfilePictureSrc | string | No | - | The location of the avatar image source file |
| dataAvatarSize | string | No | 'medium' | The size of the avatar. Options: 'extra-small', 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'extra-large', 'xx-large', or icon sizes |
| dataAvatarSizeMobile | string | No | - | The size of the avatar when using a mobile sized screen |
| dataBackgroundOption | string | No | 'default' | Sets the background color when using only initials. Options: '0', '1', '3', '4', 'high-contrast', 'theme' |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Sets the tooltip text when hovering |
| dataTooltipPlacement | string | No | 'bottom' | Sets the tooltip position |
| dataUseParentUiState | boolean | No | false | When true, if the avatar's direct parent is hovered/focused, the avatar will have a blue border |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Sets the avatar to a disabled state |
| dataSlot | string | No | - | Specifies the slot when used within another component |

## Examples

Basic avatar examples:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonAvatar } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AvatarExample() {
  return (
    <>
      <NeonAvatar />
      <NeonAvatar dataFirstName="Cory" />
      <NeonAvatar dataFirstName="Cory" dataLastName="Matthews" />
      <NeonAvatar
        dataFirstName="Cory"
        dataLastName="Matthews"
        dataProfilePictureSrc="example-files/cory-matthews.jpg"
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

Avatar with additional attributes:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonAvatar } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AvatarExampleAttributes() {
  return (
    <>
      <NeonAvatar
        id="__mfe__avatar-with-bottom-tooltip"
        dataFirstName="Cory"
        dataLastName="Matthews"
        dataTooltipText="I am large"
        dataAvatarSize="large"
        dataTooltipPlacement="top"
        dataProfilePictureSrc="example-files/cory-matthews.jpg"
      />

      <NeonAvatar
        id="__mfe__avatar-with-top-tooltip"
        dataFirstName="Cory"
        dataLastName="Matthews"
        dataTooltipText="I am small"
        dataAvatarSize="small"
        dataProfilePictureSrc="example-files/cory-matthews.jpg"
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

Avatar with parent UI state:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonAvatar } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AvatarExampleUseParentUiState() {
  const buttonStylesForDemo = {
    padding: '24px',
    display: 'inline-flex',
    gap: '16px',
    alignItems: 'center'
  };
  
  return (
    <button style={buttonStylesForDemo}>
      <NeonAvatar
        dataFirstName="Cory"
        dataLastName="Matthews"
        dataProfilePictureSrc="example-files/cory-matthews.jpg"
        dataUseParentUiState="true"
        dataAvatarSize="large"
      />
      <span>I am a button that contains an avatar</span>
    </button>
  );
}
```


# NeonBadge

A small, versatile status indicator component for displaying counts, notifications, or status indicators.

## When To Use

Use the NeonBadge component when you need to:

- Display a notification count or numerical indicator
- Show the number of items in a collection or category
- Indicate the presence of new or unread content
- Create a small visual indicator with color coding
- Add status indicators to interface elements
- Highlight that an element has associated notifications
- Show a small count indicator next to navigation items or buttons
- Display alerts or notifications that require minimal screen space
- Create a small visual marker in different colors to indicate status
- Show numerical values in a compact, visually distinct way

NeonBadge is designed to be a lightweight visual indicator that can be used in various contexts throughout your application to provide quick status information or numerical counts.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the badge |
| dataType | string | No | 'navy' | Sets type/color of badge. Options: 'yellow', 'orange', 'red', 'magenta', 'purple', 'cyan', 'navy', 'green', 'teal', 'gray', 'white' |
| dataCount | number | No | - | Sets the count text inside the badge |
| dataOverflowCount | number | No | 99 | Sets the max count, once exceeded will display that overflow-count+ |
| dataShowZero | boolean | No | false | Shows 0 when the count is 0 |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |

## Examples

Basic badge examples:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonBadge } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function BadgeExample() {
  return (
    <>
      <NeonBadge/>
      <NeonBadge dataCount={30}/>
      <NeonBadge dataCount={100}/>
    </>
  );
}
```

Different badge types/colors:

```jsx
      </div>
      <div>
        <NeonBadge dataCount={1} dataType="red"/>
        <NeonBadge dataCount={2} dataType="orange"/>

        <NeonBadge dataCount={5} dataType="teal"/>
        <NeonBadge dataCount={6} dataType="cyan"/>

        <NeonBadge dataCount={8} dataType="magenta"/>
```

# NeonBreadcrumbs

A navigation component that displays a hierarchical trail of links showing the user's current location within the application.

## When To Use

Use the NeonBreadcrumbs component when you need to:

- Provide users with context about their location within the application hierarchy
- Allow users to navigate back to previous levels in the navigation hierarchy
- Create clear navigational paths for deep or complex application structures
- Help users understand their current position relative to the overall site structure
- Enable quick backward navigation to parent pages
- Implement SEO-friendly navigation patterns
- Support users in understanding the relationship between different sections
- Improve overall user orientation within multi-level navigation systems
- Allow users to quickly jump to previously visited sections without using browser controls

NeonBreadcrumbs is a standard navigation pattern that enhances user orientation and provides efficient navigation options in multi-level applications. It works especially well when an application has clearly defined hierarchical levels or when users need to navigate between related sections.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the breadcrumbs component |
| breadcrumbs | Array<Breadcrumb> | No | - | Set a breadcrumb for each path needed. Do not set this if you are using data-global-breadcrumbs="true" |
| dataIsTopOfPage | boolean | No | false | If true, additional padding will be applied. Only use when breadcrumbs are at the top of the page |
| dataShowFirstAvatarBreadcrumb | boolean | No | true | If false and the first breadcrumb has avatar content it will not be rendered |
| dataGlobalBreadcrumbs | boolean | No | false | Set this to true in order to set the breadcrumbs globally using the breadcrumbs controller which can be retrieved by using getBreadcrumbs() |

## Examples

Basic breadcrumbs with avatar in first item:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonBreadcrumbs } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function BasicBreadcrumbsExample() {
  const breadcrumbs = [
    {
      text: 'Home',
      avatarFirstName: 'Cory',
      avatarLastName: 'Mathews',
      avatarProfilePictureSrc: '/example-files/cory-matthews.jpg',
      url: '#',
      onUserClick(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
      },
    },
    {
      text: 'Grades',
      url: '#',
      onUserClick(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
      },
    },
    {
      text: 'Science 3',
      url: '#',
      onUserClick(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
      },
    },
  ];
  return (
    <NeonBreadcrumbs id="breadcrumb-example" breadcrumbs={breadcrumbs} />
  );
}
```

Using global breadcrumbs API:
```jsx
import React, { useEffect } from 'react';
import { NeonBreadcrumbs, getBreadcrumbs } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function GlobalBreadcrumbsExample() {
  useEffect(() => {
    // Setup breadcrumbs for this page
    getBreadcrumbs().then((breadcrumbs) => {
      breadcrumbs.setBreadcrumbs('my-page', [
        { text: 'Home', url: '/' },
        { text: 'Dashboard', url: '/dashboard' },
        { text: 'Reports', url: '/dashboard/reports' }
      ]);
      
      // Turn on breadcrumbs for this module
      breadcrumbs.turnOnBreadcrumbsFor('my-page');
    });
    
    // Cleanup when component unmounts
    return () => {
      getBreadcrumbs().then((breadcrumbs) => {
        breadcrumbs.turnOffBreadcrumbsFor('my-page');
      });
    };
  }, []);

  return (
    <NeonBreadcrumbs id="global-breadcrumbs" dataGlobalBreadcrumbs="true" />
  );
}
```

Breadcrumbs with different styling variants:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonBreadcrumbs } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function BreadcrumbsVariantsExample() {
  // Single breadcrumb with avatar
  const singleBreadcrumb = [
    {
      text: 'Home',
      avatarFirstName: 'Cory',
      avatarLastName: 'Mathews',
      avatarProfilePictureSrc: '/example-files/cory-matthews.jpg',
      url: '#',
      onUserClick(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
      },
    }
  ];

  // Multiple breadcrumbs with themed avatar
  const multipleBreadcrumbs = [
    {
      text: 'Home',
      avatarFirstName: 'Cory',
      avatarLastName: 'Mathews',
      avatarBackgroundOption: 'theme',
      url: '#',
      onUserClick(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
      },
    },
    {
      text: 'Dashboard',
      url: '#',
      onUserClick(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
      },
    },
    {
      text: 'Reports',
      url: '#',
      onUserClick(event) {
        event.preventDefault();
      },
    }
  ];

  return (
    <>
      {/* Single breadcrumb with avatar */}
      <NeonBreadcrumbs 
        id="breadcrumb-single" 
        breadcrumbs={singleBreadcrumb} 
      />
      
      {/* Multiple breadcrumbs with avatar in first item */}
      <NeonBreadcrumbs 
        id="breadcrumb-multiple" 
        breadcrumbs={multipleBreadcrumbs} 
      />
      
      {/* Multiple breadcrumbs with hidden avatar */}
      <NeonBreadcrumbs 
        id="breadcrumb-no-avatar" 
        dataShowFirstAvatarBreadcrumb="false"
        breadcrumbs={multipleBreadcrumbs} 
      />
      
      {/* Breadcrumbs at top of page with extra padding */}
      <NeonBreadcrumbs 
        id="breadcrumb-top-page" 
        dataIsTopOfPage="true"
        breadcrumbs={multipleBreadcrumbs} 
      />
    </>
  );
}
```


# NeonButtonFooter

A versatile button footer component that provides a standardized way to display action buttons in containers such as cards, dialogs, drawers, and layouts.

## When To Use

Use the NeonButtonFooter component when you need to:

- Display primary and secondary actions at the bottom of a container
- Create a consistent layout for action buttons across your application
- Group related buttons with clear visual hierarchy
- Provide a tertiary action (like delete) that should be visually separated
- Present complex button patterns like button menus or split buttons
- Implement responsive button layouts that adapt to mobile screens
- Create a clear separation between content and actions

NeonButtonFooter is primarily used inside container components like NeonCardStandard, NeonModalDialog, NeonModalDrawer, and NeonLayoutDetail, typically placed in their footer slots.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the button footer |
| primaryButton | Button \| ButtonMenu \| ButtonSplit | No | - | Primary button or button menu to display in the footer. Usually a confirmation action like Save or Next. |
| buttons | Array<Button \| ButtonMenu \| ButtonSplit> | No | - | Buttons or button menus to display in the middle section of the footer. These are typically secondary actions. |
| tertiaryButton | Button \| ButtonMenu \| ButtonSplit | No | - | Tertiary button to display in the footer. Usually a destructive action like Delete. |

## Related Types

### Button
```typescript
interface Button {
  id: string;
  text: string;
  type?: 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'tertiary' | 'borderless' | 'utility' | 'utility-high-contrast' | 'back-to-page' | 'app-header' | 'ai';
  icon?: string;
  iconPosition?: 'left' | 'right';
  disabled?: boolean;
  isLoading?: boolean;
  tooltipText?: string;
  tooltipPlacement?: PopperPlacement;
  onClick: (event: Event) => void;
  href?: string;
  openInNewTab?: boolean;
  // Additional properties for badge support
  showBadge?: boolean;
  badgeCount?: number;
  badgeType?: BadgeType;
  // Others available but less commonly used
}
```

### ButtonMenu
```typescript
interface ButtonMenu extends Omit<Button, 'onClick'> {
  menuOptions: Array<MenuOption>;
}
```

### ButtonSplit
```typescript
interface ButtonSplit extends Button {
  options: Array<MenuOption>;
  menuHeading?: string;
  optionsTooltipText?: string;
  popperPlacement?: PopperPlacement;
}
```

## Examples

Basic button footer with primary action:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonButtonFooter } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ButtonFooterExampleBasic() {
  return (
    <NeonButtonFooter
      id="button-footer-basic"
      primaryButton={{
        id: "save-button",
        text: "Save",
        type: "primary",
        onClick: (event) => { console.log("Save clicked"); }
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Button footer with primary action and cancel:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonButtonFooter } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ButtonFooterExampleWithCancel() {
  return (
    <NeonButtonFooter
      id="button-footer-with-cancel"
      buttons={[
        {id: "cancel-button", text: "Cancel", type: "borderless", onClick: (event) => { console.log("Cancel clicked"); }}
      ]}
      primaryButton={{
        id: "save-button",
        text: "Save",
        type: "primary",
        onClick: (event) => { console.log("Save clicked"); }
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Complete button footer with tertiary button and button menu:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonButtonFooter } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { ButtonMenu } from '@neon/interfaces';

export function ButtonFooterExampleComplex() {
  return (
    <NeonButtonFooter
      id="button-footer-complex"
      tertiaryButton={{
        id: "delete-button",
        text: "Delete",
        type: "tertiary",
        onClick: (event) => { console.log("Delete clicked"); }
      }}
      buttons={[
        {id: "cancel-button", text: "Cancel", type: "borderless", onClick: (event) => { console.log("Cancel clicked"); }},
        {
          id: "other-actions",
          text: "Other Actions",
          menuOptions: [
            {
              id: "option-1",
              text: "Option 1",
              onClickCallback: (menuOption, context, event) => { console.log("Option 1 clicked"); }
            },
            {
              id: "option-2",
              text: "Option 2",
              onClickCallback: (menuOption, context, event) => { console.log("Option 2 clicked"); }
            }
          ]
        } as ButtonMenu
      ]}
      primaryButton={{
        id: "save-button",
        text: "Save",
        type: "primary",
        onClick: (event) => { console.log("Save clicked"); }
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Button footer in a card:
```jsx

  return (
    <NeonCardStandard dataHeading="Card with Button Footer">
      <div data-slot="body" className="__neon__text">
        <p>This is a card standard with a button footer</p>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="footer-full-width">
        <NeonButtonFooter
          id="card-button-footer"
          buttons={[
            {id: "cancel-button", text: "Cancel", type: "borderless", onClick: (event) => { console.log("Cancel clicked"); }}
          ]}
          primaryButton={{
            id: "save-button",
            text: "Save",
            type: "primary",
            onClick: (event) => { console.log("Save clicked"); }
          }}
        />
      </div>
    </NeonCardStandard>
  );
}
```

Navigation button footer with previous and next buttons:

```jsx
      ]}

        iconPosition: "right",
        type: "primary",
        onClick: (event) => { console.log("Next clicked"); }
      }}
    />
  );
}
```




# NeonButtonGroup

A component that displays a group of related buttons in a unified, selectable control with either horizontal or vertical layout.

## When To Use

Use the NeonButtonGroup component when you need to:

- Create a set of related toggle buttons that function as a single control
- Provide users with a visual way to select one option from a set of choices
- Implement filtering or sorting controls that allow users to switch between different views
- Display multiple related actions in a compact and organized layout
- Create segmented controls for toggling between different states
- Provide a user interface for single-selection from a small set of options
- Implement tabs-like navigation in space-constrained areas
- Display mode switchers (like view modes or display options)

NeonButtonGroup is ideal for situations where radio buttons would be too formal or take up too much space, but a clear selection from multiple options is needed.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the button group |
| buttons | Array<ButtonGroupButton> | Yes | - | Array of button configurations for the group |
| neonButtonGroupValueChange | (value: string \| undefined) => void | No | - | Event fired when the selected button changes |
| value | string | No | - | The currently selected button's ID |
| dateLayout | 'horizontal' \| 'vertical' | No | 'horizontal' | Controls the button group's layout orientation |
| dataLabelTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Adds extra top whitespace for use in form rows |
| dataHelperTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Adds extra bottom whitespace for use in form rows |
| dataAllowDeselect | boolean | No | true | When false, ensures at least one button remains selected |
| dataMobileFullWidth | boolean | No | false | Displays buttons at full width on mobile with horizontal scrolling |

## ButtonGroupButton Interface

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the button |
| text | string | Yes | - | Text label for the button |
| tooltip | string | No | - | Tooltip text to show on hover |
| ariaLabel | string | No | - | Accessible label for screen readers |
| icon | string | No | - | Icon name to display on the button |
| showText | boolean | No | true | Whether to show the text label |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Whether the button is disabled |

## Examples

Basic button group with horizontal layout:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonButtonGroup } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ButtonGroupExample() {
  const [selectedButton, setSelectedButton] = useState('featured');
  
  return (
    <NeonButtonGroup
      id="filter-buttons"
      buttons={[
        { id: 'featured', text: 'Featured' },
        { id: 'new', text: 'New', icon: 'star' },
        { id: 'popular', text: 'Popular' }
      ]}
      value={selectedButton}
      neonButtonGroupValueChange={(value) => {
        setSelectedButton(value);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Button group with icons only:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonButtonGroup } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ButtonGroupIconsExample() {
  const [selectedView, setSelectedView] = useState('list');
  
  return (
    <NeonButtonGroup
      id="view-switcher"
      buttons={[
        { id: 'list', text: 'List View', icon: 'view-list', showText: false, tooltip: 'List View' },
        { id: 'grid', text: 'Grid View', icon: 'grid-view', showText: false, tooltip: 'Grid View' },
        { id: 'calendar', text: 'Calendar View', icon: 'calendar-month', showText: false, tooltip: 'Calendar View' }
      ]}
      value={selectedView}
      neonButtonGroupValueChange={(value) => {
        setSelectedView(value);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Vertical layout button group:

```jsx
        { id: 'alphabetical', text: 'Sort A-Z', icon: 'sort-by-alpha' },

        setSelectedSort(value);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Button group with non-deselectable options:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonButtonGroup } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function NonDeselectableButtonGroupExample() {
  const [selectedRating, setSelectedRating] = useState('three-stars');
  
  return (
    <NeonButtonGroup
      id="rating-selector"
      buttons={[
        { id: 'one-star', text: '1 Star', icon: 'star' },
        { id: 'three-stars', text: '3 Stars', icon: 'star' },
        { id: 'five-stars', text: '5 Stars', icon: 'star' }
      ]}

      dataAllowDeselect={false}

        setSelectedRating(value);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Mobile-friendly full width button group:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonButtonGroup } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function MobileButtonGroupExample() {
  const [selectedCategory, setSelectedCategory] = useState('all');
  
  return (
    <NeonButtonGroup
      id="category-filter"
      dataMobileFullWidth={true}
      buttons={[
        { id: 'all', text: 'All Categories' },
        { id: 'electronics', text: 'Electronics' },
        { id: 'clothing', text: 'Clothing' },
        { id: 'home', text: 'Home & Garden' },
        { id: 'toys', text: 'Toys & Games' }
      ]}
      value={selectedCategory}
      neonButtonGroupValueChange={(value) => {
        setSelectedCategory(value);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```


# NeonButtonSplit

A split button component that combines a primary action button with a dropdown menu of additional options.

## When To Use

Use the NeonButtonSplit component when you need to:

- Provide a primary action with related secondary actions
- Save screen space by combining multiple related actions in one component
- Present a default or most common action prominently with additional options
- Group related actions where one action is performed more frequently than others
- Implement a primary call-to-action with contextual alternatives
- Create a hierarchical button that clearly distinguishes between main and secondary actions
- Provide quick access to a set of related commands without navigating to a new page
- Reduce cognitive load by keeping related options accessible but not immediately visible

NeonButtonSplit is ideal for situations where there is a primary action users will perform most often, but there are additional related actions that should be accessible when needed. It combines the clarity of a standard button with the flexibility of a dropdown menu.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the button split |
| dataText | string | Yes | - | Text displayed on the primary button |
| options | Array<MenuOption \| 'DIVIDER'> | Yes | - | Array of menu options or dividers for the dropdown |
| dataMenuHeading | string | No | 'Additional Options' | Heading text displayed at the top of the dropdown menu |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | When true, the entire button split is disabled |
| dataAriaLabel | string | No | - | Accessible label override for the button |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Tooltip text displayed when hovering over the primary button |
| dataTooltipPlacement | string | No | 'top' | Position of the tooltip. Options: 'top', 'top-start', 'top-end', 'right', 'right-start', 'right-end', 'bottom', 'bottom-start', 'bottom-end', 'left', 'left-start', 'left-end' |
| dataOptionsTooltipText | string | No | - | Tooltip text displayed when hovering over the dropdown button |
| dataPopperPlacement | string | No | 'bottom-start' | Position of the dropdown menu. Options: 'top-start', 'top-end', 'bottom-start', 'bottom-end' |
| dataLabelTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Add extra top whitespace for use in neon form rows |
| dataHelperTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Add extra top whitespace for use in neon form rows |
| onClick | function | No | - | Function called when the primary button is clicked |
| context | any | No | - | Additional context data that can be passed to menu option callbacks |

## Examples

Simple button split with options:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonButtonSplit } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { DEFAULT_SYSTEM_MESSAGES_FLOATING_ID, showSystemMessage } from '@neon/exported-utils';

export function ButtonSplitExampleSimple() {
  const menuOptions = [
    {
      id: 'menu-example-simple-option-1',
      text: 'Option One',
    },
    'DIVIDER',
    {
      id: 'menu-example-simple-option-2',
      text: 'Option Two',
      iconName: 'calendar-note'
    }, {
      id: 'menu-example-simple-option-3',
      text: 'Option Three',
      iconName: 'build'
    }
  ];

  return (
    <NeonButtonSplit
      id="__mfe__btn-split"
      dataText="Default"
      dataAriaLabel="Button Split Example"
      options={menuOptions}
      onClick={(event) => {
        showSystemMessage('You clicked me!', {
          sendTo: DEFAULT_SYSTEM_MESSAGES_FLOATING_ID,
          autoDismiss: true,
          messageType: 'info',
          autoDismissTime: 3000
        });
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Button split with tooltips:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonButtonSplit } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ButtonSplitExampleTooltips() {
  const menuOptions = [
    {
      id: 'menu-example-simple-option-1',
      text: 'Option One',
    },
    'DIVIDER',
    {
      id: 'menu-example-simple-option-2',
      text: 'Option Two',
      iconName: 'calendar-note'
    }, {
      id: 'menu-example-simple-option-3',
      text: 'Option Three',
      iconName: 'build'
    }
  ];

  return (
    <div className="__neon__form">
      <NeonButtonSplit
        id="button-split-secondary-text-tooltip-id"
        dataText="Tooltip Button"
        options={menuOptions}
        dataTooltipText="I am a text tooltip!"
        dataMenuHeading="check out these cool options"
        onClick={(event) => {
          console.log('You clicked me!');
        }}
      />

      <NeonButtonSplit
        id="button-split-secondary-menu-tooltip-id"
        dataText="Tooltip Options"
        options={menuOptions}
        dataOptionsTooltipText="I am a options tooltip!"
        dataMenuHeading="check out these cool options"
        onClick={() => {
          console.log('You would normally perform an action here');
        }}
      />

      <NeonButtonSplit
        id="button-split-secondary-menu-and-text-tooltip-id"
        dataText="Tooltip Options and Text"
        options={menuOptions}
        dataTooltipText="I am a text tooltip!"
        dataOptionsTooltipText="I am a options tooltip!"
        dataMenuHeading="check out these cool options"
        onClick={() => {
          console.log('I\'m sure you could do some cool stuff here!');
        }}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

Disabled button split:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonButtonSplit } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ButtonSplitDisabledExample() {
  const menuOptions = [
    {
      id: 'menu-example-simple-option-1',

      id: 'menu-example-simple-option-2',
      text: 'Option Two',

```

Button split with nested menu options:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonButtonSplit } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ButtonSplitComplexExample() {
  const menuOptions = [
    {
      id: 'menu-example-complex-option-1',
      text: 'Option One',
    },
    'DIVIDER',
    {
      id: 'menu-example-complex-option-2',
      text: 'Option Two',
      iconName: 'calendar-note'
    }, {
      id: 'menu-example-complex-option-3',
      text: 'Option Three',
      iconName: 'build',
      onClickCallback: () => {
        alert('Option Three clicked.');
      },
      menuOptionChildren: [{
        iconName: 'open-in-new|rtl-flip',
        id: 'child-item-1',
        text: 'This should go to google!',
        onClickCallback: (menuOption) => {
          window.open(menuOption.url);
        },
        url: 'https://www.google.com/'
      },
      {
        iconName: 'clipboard-edit',
        id: 'child-item-2',
        text: 'this is the second child element'
      }],
    }, {
      id: 'menu-example-complex-option-4',
      text: 'Option Disabled',
      iconName: 'build',
      isDisabled: (item) => { return true; }
    }
  ];

  return (
    <NeonButtonSplit
      id="complex-button-split"
      dataText="Complex Example"
      options={menuOptions}
      dataMenuHeading="Complex Menu Example"
      onClick={() => {
        console.log('Primary action clicked');
      }}
    />
  );
}
```


# NeonButton

A versatile button component that serves as the primary interactive element for user actions in the Neon Design System.

## When To Use

Use the NeonButton component when you need to:

- Trigger an action or event when clicked
- Submit a form
- Navigate to another page or external link
- Provide user controls for interactive features
- Create primary call-to-action elements
- Provide affordance for user interactions
- Create a visually consistent set of action controls
- Implement accessible interactive elements

NeonButton is the foundational button component in the Neon Design System and supports various styles, states, and configurations. It can be used standalone or as part of button groups, forms, cards, and other container components.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the button |
| dataText | string | Yes | - | The text displayed on the button (required for accessibility even when not visible) |
| dataType | string | No | 'secondary' | Button style type: 'primary', 'secondary', 'tertiary', 'borderless', 'utility', 'utility-high-contrast', 'back-to-page', 'back-to-page-high-contrast', 'app-header', 'ai', 'inverse' |
| dataShowText | boolean | No | true | When false, text does not appear on the button |
| dataShowTextMobile | boolean | No | true | When false, text does not appear on mobile devices |
| dataAriaLabel | string | No | - | Custom accessibility label that overrides the dataText |
| dataShape | string | No | 'rectangular' | Button shape: 'rectangular' or 'pill' |
| dataIcon | string | No | - | Icon name to display on the button |
| dataIconPosition | string | No | 'left' | Icon position: 'left' or 'right' (only 'caret-down' is allowed on the right) |
| dataConstrainWidth | boolean | No | true | When false, button takes full width |
| dataIsSubmit | boolean | No | false | When true, button type becomes "submit" for form submission |
| dataIsLoading | boolean | No | false | Shows a loading indicator instead of text when true |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Text to display in tooltip on hover |
| dataTooltipPlacement | string | No | 'top' | Tooltip position: 'top', 'top-start', 'top-end', 'right', 'right-start', 'right-end', 'bottom', 'bottom-start', 'bottom-end', 'left', 'left-start', 'left-end' |
| dataShowBadge | boolean | No | false | When true, displays a badge on the button |
| dataBadgeCount | number | No | - | Number to display in the badge |
| dataBadgeOverflowCount | number | No | - | Maximum count to display before showing overflow |
| dataBadgeShowZero | boolean | No | false | When true, shows badge with zero count |
| dataBadgeType | string | No | 'navy' | Badge color: 'navy', 'magenta', 'red', 'orange', 'yellow', 'green', 'teal', 'cyan', 'purple', 'gray', 'white' |
| href | string | No | - | When set, renders button as an anchor tag with this URL |
| dataOpenInNewTab | boolean | No | false | When true and href is set, opens link in new tab |
| dataLabelTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Adds extra whitespace for alignment in form rows |
| dataHelperTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Adds extra whitespace for alignment in form rows |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | When true, button is disabled and not interactive |
| onClick | function | No | - | Function called when button is clicked |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| button-body | No | For adding rich text content inside the button |

## Examples

Basic button with click handler:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonButton } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ButtonExampleBasic() {
  return (
    <NeonButton
      id="example-button"
      dataText="Click Me"
      onClick={() => console.log('Button clicked')}
    />
  );
}
```

Different button types:
```jsx

  return (
    <div className="__neon__button-layout">
      <NeonButton id="primary-btn" dataType="primary" dataText="Primary" />
      <NeonButton id="secondary-btn" dataType="secondary" dataText="Secondary" />
      <NeonButton id="tertiary-btn" dataType="tertiary" dataText="Tertiary" />
      <NeonButton id="borderless-btn" dataType="borderless" dataText="Borderless" />
      <NeonButton id="utility-btn" dataType="utility" dataText="Utility" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

Loading and disabled states:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';

export function ButtonExampleStates() {
  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(false);

  const handleClick = () => {
    setIsLoading(true);
    setTimeout(() => setIsLoading(false), 2000);
  };

  return (
    <div className="__neon__button-layout">
      <NeonButton
        id="loading-btn"
        dataText="Save Changes"
        dataType="primary"
        dataIsLoading={isLoading}
        onClick={handleClick}
      />
      <NeonButton
        id="disabled-btn"
        dataText="Cannot Click"
        dataType="primary"
        disabled={true}
      />

}
```

```jsx
      />
```

# NeonCardAction

A clickable card component for navigation or selection that features icons, tags, headings, and interactive elements.

## When To Use

Use the NeonCardAction component when you need to:

- Create interactive cards that navigate to different views or activate actions
- Display a visual representation of an action or option that users can select
- Group related action information with visual indicators like icons and tags
- Implement clickable navigation tiles or action cards in your application
- Create selectable option cards with consistent styling
- Present action options with supporting text and visual elements
- Add user avatars or selection dropdowns to action cards
- Create AI action cards with distinct styling

NeonCardAction is designed for interactive card experiences that lead to further actions. It features a prominent chevron icon to indicate its actionable nature and supports various interactive elements like selection dropdowns and avatar stacks.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the card action |
| dataHeading | string | No | - | Main heading text |
| dataSubheading | string | No | - | Secondary text under the heading |
| dataColor | string | No | - | Color theme for the action card (e.g., 'teal', 'blue') |
| dataFullColor | boolean | No | false | Whether to apply full color styling to the card |
| dataIsAi | boolean | No | false | Whether to style the card as an AI component |
| dataIcon | string | No | - | Icon name to display in the card |
| dataTagText | string | No | - | Text to display in a tag badge |
| selectOptions | Array<SelectOption> | No | - | Options to display in a select dropdown |
| value | string | No | - | Current selected value for the dropdown |
| users | Array<AvatarUser> | No | - | User avatars to display in the card |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class for the card |
| neonCardActionClick | function | No | - | Function called when the card is clicked |
| neonCardActionValueChange | function | No | - | Function called when a dropdown value changes |

## Examples

Simple card action with heading and subheading:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonCardAction } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CardActionSimpleExample() {
  return (
    <NeonCardAction
      id="simple-action-card"
      dataColor="teal"
      dataFullColor="false"
      dataHeading="Heading"
      dataSubheading="Sub Heading"
    />
  );
}
```

```jsx

    <NeonCardAction
      id="tag-color-action-card"

      dataFullColor="true"
      dataIcon="file-edit"
      dataHeading="Heading"
      dataSubheading="Sub Heading"
      dataTagText="update"
    />
  );
}
```

# NeonCardHeader

A versatile header component for cards that provides consistent styling with support for colors, icons, tags, and avatars.

## When To Use

Use the NeonCardHeader component when you need to:

- Create visually distinct headers for card components
- Apply consistent branding or category colors to card headers
- Include icons, avatars, or tags in card headers to provide additional context
- Create cohesive section headers within a card-based interface
- Highlight different content categories with color-coded headers
- Add visual hierarchy to card elements
- Group related information with a distinctive heading element
- Enhance card components with a professional, branded appearance

NeonCardHeader is designed to be used as a header element within NeonCardStandard or other card components. It provides a standardized way to display headings with visual enhancements like colors, icons, tags, and avatars.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the card header |
| dataHeading | string | Yes | - | The heading text displayed in the card header |
| dataSubheading | string | No | - | Optional subheading text for additional context |
| dataColor | string | No | - | Background color for the header. Options: 'cyan', 'magenta', 'yellow', 'purple', 'green', 'orange', 'teal' |
| dataColorType | string | No | 'light' | Color intensity. Options: 'light', 'dark' |
| dataBackgroundImage | string | No | - | URL path to a background image for the header |
| dataIcon | string | No | - | Icon to display in the header (uses standard icon names) |
| dataIconSize | string | No | - | Size of the icon. Options: 'x-small', 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'x-large' |
| dataIconStackShape | string | No | - | Shape for icon stack background. Options: 'circle', 'square', 'hexagon', 'diamond' |
| dataTagText | string | No | - | Text for a tag in the header |
| dataTagSubtext | string | No | - | Secondary text for a tag |
| dataTagType | string | No | - | Color/type for the tag (e.g. 'teal', 'purple', 'update') |
| dataTagIcon | string | No | - | Icon to display in the tag |
| dataShowAvatar | boolean | No | false | Whether to show an avatar in the header |
| dataAvatarFirstName | string | No | - | First name for avatar in header |
| dataAvatarLastName | string | No | - | Last name for avatar in header |
| dataAvatarProfilePictureSrc | string | No | - | Image source for avatar |
| dataAvatarBackgroundOption | string | No | - | Background style for avatar (e.g., "theme") |
| children | React.ReactNode | No | - | Content to display inside the card header |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles for the card header |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| card-header-actions | No | For content in the top right of the card header, typically action buttons |

## Examples

Basic card header with color:

```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonCardHeader } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CardHeaderExampleBasic() {
  return (
    <NeonCardHeader
      dataHeading="Card Header"
      dataColor="cyan"
    />
  );
}
```

```jsx

    <div>

      <NeonCardHeader dataHeading="Purple" dataColor="purple" />
      <NeonCardHeader dataHeading="Green" dataColor="green" />

      <NeonCardHeader dataHeading="Teal" dataColor="teal" />

      <NeonCardHeader dataHeading="Dark cyan" dataColor="cyan" dataColorType="dark" />
      <NeonCardHeader dataHeading="Dark magenta" dataColor="magenta" dataColorType="dark" />
      <NeonCardHeader dataHeading="Dark yellow" dataColor="yellow" dataColorType="dark" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

Card header within a card standard component:

```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonCardHeader, NeonCardStandard } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CardHeaderExampleInCardStandard() {
  return (
    <NeonCardStandard>
      <div data-slot="header">
        <NeonCardHeader
          dataHeading="Card Header"
          dataSubheading="This is the card subheading."
          dataColor="purple"
          dataColorType="dark"
          dataIcon="bolt"
          dataIconStackShape="hexagon"
          dataTagText="Tag"
          dataTagSubtext="tag subtext"
          dataTagIcon="lock-locked"
          dataTagType="magenta" >
          <div data-slot="card-header-actions">
            <NeonButton id="action-button" dataText="Utility Button" dataType="utility-high-contrast" dataIcon="more-vert"/>
          </div>
        </NeonCardHeader>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="body">
        <p className="__neon__text">
          This is the body of the card standard.
        </p>
      </div>
    </NeonCardStandard>
  );
}
```




# NeonCardMedia

A specialized card component designed for displaying media content (images, illustrations, or icons) with accompanying text and interactive elements.

## When To Use

Use the NeonCardMedia component when you need to:

- Display content that prominently features visual media alongside text
- Create cards with images, illustrations, or icons as a focal point
- Implement media-rich interactive cards for selection or navigation
- Present content in both vertical (media above content) or horizontal (media beside content) layouts
- Create visual navigation elements that require imagery
- Display media content with consistent aspect ratios across your interface
- Build selectable card interfaces that include visual elements
- Present media content with optional header, body content, and footer actions

NeonCardMedia is ideal for creating visually engaging content cards that feature images or other media prominently. It extends the functionality of the standard card component with specialized features for media display and layout control.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the card |
| dataHeading | string | Yes | - | Card title text |
| dataHeadingLevel | string | No | 'h2' | Heading level for the title. Options: 'h1', 'h2', 'h3', 'h4', 'h5', 'h6' |
| dataSubheading | string | No | - | Subtitle text |
| dataHeaderIcon | string | No | - | Icon to display in the header |
| dataHeaderIconColor | NeonColor | No | - | The color of the header icon |
| dataHeaderIconColorWeight | NeonColorWeight | No | - | The weight of the header icon color |
| dataHeadingUrl | string | No | - | The URL for the header |
| dataHeadingUrlOpenInNewTab | boolean | No | false | If true, the header URL will open in a new tab |
| dataSubheadingIcon | string | No | - | The icon to display in the subheading |
| dataMediaBorder | boolean | No | false | If true, a border will be displayed on the media when horizontal |
| dataMediaAspectRatio | string | No | '3:2' | The aspect ratio of the media. Options: '4:1', '3:1', '2:1', '16:9', '3:2', '4:3', '1:1', '3:4' |
| dataMediaFit | string | No | 'cover' | How the media should fit in the container. Options: 'cover', 'contain' |
| dataMediaImgSrc | string | No | - | The image source for the media |
| dataMediaImgAlt | string | No | - | The image alt text for the media |
| dataMediaSize | string | No | 'medium' | The size of the media. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'x-large' |
| dataMediaIllustration | string | No | - | The illustration to display in the media |
| dataMediaIllustrationColor | IllustrationColor | No | - | The color of the illustration |
| dataMediaIllustrationBackground | IllustrationBackground | No | - | The background of the illustration. Options: 'none', 'simple', 'complex' |
| dataMediaIllustrationShowPeople | boolean | No | true | If false, people will be removed in the illustration |
| dataMediaIcon | string | No | - | The icon to display in the media |
| dataMediaIconColor | NeonColor | No | - | The color of the media icon |
| dataMediaIconColorWeight | NeonColorWeight | No | - | The weight of the media icon color |
| dataOrientation | string | No | 'vertical' | The orientation of the card media. Options: 'vertical', 'horizontal' |
| dataFooterBorder | boolean | No | false | If true, a border will be displayed on the footer |
| dataAvatarFirstName | string | No | - | The first name for the avatar |
| dataAvatarLastName | string | No | - | The last name for the avatar |
| dataAvatarProfilePictureSrc | string | No | - | The profile picture source for the avatar |
| dataAvatarBackgroundOption | AvatarBackgroundOption | No | - | The background option for the avatar. Options: '0', '1', '2', '3', '4', 'high-contrast', 'theme' |
| dataIsLoading | boolean | No | false | If true, the card media will display a loading state |
| dataIsWhiteBackground | boolean | No | false | If true, the card media will have a white background |
| dataControlType | string | No | - | The control type for the card media. Options: 'checkbox', 'radio' |
| dataIsAi | boolean | No | false | When true, adds an AI border to the card |
| dataHeadingSize | string | No | - | Size of the heading. Options: 'medium', 'large' |
| name | string | No | - | The name for the radio group when dataControlType is set to "radio" |
| value | boolean | No | false | Sets the selected state of the checkbox or radio input |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | If true, the card is disabled and cannot be interacted with |
| neonValueChange | function | No | - | Callback called whenever the card selected state changes with checkbox or radio |
| headingUrlOnClickCallback | function | No | - | If provided, called instead of running the default link click behavior |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| card-media-object | No | A slot for adding content to the media object |
| card-media-actions | No | For button actions that appear on the top right of the content section |
| card-media-body | No | The main content slot |
| card-media-footer | No | For button actions that appear on the bottom of the content section |

## Examples

Simple vertical and horizontal examples:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonCardMedia } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CardMediaExampleSimple() {
  return (
    <div className="__neon__grid-container">
      <div className="__neon__grid-1-2">
        <NeonCardMedia
          id="example-card-media-vertical"
          dataIsWhiteBackground="true"
          dataHeading="Vertical Example"
          dataMediaImgSrc="example-files/img/folsom-office.png"
          dataMediaImgAlt="Placeholder image"
        />
      </div>
      <div className="__neon__grid-1-2">
        <NeonCardMedia
          id="example-card-media-horizontal"
          dataIsWhiteBackground="true"
          dataOrientation="horizontal"
          dataHeading="Horizontal Example"
          dataMediaImgSrc="example-files/img/folsom-office.png"
          dataMediaImgAlt="Placeholder image"
        />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Different media types:
```jsx

          </div>
        </NeonCardMedia>
      </div>
    </div>

}
```

Card media with actions and footer:

Selectable card with checkbox:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonCardMedia } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CardMediaExampleCheckbox() {
  const [isSelected, setIsSelected] = useState(false);
  
  return (
    <NeonCardMedia
      id="example-card-media-checkbox"
      dataIsWhiteBackground="true"
      dataHeading="Selectable Card"
      dataMediaImgSrc="example-files/img/folsom-office.png"
      dataMediaImgAlt="Placeholder image"
      dataControlType="checkbox"
      value={isSelected}
      neonValueChange={(value) => setIsSelected(value)}
    >
      <div data-slot="card-media-body">
        <p className="__neon__text">Click this card to select it</p>
      </div>
    </NeonCardMedia>
  );
}
```
