# NeonCardSelectable

A selectable card component that provides interactive selection functionality with checkbox or radio button controls, while maintaining a consistent card design pattern.

## When To Use

Use the NeonCardSelectable component when you need to:

- Allow users to select one or more options from a set of visually rich choices
- Create a more engaging and visually appealing alternative to standard radio buttons or checkboxes
- Display selectable items with supporting content, icons, or illustrations
- Implement a visually consistent selection pattern for complex content
- Group related information in a selectable container
- Create an interactive card-based selection experience
- Offer users radio button functionality (select one from many) in a card format
- Provide checkbox functionality (select multiple) in a card format
- Create a card that can be clicked/tapped as a whole to trigger selection

NeonCardSelectable extends the functionality of standard card components by adding selection capabilities, making it ideal for scenarios where users need to choose between visually rich options rather than simple text-based choices.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the card |
| dataHeading | string | Yes | - | Card title text |
| dataSubheading | string | No | - | Subtitle text for the card |
| dataIsWhiteBackground | boolean | No | false | Set to true when the card is on a white background |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | When true, disables the card selection functionality |
| dataDisabledTooltipText | string | No | - | Tooltip text to show when the card is disabled |
| value | boolean \| 'indeterminate' | No | false | Current selected state of the card |
| name | string | No | - | Name attribute for radio button grouping (required when dataControlType="radio") |
| dataHeadingUrl | string | No | - | URL for the heading to act as a link |
| dataHeadingUrlOpenInNewTab | boolean | No | false | When true, opens heading URL in a new tab |
| headingUrlOnClickCallback | function | No | - | Custom function to handle heading click instead of default navigation |
| dataControlType | 'radio' \| 'checkbox' | No | - | Type of selection control to use |
| dataHeaderTagType | string | No | 'gray' | Color/type for the header tag (e.g., "teal", "navy") |
| dataHeaderTagIcon | string | No | - | Icon to display in the header tag |
| dataHeaderTagText | string | No | - | Text for the header tag |
| dataHeaderTagSubtext | string | No | - | Subtext for the header tag |
| dataHeaderIcon | string | No | - | Icon to display in the card header |
| dataHeaderIconColor | string | No | 'gray' | Color for the header icon |
| dataHeaderIconColorWeight | string | No | '700' | Weight/intensity of the header icon color (100-800) |
| children | React.ReactNode | No | - | Content to display inside the card |
| neonValueChange | function | No | - | Callback for when the card's selected state changes |
| dataInjectionSpacing | boolean | No | true | When false, removes padding around the main content |
| dataIsAi | boolean | No | false | When true, adds an AI-specific border styling to the card |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| card-selectable-actions | No | Content for action buttons in the upper right corner of the card |
| card-selectable-body | Yes | The main content area of the card |
| card-selectable-footer | No | Content for the card footer, typically used for buttons or actions |

## Examples

Simple selectable card with actions:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonCardSelectable, NeonMenu } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CardSelectableExampleSimple() {
  const menuOptions = [
    {
      id: 'menu-example-simple-option-1',
      text: 'Option One',
      iconName: 'folder'
    },
    {
      id: 'menu-example-simple-option-2',
      text: 'Option Two',
      iconName: 'folder-star'
    },
    {
      id: 'menu-example-simple-option-3',
      text: 'Option Three',
      iconName: 'folder'
    }
  ];

  return (
    <NeonCardSelectable
      id="card-selectable-simple"
      dataIsWhiteBackground="true"
      dataHeading="Academic Skills and Concepts"
    >
      <div data-slot="card-selectable-actions">
        <NeonMenu
          id="menu-example"
          dataHeaderText="Menu Options"
          dataShowHeaderText="false"
          options={menuOptions}
          dataPopperPlacement="bottom-end"
        >
          <div data-slot="popper-trigger">
            <NeonButton
              id="menu-example-btn"
              dataText="Simple Menu Button"
              dataType="utility"
              dataIcon="more-vert"
              dataShowText="false"
            />
          </div>
        </NeonMenu>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="card-selectable-body">
        <p>Academic Skills and Concepts provides student opportunities to prepare for the demanding High School Assessments.</p>
      </div>
    </NeonCardSelectable>
  );
}
```

Selectable cards using radio buttons:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonCardSelectable } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CardSelectableExampleRadios() {
  const [selectedCard, setSelectedCard] = useState();

  return (
    <div className="__neon__grid-container">
      <div className="__neon__grid-1-4">
        <NeonCardSelectable
          id="card-selectable-one"
          dataIsWhiteBackground="true"
          dataHeading="Card 1"
          name="my-radio-group"
          dataControlType="radio"
          value={selectedCard === 'first-card'}
          neonValueChange={() => {
            setSelectedCard('first-card');
          }}
        >
          <div data-slot="card-selectable-body">
            <p>Card One</p>
          </div>
        </NeonCardSelectable>
      </div>

      <div className="__neon__grid-1-4">
        <NeonCardSelectable
          id="card-selectable-two"
          dataIsWhiteBackground="true"
          dataHeading="Card 2"
          name="my-radio-group"
          dataControlType="radio"
          value={selectedCard === 'second-card'}
          neonValueChange={() => {
            setSelectedCard('second-card');
          }}
        >
          <div data-slot="card-selectable-body">
            <p>Card Two</p>
          </div>
        </NeonCardSelectable>
      </div>

      <div className="__neon__grid-1-4">
        <NeonCardSelectable
          id="card-selectable-three"
          dataIsWhiteBackground="true"
          dataHeading="Card 3"
          name="my-radio-group"
          dataControlType="radio"
          value={selectedCard === 'third-card'}
          neonValueChange={() => {
            setSelectedCard('third-card');
          }}
        >
          <div data-slot="card-selectable-body">
            <p>Card Three</p>
          </div>
        </NeonCardSelectable>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Card with all slots demonstrated:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonCardSelectable } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CardSelectableExampleSlots() {
  return (
    <NeonCardSelectable
      id="card-selectable-slots"
      dataIsWhiteBackground="true"
      dataHeading="Show Off Slots"
    >
      <div data-slot="card-selectable-actions">
        <div>Card actions slot content</div>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="card-selectable-body">
        <div>Card body slot content</div>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="card-selectable-footer">
        <div>Card footer slot content</div>
      </div>
    </NeonCardSelectable>
  );
}
```

Advanced card with icon, tag, and checkbox:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonCardSelectable } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CardSelectableExampleAdvanced() {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState(false);

  return (
    <NeonCardSelectable
      id="card-selectable-advanced"
      dataIsWhiteBackground="true"
      dataHeading="Math Fundamentals"
      dataSubheading="Course includes algebra and geometry concepts"
      dataHeaderIcon="calculate"
      dataHeaderIconColor="navy"
      dataHeaderTagText="Required"
      dataHeaderTagType="red"
      dataControlType="checkbox"
      value={selected}
      neonValueChange={(newValue) => {
        setSelected(newValue);
      }}
    >
      <div data-slot="card-selectable-body">
        <p>This course covers essential mathematical principles that students need to master before advancing to higher-level mathematics.</p>
      </div>
    </NeonCardSelectable>
  );
}
```


# NeonCardStandard

A versatile card component for displaying content in a contained, styled container with consistent elevation and spacing.

## When To Use

Use the NeonCardStandard component when you need to:

- Group related content or information together in a visually distinct container
- Create clear visual separation between different sections on a page
- Display content that belongs together in a logical unit
- Implement a consistent container design throughout your application
- Present content in a clean, bordered container with optional header and footer
- Create layouts with multiple content cards that need consistent styling
- Implement content containers with consistent elevation and shadow effects
- Display information that should be visually separated from the page background

NeonCardStandard is the foundational card component in the Neon Design System and serves as a versatile container for various types of content. Use it whenever you need to visually group related information. For more specialized card use cases, consider NeonCardSelectable for making selectable cards or NeonCardMedia for cards with media content.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the card |
| dataHeading | string | No | - | Card title text |
| dataSubheading | string | No | - | Subtitle text |
| dataHeaderIcon | string | No | - | Icon to display in header |
| dataIsWhiteBackground | boolean | No | true | Whether card has white background |
| dataHeaderTagText | string | No | - | Text for a tag in the header |
| dataHeaderTagSubtext | string | No | - | Secondary text for a tag |
| dataHeaderTagType | string | No | - | Color/type for the tag (e.g., "teal") |
| dataHeaderAvatarFirstName | string | No | - | First name for avatar in header |
| dataHeaderAvatarLastName | string | No | - | Last name for avatar in header |
| dataHeaderAvatarProfilePictureSrc | string | No | - | Image source for avatar |
| dataHeaderAvatarBackgroundOption | string | No | - | Background style for avatar (e.g., "theme") |
| children | React.ReactNode | No | - | Content to display inside the card |
| dataSize | string | No | 'medium' | Size of the card. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'x-large', 'auto' |
| dataPadding | string | No | 'medium' | Padding inside the card. Options: 'none', 'small', 'medium', 'large' |
| dataElevation | string | No | 'medium' | Elevation/shadow level of the card. Options: 'none', 'small', 'medium', 'large' |
| dataBorderRadius | string | No | 'medium' | Border radius of the card. Options: 'none', 'small', 'medium', 'large' |
| dataShowBorder | boolean | No | true | Whether to show a border around the card |
| dataBackgroundColor | string | No | 'default' | Background color of the card. Options: 'default', 'light', 'white', 'transparent' |
| dataFullWidth | boolean | No | false | Whether the card should take up the full available width |
| dataFullHeight | boolean | No | false | Whether the card should take up the full available height |
| dataAlignment | string | No | 'left' | Alignment of the content inside the card. Options: 'left', 'center', 'right' |
| onClick | function | No | - | Function to call when the card is clicked |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles for the card |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |
| ariaLabel | string | No | - | Accessible label for the card |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| header | No | Custom header content |
| card-actions | No | For content in the top right of the card |
| pre-body | No | Content placed right before the body slot |
| body | Yes | The main card content area |
| post-body | No | Content placed right after the body slot |
| footer-full-width | No | For content spanning the full footer width (recommended for NeonButtonFooter) |
| footer-primary | No | (Deprecated) Use footer-full-width with NeonButtonFooter instead |
| footer-secondary | No | (Deprecated) Use footer-full-width with NeonButtonFooter instead |
| footer-tertiary | No | (Deprecated) Use footer-full-width with NeonButtonFooter instead |

## Examples

Simple card with heading:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonCardStandard } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CardStandardExampleSimple() {
  return (
    <NeonCardStandard dataHeading="Things that are cool">
      <div data-slot="body">
        <p className="__neon__text">This is the card contents.</p>
      </div>
    </NeonCardStandard>
  );
}
```

```jsx
      <div data-slot="card-actions">
        <div>Card actions slot content</div>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="pre-body" className="__neon__text">
        <div>Pre-body slot content</div>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="body" className="__neon__text">
        <div>Body slot content</div>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="post-body" className="__neon__text">
        <div>Post-body slot content</div>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="footer-primary">
        <div>Footer primary content</div>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="footer-secondary">
        <div>Footer secondary content</div>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="footer-tertiary">
        <div>Footer tertiary content</div>
      </div>
```

Complex card with header elements and button:
```jsx

import { NeonButton, NeonCardStandard } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CardStandardExampleComplex() {
  return (
    <NeonCardStandard
      dataHeading="The Complex Neon Card Standard"
      dataSubheading="This is the sub heading."
      dataIsWhiteBackground="false"
      dataHeaderIcon="article"
      dataHeaderTagText="Main text"
      dataHeaderTagSubtext="Sub text"
      dataHeaderTagType="teal"
      >
      <div data-slot="card-actions">
        <NeonButton id="card-actions-button" dataType="utility" dataIcon="more-horiz" dataShowText="false" dataText="actions" />
      </div>

      </div>

        <p>another paragraph to highlight these paragraphs being placed within the body container</p>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="post-body" className="__neon__text">
        <p>Post Body slot</p>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="footer-primary">
        <NeonButton id="primary-button" dataType="primary" dataText="Primary" />
      </div>
      <div data-slot="footer-secondary">
        <NeonButton id="secondary-button" dataType="secondary" dataText="Secondary" />
      </div>
      <div data-slot="footer-tertiary">
        <NeonButton id="tertiary-button" dataType="tertiary" dataText="Tertiary" />
      </div>
    </NeonCardStandard>
  );
}
```

Card with avatar in header:

Card with full-width footer slot:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonCardStandard } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CardStandardExampleFullWidthSlot() {
  return (
    <NeonCardStandard dataHeading="Neon Card Standard Slots" dataSubheading="This is the sub heading.">
      <div data-slot="body" className="__neon__text">
        <div>Card body content</div>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="footer-full-width">
        <div>Footer full width content</div>
      </div>
    </NeonCardStandard>
  );
}
```

Card with button footer:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonButtonFooter, NeonCardStandard } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CardStandardExampleButtonFooter() {
  return (
    <NeonCardStandard
      dataHeading="NeonCardStandard with a NeonButtonFooter"
      dataHeaderIcon="article"
    >
      <div data-slot="body" className="__neon__text">
        <p>This is a card standard with a button footer</p>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="footer-full-width">
        <NeonButtonFooter
          id="button-footer"
          buttons={[
            {
              id: 'button-menu',
              text: 'Button Menu',
              type: 'borderless',
              onClick: () => { console.log('button-menu'); },
              menuOptions: [
                {
                  id: 'menu-option-1',
                  text: 'Button Menu 1',
                  onClickCallback: () => { console.log('menu option 1'); },
                },
                {
                  id: 'menu-option-2',
                  text: 'Button Menu 2',
                  onClickCallback: () => { console.log('menu option 2'); },
                }
              ]
            },
            {
              id: 'button-delete',
              text: 'Delete',
              onClick: () => { console.log('delete'); },
            }
          ]}
          primaryButton={{
            id: 'primary-save',
            text: 'Save',
            onClick: () => { console.log('save'); },
          }}
          tertiaryButton={{
            id: 'tertiary-cancel',
            text: 'Cancel',
            onClick: () => { console.log('cancel'); },
          }}
        />
      </div>
    </NeonCardStandard>
  );
}
```


# NeonCheckboxField

A group of checkbox options that allows users to select multiple values from a list of choices.

## When To Use

Use the NeonCheckboxField component when you need to:

- Allow users to select multiple options from a list of choices
- Present a list of related, non-mutually exclusive options
- Create toggleable settings or feature selections
- Implement multi-select functionality within forms
- Create hierarchical selection interfaces with parent-child relationships
- Allow users to enable/disable multiple features or options
- Create selection lists with additional helper text for each option
- Implement toggle switches for multiple related settings

NeonCheckboxField is ideal when users need to select any number of options from a group (including none, one, or many). For single selection from a list of options, use NeonRadioField instead. For a single checkbox option, use NeonCheckboxSingle.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the checkbox field |
| dataLabelText | string | Yes | - | Label text for the field |
| options | Array<CheckboxOption> | Yes | - | Array of checkbox options to display |
| modelValue | Array<string> \| undefined | Yes | - | Array of selected option names |
| modelValueChange | function | Yes | - | Handler for value changes: (value: Array<string> \| undefined) => void |
| dataShowLabel | boolean | No | true | Whether to show the label |
| dataAriaLabel | string | No | - | Accessibility label for screen readers |
| dataHelperText | string | No | - | Helper text displayed below the field |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Text to show in a tooltip |
| dataIsRequired | boolean | No | false | Whether at least one option must be selected |
| dataHideRequiredBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to hide the required indicator |
| dataShowOptionalBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to show an optional indicator |
| dataControlLayout | string | No | 'column' | Layout direction of options. Options: 'column', 'row' |
| dataParentCheckboxBehavior | string | No | 'select-all' | Behavior for parent checkboxes. Options: 'select-all', 'disable-all' |
| dataIsReadOnly | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is read-only |
| dataSuccessMessage | string | No | - | Message to display when validation succeeds |
| dataLabelTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Whether to add space for label text alignment |
| dataHelperTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Whether to add space for helper text alignment |
| dataConstrainDescription | boolean | No | false | Whether to constrain description width to match the field |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is disabled |
| customValidationFunction | function | No | - | Custom validation function |
| onBlur | function | No | - | Handler for blur events |
| blurInterceptor | function | No | - | Function called before blur processing |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |

## CheckboxOption Interface

| Property | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|----------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the checkbox option |
| labelText | string | Yes | - | Text label for the option |
| name | string | Yes | - | Value that appears in the modelValue array when selected |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Whether this option is disabled |
| helperText | string | No | - | Additional text displayed below the option |
| checkType | string | No | 'check' | Type of control. Options: 'check', 'toggle' |
| isIndented | boolean | No | false | Whether this option appears indented |

## Examples

Basic checkbox group:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonCheckboxField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

function CheckboxFieldExample() {
  const [selectedPlanets, setSelectedPlanets] = useState(['planet-1', 'planet-3']);
  
  const planets = [
    {
      id: 'mars',
      labelText: 'Mars',
      name: 'planet-1'
    },
    {
      id: 'earth',
      labelText: 'Earth',
      name: 'planet-2'
    },
    {
      id: 'venus',
      labelText: 'Venus',
      name: 'planet-3'
    }
  ];
  
  return (
    <NeonCheckboxField
      id="planet-checkbox-list"
      dataLabelText="Select Planets"
      options={planets}
      modelValue={selectedPlanets}
      modelValueChange={setSelectedPlanets}
    />
  );
}
```

Checkbox group with toggle style:
```jsx
<NeonCheckboxField
  id="feature-toggles"
  dataLabelText="Features"
  dataHelperText="Select the features to enable"
  options={[
    {
      id: 'dark-mode',
      labelText: 'Dark Mode',
      name: 'feature-1',
      checkType: 'toggle',
      helperText: 'Enable dark color scheme'
    },
    {
      id: 'notifications',
      labelText: 'Notifications',
      name: 'feature-2',
      checkType: 'toggle',
      helperText: 'Receive notifications about updates'
    },
    {
      id: 'auto-save',
      labelText: 'Auto Save',
      name: 'feature-3',
      checkType: 'toggle',
      helperText: 'Automatically save changes'
    }
  ]}
  modelValue={enabledFeatures}
  modelValueChange={setEnabledFeatures}
/>
```

Checkbox group with row layout:
```jsx
<NeonCheckboxField
  id="categories"
  dataLabelText="Categories"
  dataControlLayout="row"
  options={[
    { id: 'cat1', labelText: 'News', name: 'news' },
    { id: 'cat2', labelText: 'Sports', name: 'sports' },
    { id: 'cat3', labelText: 'Entertainment', name: 'entertainment' }
  ]}
  modelValue={selectedCategories}
  modelValueChange={setSelectedCategories}
/>
```

Checkbox group with indented options:
```jsx
<NeonCheckboxField
  id="permissions"
  dataLabelText="Permissions"
  dataParentCheckboxBehavior="select-all"
  options={[
    { id: 'read', labelText: 'Read', name: 'read' },
    { id: 'write', labelText: 'Write', name: 'write' },
    { id: 'delete', labelText: 'Delete', name: 'delete' },
    { id: 'admin', labelText: 'Admin', name: 'admin' },
    { id: 'admin-users', labelText: 'Manage Users', name: 'admin-users', isIndented: true },
    { id: 'admin-groups', labelText: 'Manage Groups', name: 'admin-groups', isIndented: true },
    { id: 'admin-settings', labelText: 'Configure Settings', name: 'admin-settings', isIndented: true }
  ]}
  modelValue={selectedPermissions}
  modelValueChange={setSelectedPermissions}
  dataIsRequired={true}
/>
```

Required checkbox field with disabled options:
```jsx

  id="terms"
  dataLabelText="Terms and Conditions"
  dataIsRequired={true}
  options={[
    { id: 'required-terms', labelText: 'I accept the Terms of Service', name: 'terms' },
    { id: 'newsletter', labelText: 'Subscribe to newsletter', name: 'newsletter' },
    { id: 'beta', labelText: 'Join beta program', name: 'beta', disabled: true, helperText: 'Currently not available' }
  ]}
  modelValue={acceptedTerms}
  modelValueChange={setAcceptedTerms}
  dataHelperText="You must accept the Terms of Service to continue"
/>
```


# NeonCheckboxSingle

A versatile standalone checkbox component that supports multiple display styles, states, and customization options.

## When To Use

Use the NeonCheckboxSingle component when you need to:

- Allow users to make a binary choice (yes/no, true/false)
- Create a standalone checkbox control for a single option
- Implement a toggle switch for enabling/disabling a feature
- Display a checkbox in an indeterminate state (partially selected)
- Create customized checkbox controls with special icons
- Display a checkbox that needs to be larger and more prominent
- Create a standalone clickable icon that behaves like a checkbox
- Add a checkbox to a form with consistent styling and behavior
- Create an accessible checkbox control with proper labeling

NeonCheckboxSingle is intended for individual checkbox controls. For multiple related checkboxes, consider using NeonCheckboxField instead.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the checkbox |
| dataLabelText | string | Yes | - | The text label for the checkbox |
| name | string | No | - | The name attribute for the underlying input element |
| value | boolean \| 'indeterminate' \| 'true' \| 'false' | No | - | Controls the checkbox state (checked, unchecked, or indeterminate) |
| dataSize | 'small' \| 'medium' \| 'large' \| 'x-large' \| 'auto' | No | 'auto' | Sets the width of the label |
| dataShowLabel | boolean | No | true | When set to false, will hide the label text visually (still accessible to screen readers) |
| dataLabelTextSpace | boolean | No | false | When true, adds larger space to the top of the checkbox |
| dataHelperTextSpace | boolean | No | false | When true, adds space to the top of the checkbox |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | When true, disables the checkbox (it remains visible but non-interactive) |
| dataHelperText | string | No | - | Additional text displayed under the checkbox for context |
| dataCheckType | 'check' \| 'toggle' | No | 'check' | Changes the appearance of the checkbox between standard and toggle-switch style |
| dataIsIndented | boolean | No | false | When true, indents the checkbox field |
| onInput | (event: Event) => void | No | - | Function called when checkbox state changes |
| dataIconChecked | string | No | - | Custom icon to use when the checkbox is checked |
| dataIconUnchecked | string | No | - | Custom icon to use when the checkbox is unchecked |
| dataIconIndeterminate | string | No | - | Custom icon to use when the checkbox is in indeterminate state |
| dataIconColor | string | No | 'navy' | Color for the custom icons (options: 'navy', 'purple', 'magenta', 'red', 'orange', 'yellow', 'green', 'teal', 'cyan', 'gray') |
| dataStandAlone | boolean | No | false | When true, makes the icon larger and hides the label text |
| dataIsReadOnly | boolean | No | false | When true, makes the checkbox non-interactive but still displays its state |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Text for tooltip when hovering (only works when label is hidden or in stand-alone mode) |

## Examples

Simple checkbox with indeterminate state:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonCheckboxSingle } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CheckboxSingleExampleSimple() {
  const [isChecked, setIsChecked] = useState('indeterminate');

  return (
    <NeonCheckboxSingle
      id="__mfe__single-checkbox"
      dataLabelText="Single Checkbox"
      value={isChecked}
      onInput={(event) => {
        const value = event.target.getValue();
        console.log('Setting isChecked to ' + value);
        setIsChecked(value);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Checkbox with helper text:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonCheckboxSingle } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CheckboxSingleExampleWithHelperText() {
  return (
    <NeonCheckboxSingle
      id="checkbox-with-helper"
      dataLabelText="Accept terms and conditions"
      dataHelperText="Please read the terms before accepting"
      value={false}
    />
  );
}
```

Toggle-style checkbox:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonCheckboxSingle } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CheckboxSingleExampleToggle() {
  const [isEnabled, setIsEnabled] = useState(false);

  return (
    <NeonCheckboxSingle
      id="toggle-example"
      dataLabelText="Enable feature"
      dataCheckType="toggle"
      value={isEnabled}
      onInput={(event) => {
        setIsEnabled(event.target.getValue());
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Custom icon checkbox:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonCheckboxSingle } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CheckboxSingleExampleCustomIcon() {
  const [isFavorite, setIsFavorite] = useState(false);

  return (
    <NeonCheckboxSingle
      id="favorite-checkbox"
      dataLabelText="Mark as favorite"
      dataIconUnchecked="heart-outline"
      dataIconChecked="heart-solid"
      dataIconColor="red"
      value={isFavorite}
      onInput={(event) => {
        setIsFavorite(event.target.getValue());
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Standalone checkbox icon:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonCheckboxSingle } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CheckboxSingleExampleStandalone() {
  const [isStarred, setIsStarred] = useState(false);

  return (
    <NeonCheckboxSingle
      id="star-checkbox"
      dataLabelText="Star this item"
      dataStandAlone="true"
      dataShowLabel="false"
      dataTooltipText="Star this item"
      dataIconUnchecked="star-outline"
      dataIconChecked="star-solid"
      dataIconColor="yellow"
      value={isStarred}
      onInput={(event) => {
        setIsStarred(event.target.getValue());
      }}
    />
  );
}
```


# NeonChipMultiSelectField

A form field component that allows users to select multiple options from a set of choices, displaying each selection as a chip (tag).

## When To Use

Use the NeonChipMultiSelectField component when you need to:

- Allow users to select multiple options from a predefined list
- Display selected options as interactive chips/tags that can be toggled on and off
- Present a more visual and space-efficient alternative to standard checkboxes
- Show selected options in a compact, scannable format
- Allow users to quickly toggle selections with minimal clicks
- Provide a visually engaging multi-selection interface
- Create a form field that clearly indicates multiple selections are allowed
- Present options in a horizontal layout that can wrap to new lines when space is limited
- Support selection of multiple items from categories, tags, filters, or attributes

NeonChipMultiSelectField is ideal for scenarios where you need a more visually appealing and compact alternative to checkbox lists or multi-select dropdowns. It's especially useful when the selected items benefit from being immediately visible and interactive.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the field |
| modelValue | Array<string> \| undefined | Yes | - | Array of selected option values |
| modelValueChange | function | Yes | - | Callback function when selected options change |
| options | Array<ChipSelectOption> | Yes | - | Array of available options to display |
| dataLabelText | string | Yes | - | Label text for the field |
| dataShowLabel | boolean | No | true | Whether to show the label |
| dataIsRequired | boolean | No | false | Indicates if the field is required |
| dataHideRequiredBadge | boolean | No | false | Hides the required badge even when required |
| dataShowOptionalBadge | boolean | No | false | Shows an optional badge when field is not required |
| dataHelperText | string | No | - | Helper text displayed below the field |
| dataIsReadOnly | boolean | No | false | Makes the field read-only |
| dataMaxSelections | number | No | - | Maximum number of options that can be selected |
| dataLayout | string | No | - | Layout mode, use 'always-wrap' to force chips to wrap |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Disables the field |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Text to display in tooltip |
| dataAriaLabel | string | No | - | ARIA label for accessibility |
| dataSuccessMessage | string | No | - | Success message to display when field is valid |
| customValidationFunction | function | No | - | Custom validation function |
| blurInterceptor | function | No | - | Function called before blur behavior |
| onBlur | function | No | - | Function called when field loses focus |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |

## Examples

Basic usage with a list of options:
```jsx
import React, { useState, useMemo } from 'react';
import { NeonChipMultiSelectField } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { CheckboxOption } from '@neon/interfaces';

export function ChipMultiSelectFieldBasicExample() {
  const cars = useMemo<Array<CheckboxOption>>(() => {
    return [{
      id: 'car-option-1',
      labelText: 'Nexon',
      name: 'nexon',
    }, {
      id: 'car-option-2',
      labelText: 'Punch',
      name: 'punch',
    }, {
      id: 'car-option-3',
      labelText: 'Harrier',
      name: 'harrier',
    }, {
      id: 'car-option-4',
      labelText: 'Safari',
      name: 'safari',
    }];
  }, []);

  const [selectedCars, setSelectedCars] = useState<Array<string> | undefined>(['harrier']);

  return (
    <NeonChipMultiSelectField
      id="basic-car-selection"
      modelValue={selectedCars}
      modelValueChange={(cars: Array<string> | undefined): void => { setSelectedCars(cars); }}
      options={cars}
      dataLabelText="Select Cars"
    />
  );
}
```

With disabled options and maximum selections:
```jsx
import React, { useState, useMemo } from 'react';
import { NeonChipMultiSelectField } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { CheckboxOption } from '@neon/interfaces';

export function ChipMultiSelectFieldAdvancedExample() {
  const planets = useMemo<Array<CheckboxOption>>(() => {
    return [{
      id: 'planet-option-1',
      labelText: 'Mercury',
      name: 'mercury',
    }, {
      id: 'planet-option-2',
      labelText: 'Venus',
      name: 'venus',
    }, {
      id: 'planet-option-3',
      labelText: 'Earth',
      name: 'earth',
      dataTooltipText: 'Your home planet'
    }, {
      id: 'planet-option-4',
      labelText: 'Mars',
      name: 'mars',
    }, {
      id: 'planet-option-5',
      labelText: 'Jupiter',
      name: 'jupiter',
      disabled: true,
    }];
  }, []);

  const [selectedPlanets, setSelectedPlanets] = useState<Array<string> | undefined>(['earth']);

  return (
    <NeonChipMultiSelectField
      id="planet-selection"
      modelValue={selectedPlanets}
      modelValueChange={(planets: Array<string> | undefined): void => { setSelectedPlanets(planets); }}
      options={planets}
      dataLabelText="Select Planets"
      dataHelperText="You can select up to 3 planets"
      dataMaxSelections={3}
      dataIsRequired={true}
    />
  );
}
```

With always-wrap layout:
```jsx
import React, { useState, useMemo } from 'react';
import { NeonChipMultiSelectField } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { CheckboxOption } from '@neon/interfaces';

export function ChipMultiSelectFieldWrappingExample() {
  const colors = useMemo<Array<CheckboxOption>>(() => {
    return [{
      id: 'color-option-1',
      labelText: 'Red',
      name: 'red',
    }, {
      id: 'color-option-2',
      labelText: 'Orange',
      name: 'orange',
    }, {
      id: 'color-option-3',
      labelText: 'Yellow',
      name: 'yellow',
    }, {
      id: 'color-option-4',
      labelText: 'Green',
      name: 'green',
    }, {
      id: 'color-option-5',
      labelText: 'Blue',
      name: 'blue',
    }, {
      id: 'color-option-6',
      labelText: 'Indigo',
      name: 'indigo',
    }, {
      id: 'color-option-7',
      labelText: 'Violet',
      name: 'violet',
    }];
  }, []);

  const [selectedColors, setSelectedColors] = useState<Array<string> | undefined>([]);

  return (
    <NeonChipMultiSelectField
      id="color-selection"
      modelValue={selectedColors}
      modelValueChange={(colors: Array<string> | undefined): void => { setSelectedColors(colors); }}
      options={colors}
      dataLabelText="Select Colors"
      dataLayout="always-wrap"
    />
  );
}
```




# NeonChipSelectField

A component that displays selectable options as interactive chips with dropdown functionality, allowing users to make a single selection from a group of choices.

## When To Use

Use the NeonChipSelectField component when you need to:

- Present a set of options as interactive chips that users can select from
- Allow users to choose a single option from multiple choices
- Display selectable options in a compact, visual format
- Provide selection functionality in a space-efficient manner
- Create a more engaging selection interface than standard radio buttons or dropdown menus
- Show options that benefit from visual recognition and selection
- Implement a modern, chip-based selection pattern in forms
- Conserve space while maintaining clear option visibility
- Present categorical options that work well with the chip visual metaphor

NeonChipSelectField is particularly effective when the options are relatively short labels that can fit well within chips, and when you want to make all options visible at once rather than hidden in a dropdown.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the field |
| modelValue | string \| undefined | Yes | - | The currently selected value |
| modelValueChange | (value: string \| undefined) => void | Yes | - | Callback function called when selection changes |
| options | Array<ChipSelectOption> | Yes | - | Array of options to display as selectable chips |
| dataLabelText | string | Yes | - | Label text for the field |
| dataShowLabel | boolean | No | true | Whether to show the label |
| dataAriaLabel | string | No | - | Accessible label for screen readers |
| dataHelperText | string | No | - | Additional helper text displayed below the field |
| dataIsRequired | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is required |
| dataHideRequiredBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to hide the required badge |
| dataShowOptionalBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to show an optional badge |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Text for tooltip that appears on hover |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is disabled |
| dataSuccessMessage | string | No | - | Success message to display when validation passes |
| dataIsReadOnly | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is read-only |
| dataLayout | 'always-wrap' | No | - | When set to 'always-wrap', the chips will wrap regardless of the break point |
| customValidationFunction | ValidationFunction | No | - | Custom function for validation |
| blurInterceptor | (widgetElement: any) => void | No | - | Function called before blur events |
| onBlur | (e: Event) => void | No | - | Function called when field loses focus |

## ChipSelectOption Interface

| Property | Type | Required | Description |
|----------|------|----------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | Unique identifier for the option |
| labelText | string | Yes | The text label displayed on the chip |
| name | string | Yes | The value that will be in modelValue when selected |
| disabled | boolean | No | Whether this specific option is disabled |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | Tooltip text for this specific chip |
| dataTooltipPlacement | string | No | Tooltip placement position |

## Examples

Simple example with a list of cars:
```jsx
import React, { useState, useMemo } from 'react';
import { NeonChipSelectField } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { CheckboxOption } from '@neon/interfaces';

export function NeonChipSelectFieldExampleSimple() {
  const cars = useMemo(() => [
    {
      id: '__mfe__num-1111',
      labelText: 'Nexon',
      name: 'nexon',
    }, {
      id: '__mfe__num-2222',
      labelText: 'Punch',
      name: 'punch',
    }, {
      id: '__mfe__num-3333',
      labelText: 'Harrier',
      name: 'harrier',
    }, {
      id: '__mfe__num-1112',
      labelText: 'Safari',
      name: 'safari',
    }, {
      id: '__mfe__num-2221',
      labelText: 'Ertiga',
      name: 'ertiga',
      disabled: true,
    }, {
      id: '__mfe__num-3331',
      labelText: 'Brezza',
      name: 'brezza',
    }
  ], []);
  
  const [selectedCar, setSelectedCar] = useState('harrier');
  
  return (
    <NeonChipSelectField 
      id="unique-id-here"
      modelValue={selectedCar}
      modelValueChange={(car) => { setSelectedCar(car); }}
      options={cars} 
      dataLabelText="Cars" 
    />
  );
}
```

With helper text and required field:
```jsx
import React, { useState, useMemo } from 'react';
import { NeonChipSelectField } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { ChipSelectOption } from '@neon/interfaces';

export function ChipSelectFieldWithHelperText() {
  const planets = useMemo(() => [
    {
      id: 'planet-1',
      labelText: 'Mars',
      name: 'mars',
    }, {
      id: 'planet-2',
      labelText: 'Earth',
      name: 'earth',
      dataTooltipText: 'Earth is the third planet from the Sun'
    }, {
      id: 'planet-3',
      labelText: 'Venus',
      name: 'venus',
      dataTooltipText: 'Venus is the second planet from the Sun',
      dataTooltipPlacement: 'bottom'
    }
  ], []);
  
  const [selectedPlanet, setSelectedPlanet] = useState('earth');
  
  return (
    <NeonChipSelectField 
      id="planet-selector"
      modelValue={selectedPlanet}
      modelValueChange={setSelectedPlanet}
      options={planets} 
      dataLabelText="Select a Planet"
      dataHelperText="Please select your favorite planet"
      dataIsRequired="true"
    />
  );
}
```

With custom layout and disabled state:
```jsx
import React, { useState, useMemo } from 'react';
import { NeonChipSelectField } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { ChipSelectOption } from '@neon/interfaces';

export function ChipSelectFieldCustomLayout() {
  const colors = useMemo(() => [
    {
      id: 'color-1',
      labelText: 'Red',
      name: 'red',
    }, {
      id: 'color-2',
      labelText: 'Green',
      name: 'green',
    }, {
      id: 'color-3',
      labelText: 'Blue',
      name: 'blue',
    }, {
      id: 'color-4',
      labelText: 'Yellow',
      name: 'yellow',
    }, {
      id: 'color-5',
      labelText: 'Purple',
      name: 'purple',
    }
  ], []);
  
  const [selectedColor, setSelectedColor] = useState('blue');
  
  return (
    <NeonChipSelectField 
      id="color-picker"
      modelValue={selectedColor}
      modelValueChange={setSelectedColor}
      options={colors} 
      dataLabelText="Choose Color"
      dataLayout="always-wrap"
      disabled="true"
    />
  );
}
```




# NeonChipSelectSingle

A toggleable chip component that displays as a selectable, contained element with an optional icon and label text. It provides a visually distinct way to make boolean selections.

## When To Use

Use the NeonChipSelectSingle component when you need to:

- Create a visually distinct toggle control that appears as a chip/pill
- Provide a checkbox-like functionality with a more prominent visual treatment
- Allow users to select/deselect a single option
- Present a compact, contained selection control with clear visual feedback
- Show selection state with a more engaging visual treatment than a standard checkbox
- Create space-efficient toggle controls that don't require traditional checkbox styling
- Implement selections that benefit from the chip/pill visual metaphor
- Display toggles with custom icons or indicators

NeonChipSelectSingle acts as a specialized selection control that combines checkbox functionality with a chip/pill visual appearance. It's particularly useful when you need a more visually prominent selection mechanism that provides clear state indication in a compact format.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the chip select |
| dataLabelText | string | Yes | - | Text label displayed on the chip |
| name | string | No | - | Name attribute for the underlying input element |
| value | boolean \| 'true' \| 'false' \| 'indeterminate' | No | false | Current state of the chip (selected/unselected) |
| dataSize | string | No | 'auto' | Width of the chip. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'x-large', 'auto' |
| dataShowLabel | boolean | No | true | Whether to display the label text |
| dataLabelTextSpace | boolean | No | false | When true, adds larger spacing above the chip |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | When true, disables the chip but keeps it visible |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Text to display in tooltip when hovering |
| dataTooltipPlacement | string | No | 'top' | Position of the tooltip. Options: 'top', 'top-start', 'top-end', 'right', 'right-start', 'right-end', 'bottom', 'bottom-start', 'bottom-end', 'left', 'left-start', 'left-end' |
| dataUncheckedIcon | string | No | 'status-inactive' | The icon to display when chip is unchecked |
| dataUseUncheckedIcon | boolean | No | true | Whether to display an icon in the unchecked state |
| onInput | function | No | - | Event handler for input changes |

## Events

| Name | Description | Return Value |
|------|-------------|-------------|
| input | Fired when the chip state changes | Event object with target.getValue() method returning boolean |

## Examples

Simple chip select single:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonChipSelectSingle } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ChipSelectSingleExampleSimple() {
  const [isChecked, setIsChecked] = useState<boolean>(true);

  return (
    <NeonChipSelectSingle
      id="simple-chip-select"
      dataLabelText="Single Select Chip"
      value={isChecked}
      onInput={(event) => {
        const value = event.target.getValue();
        setIsChecked(value);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Chip select with tooltip and custom icon:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonChipSelectSingle } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ChipSelectSingleExampleWithTooltip() {
  const [isChecked, setIsChecked] = useState<boolean>(false);

  return (
    <NeonChipSelectSingle
      id="tooltip-chip-select"
      dataLabelText="Add Item"
      dataTooltipText="Click to add a new item"
      dataTooltipPlacement="bottom"
      dataUncheckedIcon="add"
      value={isChecked}
      onInput={(event) => {
        const value = event.target.getValue();
        setIsChecked(value);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Disabled chip select:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonChipSelectSingle } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ChipSelectSingleExampleDisabled() {
  return (
    <NeonChipSelectSingle
      id="disabled-chip-select"
      dataLabelText="Unavailable Option"
      disabled={true}
      value={false}
    />
  );
}
```

Different sizes for chip select:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonChipSelectSingle } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ChipSelectSingleExampleSizes() {
  const [isCheckedSmall, setIsCheckedSmall] = useState<boolean>(false);
  const [isCheckedMedium, setIsCheckedMedium] = useState<boolean>(true);
  const [isCheckedLarge, setIsCheckedLarge] = useState<boolean>(false);
  
  return (
    <>
      <NeonChipSelectSingle
        id="small-chip-select"
        dataLabelText="Small Chip"
        dataSize="small"
        value={isCheckedSmall}
        onInput={(event) => setIsCheckedSmall(event.target.getValue())}
      />
      
      <NeonChipSelectSingle
        id="medium-chip-select"
        dataLabelText="Medium Chip"
        dataSize="medium"
        value={isCheckedMedium}
        onInput={(event) => setIsCheckedMedium(event.target.getValue())}
      />
      
      <NeonChipSelectSingle
        id="large-chip-select"
        dataLabelText="Large Chip"
        dataSize="large"
        value={isCheckedLarge}
        onInput={(event) => setIsCheckedLarge(event.target.getValue())}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Accessibility

The NeonChipSelectSingle component:

- Uses a native checkbox input element for accessibility, ensuring keyboard navigation and screen reader support
- Maintains focus states with appropriate visual indicators (box-shadow on focus)
- Provides properly associated labels for screen readers
- Offers tooltip support for additional information
- Includes proper ARIA attributes via the underlying checkbox input
- Supports disabled states with appropriate visual and interaction behaviors
- Has specific mobile optimizations for touch targets and visual sizes

## Related Components

- **NeonChipSelectField**: For selecting a single option from multiple chip choices
- **NeonChipMultiSelectField**: For selecting multiple options using chips
- **NeonChipSet**: For displaying a collection of chip elements
- **NeonCheckboxSingle**: For a traditional checkbox selection when the chip appearance isn't needed
- **NeonRadioSingle**: For mutually exclusive selections in traditional radio button style


# NeonChipSet

A component for displaying and managing a collection of chips, handling overflow and clear-all functionality.

## When To Use

Use the NeonChipSet component when you need to:

- Display a collection of related items as compact, interactive chips
- Allow users to view and remove selected items or filters
- Manage multiple selections in limited space with automatic overflow handling
- Show selected options from multi-select fields
- Present filter selections or tags with the ability to remove individual items
- Create token-based input interfaces with removable elements
- Display multiple selected items in a compact, scannable format
- Provide users with the ability to clear all selections at once
- Represent complex hierarchical selections as simple, manageable tokens

NeonChipSet is designed to manage groups of chip elements efficiently, with smart overflow handling that automatically creates a menu for chips that don't fit in the available space. It's an excellent choice when you need to display multiple selections or filters in a limited space.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the chip set |
| chips | Array<Chip> | No | - | An array of Chips to display |
| dataDisableOverflowMenu | boolean | No | false | When true, chips will overflow naturally without creating an overflow menu |
| dataIsDisableOverflowMenu | boolean | No | false | Deprecated, use dataDisableOverflowMenu instead |
| dataIsEnableClearAll | boolean \| 'auto' | No | false | Specifies when the clear-all button should show up in the chip set |
| dataClearAllThreshold | number | No | 8 | When dataIsEnableClearAll is set to 'auto', the clear all button will show when the number of chips is >= the threshold |
| dataClearButtonText | string | No | 'clear all' | Text to display on the clear button |
| dataIsOnGray | boolean | No | false | Changes the chips to appear white when used on top of a gray background |
| dataIsReadOnly | boolean | No | false | Sets the chip set to a read only mode |
| dataSize | 'small' \| 'medium' | No | 'small' | Sets chip size |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Disables the chips interactions |
| dataModalType | 'auto' \| 'dialog' \| 'drawer' | No | 'auto' | Determines if overflow chips will be shown in a drawer or dialog |
| dataModalThreshold | number | No | 100 | When the number of overflow chips is >= the threshold, shows a modal instead of a popper |
| dataModalTitle | string | No | - | Title displayed in the overflow modal dialog or drawer |
| dataLabelText | string | No | - | When provided, this will put a label above the chip set |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| neonChipSetChipRemoved | (event: CustomEvent) => void | No | - | Called when a chip is removed, with event.detail.chipId containing the ID of the removed chip |
| neonChipSetChipAllChipsRemoved | (event: CustomEvent) => void | No | - | Called when all chips are removed via the clear button, with event.detail.chipIds containing an array of removed chip IDs |

## Examples

Basic chip set with multiple chips:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonChipSet } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { Chip } from '@neon/interfaces';

export function SimpleChipSetExample() {
  const chips = [
    {id: 'chocolate-001', dataText: 'Chocolate'},
    {id: 'cheese-002', dataText: 'Cheese'},
    {id: 'onion-003', dataText: 'Onion'},
    {id: 'blue-004', dataText: 'Blue Corn'}
  ];

  return (
    <NeonChipSet
      id="simple-chip-set"
      chips={chips}
      neonChipSetChipRemoved={(event) => {
        console.log(event.detail.chipId);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Chip set with clear all button:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonChipSet } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { Chip } from '@neon/interfaces';

export function ClearAllChipSetExample() {
  const chips = [
    {id: 'chocolate-001', dataText: 'Chocolate'},
    {id: 'cheese-002', dataText: 'Cheese'},
    {id: 'onion-003', dataText: 'Onion'},
    {id: 'blue-004', dataText: 'Blue Corn'},
    {id: 'sweet-005', dataText: 'Sweet Potato'},
    {id: 'garlic-006', dataText: 'Garlic'},
    {id: 'bbq-007', dataText: 'BBQ'},
    {id: 'ranch-008', dataText: 'Ranch'}
  ];

  return (
    <NeonChipSet
      id="clear-all-chip-set"
      chips={chips}
      dataIsEnableClearAll="true"
      dataClearButtonText="Clear Filter"
      neonChipSetChipAllChipsRemoved={(event) => {
        console.log('All chips removed', event.detail.chipIds);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Chip set with disabled overflow menu:

```jsx
      id: 'user-2',

      chips={chips}
    />
  );
```

# NeonChip

A compact, interactive component used to display discrete information, represent selected items, or trigger actions.

## When To Use

Use the NeonChip component when you need to:

- Display selected items or values in a compact format
- Create removable tags or labels
- Indicate the status of an item
- Display contact or user information with an avatar
- Create interactive filters or categories
- Present multiple discrete values in a limited space
- Show items that can be individually removed from a collection
- Represent selected options in multi-selection interfaces

NeonChip is ideal for representing discrete data points, selected values, or options in a compact, visually distinctive format. For multiple chips, consider using NeonChipSet to manage collections of chips.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the chip |
| dataText | string | Yes | - | Main text displayed on the chip |
| dataSubtext | string | No | - | Secondary text displayed on the chip |
| dataSize | 'small' \| 'medium' | No | 'small' | Sets the size of the chip |
| dataTooltip | string | No | - | Text to display in the tooltip when hovering over the chip |
| dataTooltipPosition | PopperPlacement | No | 'top' | Position of the tooltip relative to the chip |
| dataShowAvatar | boolean | No | false | Forces an avatar placeholder when all other avatar props are undefined |
| dataAvatarFirstName | string | No | - | First name for the avatar |
| dataAvatarLastName | string | No | - | Last name for the avatar |
| dataAvatarProfilePictureSrc | string | No | - | Image source URL for the avatar |
| dataAvatarBackgroundOption | string | No | - | Background style option for the avatar |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Disables all chip interactions |
| dataIsReadOnly | boolean | No | false | Sets the chip to read-only mode |
| dataIsOnGray | boolean | No | false | Changes the chip appearance to white when used on a gray background |
| children | Array<Chip> | No | - | An array of Chip children objects, displayed in a menu |

## Events

| Name | Detail | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| neonChipRemove | `{chipId: string}` | Fired when the remove button is clicked, with the chip ID in the event detail |

## Examples

Basic chip:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonChip } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ChipExampleBasic() {
  return (
    <NeonChip
      id="basic-chip"
      dataText="Hello World"
      neonChipRemove={(event) => {
        console.log('Chip removed', event.detail.chipId);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Chip with avatar:
```jsx
import React from 'react';

  return (
    <NeonChip
      id="avatar-chip"
      dataText="Cory Matthews"
      dataShowAvatar={true}
      dataAvatarFirstName="Cory"
      dataAvatarLastName="Matthews"
      dataAvatarProfilePictureSrc="/example-files/cory-matthews.jpg"
    />
  );
}
```

Chip with subtext:
```jsx

  return (
    <NeonChip
      id="subtext-chip"
      dataText="Project X"
      dataSubtext="In Progress"
      dataSize="medium"
    />
  );
}
```

```jsx

  return (
    <NeonChip
      id="tooltip-chip"
      dataText="Hover Me"
```

```jsx

  const items = ["One", "Two", "Three", "Four"];
```

# NeonDateField

A form field component for selecting and inputting dates with an accompanying calendar picker.

## When To Use

Use the NeonDateField component when you need to:

- Allow users to select a specific date from a calendar interface
- Collect date information in a standardized format
- Validate that user input conforms to date requirements
- Enforce date constraints such as min/max allowed dates
- Create form fields that require date selection
- Implement date input with a visual calendar picker
- Present date selection in a localized format

NeonDateField is ideal for forms requiring date selection with visual confirmation. It combines text input with a calendar UI to ensure accurate date selection. If you need to collect a date range instead of a single date, consider using NeonDateRangeField instead.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the date field |
| dataLabelText | string | Yes | - | Label text for the field |
| modelValue | string \| undefined | Yes | - | Current selected date value (ISO format) |
| modelValueChange | function | Yes | - | Handler for value changes: (value: string \| undefined) => void |
| dataShowLabel | boolean | No | true | Whether to show the label |
| dataPlaceholderText | string | No | - | Placeholder text when the field is empty |
| dataAriaLabel | string | No | - | Accessibility label for screen readers |
| dataHelperText | string | No | - | Helper text displayed below the field |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Text to show in a tooltip |
| dataSize | string | No | 'auto' | Width of the field. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'x-large', 'auto' |
| dataIsRequired | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is required |
| dataHideRequiredBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to hide the required indicator |
| dataShowOptionalBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to show an optional indicator |
| dataIsReadOnly | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is read-only |
| dataMinDate | string | No | - | Minimum allowed date (ISO format) |
| dataMaxDate | string | No | - | Maximum allowed date (ISO format) |
| dataDisabledDates | Array<string> | No | - | Array of specific dates to disable (ISO format) |
| dataCustomDateValidator | function | No | - | Custom function for date validation |
| dataFormat | string | No | 'MM/DD/YYYY' | Date format to display to the user |
| dataShowTodayButton | boolean | No | true | Whether to show a "Today" button on the calendar |
| dataShowClearButton | boolean | No | true | Whether to show a button to clear the selected date |
| dataSuccessMessage | string | No | - | Message to display when validation succeeds |
| dataLabelTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Whether to add space for label text alignment |
| dataHelperTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Whether to add space for helper text alignment |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is disabled |
| customValidationFunction | function | No | - | Custom validation function |
| onBlur | function | No | - | Handler for blur events |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |

## Examples

Basic date field:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonDateField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

function BasicDateFieldExample() {
  const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState();
  
  return (
    <NeonDateField
      id="birth-date"
      dataLabelText="Date of Birth"
      modelValue={selectedDate}
      modelValueChange={(value) => setSelectedDate(value)}
      dataPlaceholderText="MM/DD/YYYY"
    />
  );
}
```

Date field with min/max constraints:
```jsx
<NeonDateField
  id="appointment-date"
  dataLabelText="Appointment Date"
  dataIsRequired={true}
  dataMinDate="2023-06-01" // No dates before June 1, 2023
  dataMaxDate="2023-12-31" // No dates after December 31, 2023
  dataHelperText="Choose a date between June and December 2023"
  modelValue={appointmentDate}
  modelValueChange={setAppointmentDate}
  dataFormat="MM/DD/YYYY"
/>
```

Date field with disabled dates:
```jsx
<NeonDateField
  id="delivery-date"
  dataLabelText="Delivery Date"
  dataIsRequired={true}
  dataDisabledDates={['2023-07-04', '2023-12-25', '2023-01-01']} // Holidays when delivery is unavailable
  dataHelperText="Select a delivery date (holidays excluded)"
  modelValue={deliveryDate}
  modelValueChange={setDeliveryDate}
/>
```

Custom date format:
```jsx
<NeonDateField
  id="event-date"
  dataLabelText="Event Date"
  dataFormat="DD MMM YYYY" // Format as "25 Dec 2023"
  modelValue={eventDate}
  modelValueChange={setEventDate}
  dataHelperText="Date format: Day Month Year"
/>
```

Disabled date field:
```jsx
<NeonDateField
  id="contract-date"
  dataLabelText="Contract Signed Date"
  modelValue="2023-03-15"
  modelValueChange={() => {}} // No-op since field is disabled
  disabled={true}
  dataFormat="MM/DD/YYYY"
/>
```

Date field with custom validation:
```jsx
<NeonDateField
  id="future-date"
  dataLabelText="Future Planning Date"
  dataIsRequired={true}
  dataCustomDateValidator={(dateValue) => {
    // Only allow dates at least 30 days in the future
    const today = new Date();
    const selectedDate = new Date(dateValue);
    const thirtyDaysFromNow = new Date(today);
    thirtyDaysFromNow.setDate(today.getDate() + 30);
    
    if (selectedDate < thirtyDaysFromNow) {
      return { isValid: false, errorMessage: 'Date must be at least 30 days in the future' };
    }
    return { isValid: true };
  }}
  modelValue={planningDate}
  modelValueChange={setPlanningDate}
  dataHelperText="Select a date at least 30 days in the future"
/>
```




# NeonDatePicker

A versatile date picker component that allows users to select dates from a calendar interface with support for single date, multiple dates, or date range selection.

## When To Use

Use the NeonDatePicker component when you need to:

- Allow users to select a specific date from a calendar view
- Enable selection of multiple individual dates
- Allow users to select a date range with start and end dates
- Provide an intuitive calendar interface for date selection
- Validate dates against custom business rules
- Restrict date selection to specific ranges (min/max values)
- Allow selection of only weekdays
- Create interactive date selection interfaces within forms or dialogs
- Provide a consistent date selection experience across your application

NeonDatePicker is the core date selection component in the Neon Design System and offers flexible modes to handle different date selection requirements. Use it when you need a full calendar interface for date selection. For simpler date input with text fields, consider NeonDateField.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the date picker |
| dataMonth | number | No | current month | The month to display (0-11, where 0 is January) |
| dataYear | number | No | current year | The year to display (e.g. 2023) |
| dataMode | string | No | 'single' | Selection mode for the date picker. Options: 'single', 'multi', 'range' |
| singleModeValue | Date \| undefined | No | undefined | When in single mode, represents the selected date |
| rangeModeValue | DateRange | No | undefined | When in range mode, contains the start and end dates |
| multiModeValue | Array<Date> | No | undefined | When in multi mode, contains the array of selected dates |
| dataMinValue | string | No | - | Minimum selectable date in mm/dd/yyyy format |
| dataMaxValue | string | No | - | Maximum selectable date in mm/dd/yyyy format |
| dataWeekdaysOnly | string | No | - | When set to 'true', only weekdays are selectable |
| customValidationFunction | ValidationFunction | No | - | Custom function to validate selectable dates |
| neonDatePickerSingleDateChanged | (value: Date \| undefined) => void | No | - | Callback when a single date is selected |
| neonDatePickerMultiDatesChanged | (date: Array<Date>) => void | No | - | Callback when multiple dates selection changes |
| neonDatePickerDateRangeChanged | (DateRange: { start: Date, end: Date }) => void | No | - | Callback when date range selection changes |

## Examples

Single date selection:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonChip, NeonDatePicker } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { formatDate } from '@ps-refarch-ux/mfe-utils';

export function DatePickerSingleExample() {
  const [myDate, setMyDate] = useState();

  return (
    <>
      <NeonDatePicker
        id="date-picker-single"
        dataMonth={1}
        dataYear={2023}
        dataMode="single"
        singleModeValue={myDate}
        neonDatePickerSingleDateChanged={(date) => {
          setMyDate(date);
        }}
      />
      {myDate && (
        <NeonChip
          id="selected-date-chip"
          dataText={formatDate(myDate, 'DATE') || ''}
          neonChipRemove={() => {
            setMyDate(undefined);
          }}
        />
      )}
    </>
  );
}
```

Multiple date selection:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonChipSet, NeonDatePicker } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { formatDate } from '@ps-refarch-ux/mfe-utils';

export function DatePickerMultiExample() {
  const [myDates, setMyDates] = useState([]);

  return (
    <>
      <NeonDatePicker
        id="date-picker-multi"
        dataMonth={1}
        dataYear={2023}
        dataMode="multi"
        multiModeValue={myDates}
        neonDatePickerMultiDatesChanged={(dates) => {
          setMyDates(dates);
        }}
      />
      {myDates && myDates.length > 0 && (
        <NeonChipSet
          id="multi-selected-dates"
          chips={myDates.map((date, index) => ({
            id: `date-chip-${index}`,
            dataText: formatDate(date, 'DATE')
          }))}
          neonChipSetChipRemoved={(event) => {
            const selectedDates = [...myDates];
            const removeIndex = selectedDates.findIndex((_, index) => 
              `date-chip-${index}` === event.detail.chipId
            );
            selectedDates.splice(removeIndex, 1);
            setMyDates(selectedDates);
          }}
        />
      )}
    </>
  );
}
```

Date range selection:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonChip, NeonDatePicker } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { formatDate } from '@ps-refarch-ux/mfe-utils';

export function DatePickerRangeExample() {
  const [dateRange, setDateRange] = useState();

  return (
    <>
      <NeonDatePicker
        id="date-picker-range"
        dataMonth={1}
        dataYear={2023}
        dataMode="range"
        rangeModeValue={dateRange}
        neonDatePickerDateRangeChanged={(range) => {
          setDateRange(range);
        }}
      />
      {dateRange && dateRange.start && dateRange.end && (
        <>
          <NeonChip
            id="start-date-chip"
            dataText={formatDate(dateRange.start, 'DATE') || ''}
            neonChipRemove={() => {
              setDateRange(undefined);
            }}
          />
          <NeonChip
            id="end-date-chip"
            dataText={formatDate(dateRange.end, 'DATE') || ''}
            neonChipRemove={() => {
              setDateRange(undefined);
            }}
          />
        </>
      )}
    </>
  );
}
```

Date picker with custom validation:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonDatePicker } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function DatePickerCustomValidationExample() {
  const validationFunction = (value, condition, context) => {
    const date = context.parsedDate;
    
    const result = {
      isValid: date?.getDay() !== 1 // Disallow Mondays
    };
    
    if (!result.isValid) {
      result.errorMessage = 'Do not select Mondays';
    }
    
    return result;
  };

  return (
    <NeonDatePicker
      id="date-picker-custom-validate"
      customValidationFunction={validationFunction}
      dataMonth={5}
      dataYear={2024}
      dataMode="single"
    />
  );
}
```


# NeonDateRangeField

A form component that allows users to select a date range with start and end dates through a visual calendar interface.

## When To Use

Use the NeonDateRangeField component when you need to:

- Collect a range of dates from users (start date and end date)
- Allow users to select date ranges for reservations or bookings
- Create date filters with start and end parameters
- Define date ranges for reporting or analytics
- Set scheduling periods with clear start and end points
- Create event planning interfaces that require duration selection
- Implement date-based search functionality with range parameters
- Define term dates, enrollment periods, or any time-bounded activity
- Collect date ranges where the relationship between start and end dates is important
- Provide a user-friendly alternative to entering two separate dates manually

NeonDateRangeField is built on top of NeonDateField and NeonDatePicker components. It combines two date inputs with calendar pickers in a single, cohesive interface that ensures the start date logically precedes the end date.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the date range field |
| dataStartDateLabelText | string | No | "Start Date" | The label text for the start date field |
| dataEndDateLabelText | string | No | "End Date" | The label text for the end date field |
| dataYear | string | No | Current year | The initial year for the date picker |
| dataMonth | string | No | Current month | The initial month for the date picker (0-11) |
| dataMinValue | string | No | - | Format: mm/dd/yyyy. The minimum valid date this component will accept |
| dataMaxValue | string | No | - | Format: mm/dd/yyyy. The maximum valid date this component will accept |
| dataWeekdaysOnly | boolean | No | false | When true, Saturdays and Sundays will be invalid |
| dataStartDateAriaLabel | string | No | - | An aria-label for the start date field |
| dataEndDateAriaLabel | string | No | - | An aria-label for the end date field |
| dataStartDateAutocomplete | string | No | - | Autocomplete attribute for start date field |
| dataEndDateAutocomplete | string | No | - | Autocomplete attribute for end date field |
| dataStartDatePlaceholderText | string | No | - | Placeholder text for the start date field |
| dataEndDatePlaceholderText | string | No | - | Placeholder text for the end date field |
| dataIsRequired | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is required |
| dataHideRequiredBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to hide the required indicator |
| dataShowOptionalBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to show an optional indicator |
| dataShowLabel | boolean | No | true | Whether to show the field label |
| dataIsReadOnly | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is read-only |
| dataLabelTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Add extra top whitespace for use in neon form rows |
| dataHelperTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Add extra top whitespace for use in neon form rows |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is disabled |
| dataPopperPlacement | string | No | 'bottom-start' | Sets the popover position. Options: 'top-start', 'top-end', 'bottom-start', 'bottom-end' |
| customValidationFunction | function | No | - | Validates both start and end date fields. Invalid dates will be disabled in the picker |
| startDateCustomValidationFunction | function | No | - | Validates only the start date field |
| endDateCustomValidationFunction | function | No | - | Validates only the end date field |
| modelValue | DateRange | Yes | - | Object containing start and end dates |
| modelValueChange | function | Yes | - | Callback function when the date range changes |

## Examples

Basic date range field example:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonDateRangeField } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { type DateRange } from '@neon/interfaces';
import { formatDate } from '@ps-refarch-ux/mfe-utils';

export function DateRangeFieldExample() {
  const [modelValue, setModelValue] = useState<DateRange>();

  return (
    <>
      <NeonDateRangeField
        id="date-range-field"
        modelValue={modelValue}
        modelValueChange={(value: DateRange): void => {
          setModelValue(value);
        }}
      />

      {modelValue && (
        <dl className="__neon__text">
          <dt>Start Date</dt>
          <dd>{formatDate(modelValue.start, 'DATE_PRETTY')}</dd>
          <dt>End Date</dt>
          <dd>{formatDate(modelValue.end, 'DATE_PRETTY')}</dd>
        </dl>
      )}
    </>
  );
}
```

Custom label text example:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonDateRangeField } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { type DateRange } from '@neon/interfaces';

export function DateRangeFieldCustomLabelsExample() {
  const [modelValue, setModelValue] = useState<DateRange>();

  return (
    <NeonDateRangeField
      id="date-range-field-custom-labels"
      dataStartDateLabelText="Registration Opens"
      dataEndDateLabelText="Registration Closes"
      modelValue={modelValue}
      modelValueChange={(value: DateRange): void => {
        setModelValue(value);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Advanced date range field with validation:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonDateRangeField } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { type DateRange } from '@neon/interfaces';
import { type ValidationResult } from '@neon/interfaces/validation-engine';

export function DateRangeFieldAdvancedExample() {
  const [modelValue, setModelValue] = useState<DateRange>();

  // Custom validation to ensure no weekends can be selected
  const validateWeekdaysOnly = (value: string, condition: any, context: { [key: string]: any }): ValidationResult => {
    const vr: ValidationResult = {
      isValid: true
    };

    if (value && context && context.parsedDate) {
      const day = context.parsedDate.getDay();
      if (day === 0 || day === 6) { // 0 = Sunday, 6 = Saturday
        vr.isValid = false;
        vr.errorMessage = 'Weekend dates are not allowed';
      }
    }

    return vr;
  };

  return (
    <NeonDateRangeField
      id="date-range-field-advanced"
      dataStartDateLabelText="Course Start"
      dataEndDateLabelText="Course End"
      dataIsRequired={true}
      dataMinValue="01/01/2023"
      dataMaxValue="12/31/2025"
      customValidationFunction={validateWeekdaysOnly}
      modelValue={modelValue}
      modelValueChange={(value: DateRange): void => {
        setModelValue(value);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```


# NeonEllipsis

A component that truncates text with an ellipsis when it exceeds a specified number of lines, and displays the full text in a tooltip on hover.

## When To Use

Use the NeonEllipsis component when you need to:

- Display text that might overflow its container in a clean, controlled way
- Limit text to a specific number of lines with an ellipsis at the end when truncated
- Show the full text content in a tooltip when the user hovers over truncated text
- Maintain a consistent text layout when dealing with variable-length content
- Prevent text overflow from breaking your UI layout
- Present lengthy text content in a space-efficient manner
- Enhance readability in UI elements with limited space
- Implement responsive text behavior across different screen sizes

NeonEllipsis is an essential utility component for managing text overflow in the Neon Design System. It provides a clean solution for displaying content that might be too long for its container while still making the full content accessible via tooltip.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the component |
| children | React.ReactNode | Yes | - | Text content to display and potentially truncate |
| dataLineClamp | number | No | 1 | Number of lines to display before truncating text |
| dataPopperPlacement | string | No | 'top' | Tooltip placement relative to text ('top', 'right', 'bottom', 'left', etc.) |
| dataShowTooltip | boolean | No | true | Whether to show tooltip when text is truncated |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Custom text for tooltip, defaults to full text content if not provided |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |

## Examples

Basic usage with default settings:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonEllipsis } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function EllipsisExampleBasic() {
  return (
    <NeonEllipsis id="basic-ellipsis-example">
      This is a long text that will be truncated with an ellipsis if it exceeds the available space in a single line.
    </NeonEllipsis>
  );
}
```

Multi-line ellipsis with custom tooltip placement:
