```jsx
import { NeonEllipsis } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function EllipsisExampleMultiLine() {
  return (
    <NeonEllipsis
      id="multi-line-ellipsis-example"
      dataLineClamp={2}
      dataPopperPlacement="bottom"
    >
      Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text
      Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text
      Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text
      Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text
      Sample Text Sample Text Sample Text
    </NeonEllipsis>
  );
}
```

Ellipsis with custom tooltip text:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonEllipsis } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function EllipsisExampleCustomTooltip() {
  return (
    <NeonEllipsis
      id="custom-tooltip-ellipsis-example"
      dataTooltipText="This is a custom tooltip that displays instead of the full text content"
    >
      This text will be truncated if necessary, but the tooltip will show custom text instead of this content.
    </NeonEllipsis>
  );

```

Ellipsis with tooltip disabled:
```jsx

  return (
    <NeonEllipsis
      id="no-tooltip-ellipsis-example"
      dataShowTooltip={false}
      dataLineClamp={3}
    >
      The very best part of being a developer is that we get to write code every day and it is a lot of fun to do that.
      Every day I wake up and I am excited to go work at my job as a software engineer.
      This text will be truncated after 3 lines but will not show a tooltip on hover.
    </NeonEllipsis>
  );
}
```

# NeonErrorCardContent

A component for displaying error states and empty states with an illustration, message, and optional action buttons.

## When To Use

Use the NeonErrorCardContent component when you need to:

- Display errors in retrieving or processing data within a card or section
- Create user-friendly empty state messages with visual indicators
- Provide error feedback with options for users to retry or take other actions
- Show a standardized error presentation within your application
- Create consistent error states across different components and pages
- Present error messages with supporting illustrations for better user comprehension
- Implement empty state messaging for when content is not available
- Guide users with clear actions to resolve error conditions

NeonErrorCardContent is designed to be used both standalone and within container components like NeonCardStandard. It combines an illustration, error message, and action buttons to create a comprehensive error or empty state display.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | No | - | Unique identifier for the component |
| dataIllustration | string | No | 'paper-airplane' | The illustration to display. Options: 'add-document', 'folder', 'message', 'notebook', 'paper-airplane', 'people-search', 'search', 'tasks-complete' |
| dataErrorText | string | No | 'The information could not be found. Click Refresh to try again.' | The error text to display |
| children | React.ReactNode | No | - | Content to display inside the component, typically for the card-error-buttons slot |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| card-error-buttons | No | Container for action buttons with proper spacing and alignment |

## Examples

Simple error card with default settings and action buttons:

```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonErrorCardContent, NeonButton } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ErrorCardContentExampleSimple() {
  return (
    <NeonErrorCardContent>
      <div data-slot="card-error-buttons">
        <NeonButton
          id="refresh-button"
          dataText="Refresh"
          dataIcon="refresh"
          dataType="primary" />
        <NeonButton
          id="second-button"
          dataText="Button" />
      </div>
    </NeonErrorCardContent>
  );
}
```

Error card content within a card standard component with custom message and illustration:

```jsx

export function ErrorCardContentExampleCardStandard() {
  return (
    <NeonCardStandard
      dataHeading="My MFE">
      <div data-slot="card-actions">
        <NeonButton
          id="card-refresh-button"
          dataText="refresh"
          dataType="utility"
          dataIcon="refresh"
          dataTooltipText="Refresh" />
      </div>
      <div data-slot="body">
        <NeonErrorCardContent
          dataErrorText="Something went wrong. Please try again!"
          dataIllustration="search">
          <div data-slot="card-error-buttons">
            <NeonButton
              id="error-refresh-button"
              dataText="Refresh"
              dataIcon="refresh"
              dataType="primary" />
          </div>
        </NeonErrorCardContent>
      </div>
    </NeonCardStandard>
  );
}
```

# NeonErrorPageContent

A component for displaying error pages with consistent styling and customizable content for various HTTP error codes and custom error states.

## When To Use

Use the NeonErrorPageContent component when you need to:

- Display standardized error pages for common HTTP error codes (403, 404, 408, 500)
- Create custom error states with your own heading, subheading, and body content
- Provide users with clear information about an error that has occurred
- Include visual illustrations or custom media with error messages
- Add action buttons for users to retry operations or navigate elsewhere
- Present errors in a consistent, branded format across your application
- Ensure error messages are accessible and user-friendly

NeonErrorPageContent is part of the Neon Design System and provides predefined content for common error codes while allowing for complete customization when needed. Use it to display errors in a consistent, professional manner that aligns with your application's design language.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | No | - | Unique identifier for the error page content |
| dataHeading | string | No | - | Override the default error heading |
| dataSubheading | string | No | - | Override the default error subheading |
| dataBody | string | No | - | Override the default error body text |
| dataErrorCode | string | No | - | Sets predefined content specific to error code. Options: '403', '404', '408', '500' |
| dataShowErrorCode | boolean | No | true | Show or hide the "Your error code is:" message |
| children | React.ReactNode | No | - | Additional content or action buttons to display |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| error-page-content-media | No | Custom visual element or image to display with the error message |

## Examples

# NeonFilePicker

A component for uploading files with various display options, including a button interface and a drag-and-drop zone.

## When To Use

Use the NeonFilePicker component when you need to:

- Allow users to upload files to your application
- Provide a simple button interface for file selection
- Offer drag-and-drop functionality for easier file uploads
- Display a list of selected files with optional thumbnails
- Restrict uploads to specific file types or extensions
- Validate files based on custom requirements
- Create form fields that accept file uploads
- Display visual feedback for uploaded files
- Support both single and multiple file selection
- Create a user-friendly file upload experience

NeonFilePicker is the primary file upload component in the Neon Design System. It offers flexible configuration options for different upload scenarios and integrates with form validation systems.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the file picker |
| modelValue | FileList \| undefined | Yes | - | The files that have been selected |
| modelValueChange | (value: FileList \| undefined) => void | Yes | - | Callback when selected files change |
| dataLabelText | string | Yes | - | Label text for the file picker |
| dataShowLabel | BooleanAttribute | No | true | Whether to show the label |
| dataHelperText | string | No | - | Helper text displayed below the component |
| dataAriaLabel | string | No | - | Accessible label for screen readers |
| dataIsRequired | BooleanAttribute | No | false | Whether the field is required |
| dataShowSelectedFiles | BooleanAttribute | No | true | Shows/Hides the file name(s) |
| dataButtonText | string | No | 'Add File' | Text displayed on the select file button |
| dataDropZoneText | string | No | 'Drag and drop or click to add file' | Text displayed in the drop zone area |
| dataShowFileDropZone | BooleanAttribute | No | false | When true, displays a drop zone instead of just a button |
| dataShowImageThumbnails | BooleanAttribute | No | true | Shows thumbnails for image files |
| dataShowIcons | BooleanAttribute | No | true | Shows file type icons in the file list |
| multiple | BooleanAttribute | No | false | Allows multiple files to be selected |
| accept | string | No | - | File types that can be selected (e.g., ".jpg, .png" or "image/*") |
| disabled | BooleanAttribute | No | false | Whether the file picker is disabled |
| dataSuccessMessage | string | No | - | Message to display on successful validation |
| customValidationFunction | function | No | - | Custom validation function for files |
| onBlur | function | No | - | Function called when the file picker loses focus |

## Examples

Simple file picker:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonFilePicker } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function FilePickerExampleSimple() {
  const [fileList, setFileList] = useState();
  
  return (
    <NeonFilePicker
      id="simple-file-picker"
      dataLabelText="File Picker Example Simple"
      dataShowLabel="false"
      modelValue={fileList}
      modelValueChange={(file) => { setFileList(file); }}
    />
  );
}
```

File picker with drop zone:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonFilePicker } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function FilePickerExampleDropZone() {
  const [fileList, setFileList] = useState();
  
  return (
    <NeonFilePicker
      id="drop-zone-file-picker"
      dataLabelText="File picker example drop zone"
      dataShowLabel="false"
      dataShowFileDropZone="true"
      modelValue={fileList}
      modelValueChange={(file) => { setFileList(file); }}
    />
  );
}
```

File picker with extension filtering:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonFilePicker } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function FilePickerExampleAcceptExtensions() {
  const [fileList, setFileList] = useState();
  
  return (
    <NeonFilePicker
      id="file-picker-with-extensions"
      dataLabelText="Upload a .txt or .jpg file"
      dataHelperText=".jpeg files should also work"
      dataShowFileDropZone="true"
      accept=".txt, .jpg"
      modelValue={fileList}
      modelValueChange={(file) => { setFileList(file); }}
    />
  );
}
```

File picker with custom validation:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonFilePicker } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function FilePickerExampleCustomValidation() {
  const [fileList, setFileList] = useState();
  
  return (
    <NeonFilePicker
      id="custom-validation-file-picker"
      dataLabelText="File Picker with Custom Validation"
      dataShowLabel="false"
      modelValue={fileList}
      multiple="true"
      modelValueChange={(file) => { setFileList(file); }}
      customValidationFunction={(value, condition) => {
        if (value == null) {
          value = '';
        }
        const fileList = value.split(', ');
        
        if (fileList.find((fileName) => {
          return !/\.(jpg|jpeg)$/.test(fileName);
        }) != null) {
          return {
            isValid: false,
            errorMessage: 'Only .jpg or .jpeg files are valid'
          };
        } else {
          return {isValid: true};
        }
      }}
    />
  );
}
```




# NeonFloatingActionButton

A floating action button (FAB) component that provides a persistent, circular button typically used for primary or assistive actions, with optional expanding content panel.

## When To Use

Use the NeonFloatingActionButton component when you need to:

- Provide easy access to a key action across various screens
- Create a persistent chatbot or AI assistant interface
- Allow users to quickly access help or support functionality
- Implement a collapsible panel for information or interaction
- Display a notification indicator for new messages or updates
- Create a consistently positioned interactive element
- Provide an assistive interface component that remains accessible across different screens
- Implement a floating chat or feedback mechanism

NeonFloatingActionButton is designed to provide quick access to important functions while minimizing screen real estate usage. It's especially useful for AI assistants, support chats, or other features that should be persistently available but not intrusive.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the button |
| dataAriaLabel | string | Yes | - | Accessible label for the button |
| dataContentAriaLabel | string | Yes | - | Accessible label for the content panel |
| dataHasMessages | boolean | No | false | Whether the button should display a notification indicator |
| dataUseCloseIcon | boolean | No | true | Whether to use the default close icon when content is visible |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Text to display in a tooltip when hovering over the button |
| dataImgSrc | string | No | - | Custom image source URL for the button icon (defaults to PowerBuddy logo if not specified) |
| dataImgAlt | string | Yes | - | Alt text for the button icon (required for accessibility) |
| dataContentsVisible | boolean | No | false | Whether the content panel is visible |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Whether the button is disabled |
| children | React.ReactNode | No | - | Children elements for the content panel |
| neonFloatingActionButtonClick | function | No | - | Callback function when the button is clicked, receives contentsVisible state as parameter |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| floating-action-button-content | No | Content to display in the expanded panel when the button is clicked |
| floating-action-button-button-content | No | Custom content for the FAB button itself, replacing the default image |

## Events

| Name | Payload | Description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| neonFloatingActionButtonClick | { contentsVisible: boolean } | Fired when the button is clicked, includes current visibility state of the content panel |

## CSS Classes

The component automatically applies these CSS classes:

- `neon-floating-action-button` - Base class for the button
- `neon-floating-action-button-new-message-alert` - Applied when dataHasMessages is true and the user hasn't interacted with the button
- `neon-floating-action-button-has-chat-open` - Applied when the content panel is visible
- `neon-floating-action-button-content-container` - Container for the expanded content panel

## Container

For proper positioning and behavior, especially with modal dialogs, wrap the component in a container with the `__neon__floating-action-button-container` class. This container supports additional attributes:

- `data-move-up="true"` - Adjusts the position when a detail layout with footer is open
- `data-relative-to-modal="above|below"` - Controls whether the FAB appears above or below modal dialogs

## Examples

Basic floating action button:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonFloatingActionButton } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function FloatingActionButtonExample() {
  return (
    <NeonFloatingActionButton
      dataContentAriaLabel="Floating Action Button Content"
      dataAriaLabel="Launch PowerBuddy Chat"
      dataTooltipText="I'm here if you need any help"
      dataImgAlt="PowerSchool PowerBuddy Avatar"
      id="neon-fab-example"
    />
  );
}
```

FAB with notification indicator:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonFloatingActionButton } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function FloatingActionButtonWithMessages() {
  const [hasMessages, setHasMessages] = useState(true);
  
  return (
    <NeonFloatingActionButton
      id="neon-fab-has-messages"
      dataAriaLabel="Launch PowerBuddy Chat"
      dataHasMessages={hasMessages}
      dataImgAlt="PowerSchool PowerBuddy Avatar"
      dataContentAriaLabel="Floating Action Button Content"
    />
  );
}
```

FAB with custom button content:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonFloatingActionButton } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { CustomButtonIcon } from './CustomButtonIcon';

export function FloatingActionButtonCustomButton() {
  const [fabContentVisible, setFabContentVisible] = useState(false);
  
  return (
    <NeonFloatingActionButton
      dataAriaLabel="Custom FAB button"
      dataContentAriaLabel="Floating Action Button Content"
      dataTooltipText="Click for assistance"
      dataImgAlt=""
      id="neon-fab-custom-button"
      neonFloatingActionButtonClick={(state) => {
        setFabContentVisible(state);
      }}
    >
      <div data-slot="floating-action-button-button-content">
        <CustomButtonIcon isOpen={fabContentVisible} />
      </div>
    </NeonFloatingActionButton>
  );
}
```

Complete example with content and proper container:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonCardStandard, NeonFloatingActionButton } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function FloatingActionButtonComplete() {
  return (
    <div className="__neon__floating-action-button-container">
      <NeonFloatingActionButton
        dataContentAriaLabel="Floating Action Button Content"
        id="neon-fab-full-example"
        dataAriaLabel="Launch PowerBuddy Chat"
        dataTooltipText="I'm here if you need any help"
        dataImgAlt="PowerSchool PowerBuddy Avatar"
        neonFloatingActionButtonClick={(contentsVisible) => {
          console.log('FAB state changed:', contentsVisible);
        }}
      >
        <div data-slot="floating-action-button-content">
          <NeonCardStandard dataHeading="Help Assistant">
            <div data-slot="card-actions">
              <NeonButton
                data-neon-floating-action-button-close
                id="fab-close-button"
                dataText="Close"
                dataIcon="close"
                dataType="utility"
              />
            </div>
            <div data-slot="body" className="__neon__text">
              <p>This is the expanded content for the floating action button.</p>
              <p>Click the close button or the FAB again to dismiss.</p>
            </div>
          </NeonCardStandard>
        </div>
      </NeonFloatingActionButton>
    </div>
  );
}
```


# NeonFooter

A standard footer component that displays copyright information, navigation links, and optional address details.

## When To Use

Use the NeonFooter component when you need to:

- Display consistent footer information across your application
- Include standard legal links such as privacy policy and terms of service
- Show organizational address information
- Provide copyright attribution at the bottom of your pages
- Implement a standardized page footer that matches the Neon Design System
- Create a clear visual separation between page content and footer information
- Add required legal and policy links to comply with regulations
- Display contact information for an organization or institution

NeonFooter should be used at the bottom of your application pages to provide consistent footer information and navigation links. It's designed to be part of your overall page layout and works best when used with other Neon Design System components.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| footerInfo | FooterInfo | Yes | - | Object containing all footer information including addresses and navigation links |

### FooterInfo Interface

```typescript
interface FooterInfo {
  footerNav?: Array<{ name: string, url: string, id: string, isNewTab?: boolean }>;
  footerAddressTitle1?: string;
  footerAddressTitle2?: string;
  footerAddress1?: Array<{ addressLine: string, id: string }>;
  footerAddress2?: Array<{ addressLine: string, id: string }>;
}
```

## Examples

Basic footer with navigation links and two address sections:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonFooter } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { type FooterInfo } from '@neon/interfaces';

export function FooterExample() {
  const footerInfo: FooterInfo = {
    footerAddressTitle1: 'Bella Vista HS',
    footerAddress1: [{
      id: 'bvhs-address-line-1',
      addressLine: '8301 Madison Ave'
    }, {
      id: 'bvhs-address-line-2',
      addressLine: 'Fair Oaks, CA 95628'
    }],
    footerAddressTitle2: 'San Juan Unified',
    footerAddress2: [{
      id: 'sjusd-address-line-1',
      addressLine: '3738 Walnut Ave'
    }, {
      id: 'sjusd-address-line-2',
      addressLine: 'Carmichael, CA 95608'
    }],
    footerNav: [{
      name: 'Privacy Statement',
      url: 'http://www.example.com/privacy',
      id: 'privacy-statement',
      isNewTab: true
    }, {
      name: 'Terms of Use',
      url: 'http://www.example.com/terms',
      id: 'terms-of-use',
      isNewTab: true
    }, {
      name: 'Help Center',
      url: 'http://www.example.com/help',
      id: 'help-center',
      isNewTab: true
    }]
  };

  return <NeonFooter footerInfo={footerInfo} />;
}
```

Footer with single address and navigation links:

Dynamic footer with configurable elements:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonFooter, NeonCheckboxSingle, NeonSelectField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

function ConfigurableFooter() {
  const [showAddress1, setShowAddress1] = useState(true);
  const [showAddress2, setShowAddress2] = useState(true);
  const [numberOfLinks, setNumberOfLinks] = useState(2);
  
  const footerAddress1 = {
    footerAddressTitle1: 'Main Office',
    footerAddress1: [{
      id: 'office-address-line-1',
      addressLine: '1000 Main Street'
    }, {
      id: 'office-address-line-2',
      addressLine: 'Anytown, ST 12345'
    }]
  };
  
  const footerAddress2 = {
    footerAddressTitle2: 'Satellite Office',
    footerAddress2: [{
      id: 'satellite-address-line-1',
      addressLine: '500 Branch Avenue'
    }, {
      id: 'satellite-address-line-2',
      addressLine: 'Othertown, ST 67890'
    }]
  };
  
  const footerNav = [{
    name: 'Privacy',
    url: '/privacy',
    id: 'privacy',
    isNewTab: false
  }, {
    name: 'Terms',
    url: '/terms',
    id: 'terms',
    isNewTab: false
  }, {
    name: 'Support',
    url: '/support',
    id: 'support',
    isNewTab: false
  }];
  
  const footerInfo = {
    footerNav: footerNav.slice(0, numberOfLinks)
  };
  
  if (showAddress1) {
    footerInfo.footerAddressTitle1 = footerAddress1.footerAddressTitle1;
    footerInfo.footerAddress1 = footerAddress1.footerAddress1;
  }
  
  if (showAddress2) {
    footerInfo.footerAddressTitle2 = footerAddress2.footerAddressTitle2;
    footerInfo.footerAddress2 = footerAddress2.footerAddress2;
  }
  
  return (
    <div>
      <div className="__neon__form">
        <NeonCheckboxSingle
          id="show-address-1"
          dataLabelText="Show Address 1"
          value={showAddress1}
          onInput={(e) => setShowAddress1(e.target.getValue())}
        />
        <NeonCheckboxSingle
          id="show-address-2"
          dataLabelText="Show Address 2"
          value={showAddress2}
          onInput={(e) => setShowAddress2(e.target.getValue())}
        />
        <NeonSelectField
          id="number-of-links"
          dataLabelText="Number of Links"
          modelValue={String(numberOfLinks)}
          modelValueChange={(value) => setNumberOfLinks(Number(value))}
          options={[
            {text: '0', value: '0'},
            {text: '1', value: '1'},
            {text: '2', value: '2'},
            {text: '3', value: '3'}
          ]}
        />
      </div>
      
      <NeonFooter footerInfo={footerInfo} />
    </div>
  );
}
```


# NeonFullPageSkeleton

A loading state component that displays placeholder content while data is being fetched or processed, providing visual feedback to users during loading operations with various layout options.

## When To Use

Use the NeonFullPageSkeleton component when you need to:

- Indicate to users that content is loading without showing a blank screen
- Maintain user engagement during data fetching operations
- Provide a visual preview of the page structure before content loads
- Improve perceived performance by showing content placeholders
- Create a smooth transition between loading and loaded states
- Display appropriate loading states for different types of content layouts (tables, calendars, grades, assignments, etc.)
- Reduce user frustration during network delays
- Implement a consistent loading experience across your application

NeonFullPageSkeleton is designed to mimic the layout of various content types, showing placeholder elements that match the expected content structure. This helps users understand what kind of content to expect while waiting for actual data to load.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the component |
| dataType | string | No | 'table-tiles' | Determines the skeleton layout type to display |

### Available dataType values:

- `table-tiles`: Default option showing a tile-based table layout
- `assignments`: Shows a skeleton for assignment list layouts
- `attendance`: Displays a full attendance record layout skeleton
- `attendance-body`: Shows a partial attendance layout (body only)
- `accordion`: Renders an accordion-style skeleton with expandable sections
- `calendar`: Displays a calendar view with time slots and day headers
- `grades`: Shows an academic grades layout skeleton
- `table`: Renders a full tabular data layout skeleton

## Examples

Basic skeleton loader for a table:

```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonFullPageSkeleton } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function BasicSkeletonExample() {
  return (
    <NeonFullPageSkeleton id="table-skeleton" dataType="table" />
  );
}
```

Calendar skeleton loader:

```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonFullPageSkeleton } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CalendarSkeletonExample() {
  return (
    <NeonFullPageSkeleton id="calendar-skeleton" dataType="calendar" />
  );
}
```

Assignments skeleton loader:

```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonFullPageSkeleton } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AssignmentsSkeletonExample() {
  return (
    <NeonFullPageSkeleton id="assignments-skeleton" dataType="assignments" />
  );
}
```

Using skeleton loader in a loading state context:

```jsx
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
import { NeonFullPageSkeleton } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function LoadingStateExample() {
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true);
  const [data, setData] = useState(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    // Simulate data fetching
    const fetchData = async () => {
      try {
        // Replace with your actual data fetching logic
        await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 2000));
        setData({ /* your data here */ });
        setLoading(false);
      } catch (error) {
        console.error('Error fetching data:', error);
        setLoading(false);
      }
    };

    fetchData();
  }, []);

  return (
    <div className="__neon__layout">
      <div className="__neon__layout-scrollable">
        {loading ? (
          <NeonFullPageSkeleton id="grades-skeleton" dataType="grades" />
        ) : (
          <div>
            {/* Your actual content here */}
            {data && <p>Data loaded successfully!</p>}
          </div>
        )}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Using attendance body skeleton (partial skeleton):

```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonFullPageSkeleton } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AttendanceBodySkeletonExample() {
  return (
    <div>
      <h2>Attendance Records</h2>
      <NeonFullPageSkeleton id="attendance-body-skeleton" dataType="attendance-body" />
    </div>
  );
}
```


# NeonGradeBlock

A simple component for displaying grades or scores in a colored block with optional percentage value.

## When To Use

Use the NeonGradeBlock component when you need to:

- Display academic grades or scores in a visually consistent way
- Show performance metrics with both a letter grade and percentage
- Create visual indicators of status or performance levels
- Display grades in a compact, color-coded format
- Indicate assessment results in education or evaluation contexts
- Provide quick visual feedback on performance metrics

NeonGradeBlock is designed to display simple grade data with optional percentage values in a colored block. It's ideal for dashboards, report cards, assessment summaries, or anywhere you need to display grades or performance indicators visually.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | No | - | Unique identifier for the component |
| dataBackgroundColor | string | No | - | Background color of the block. Options include: yellow, orange, red, magenta, purple, cyan, navy, green, teal, gray |
| dataGrade | string | No | - | The grade or score text to display (appears in uppercase) |
| dataGradeBlockPercentage | number | No | - | Percentage value to display below the grade |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |

## Examples

Basic grade block:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonGradeBlock } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function GradeBlockExample() {
  return (
    <NeonGradeBlock
      id="grade-example"
      dataBackgroundColor="green"
      dataGrade="A"
    />
  );
}
```

Grade block with percentage:

# NeonIconCustom

A component for registering custom SVG icons that can be used with the Neon Icon system.

## When To Use

Use the NeonIconCustom component when you need to:

- Add custom SVG icons to your application that aren't available in the standard icon set
- Integrate product-specific or app-specific iconography into your application
- Use branded or specialized icons that follow your design system
- Create a custom icon library for use within your micro frontend
- Register SVG icons that can be referenced by NeonIcon and other Neon components
- Support Right-to-Left (RTL) language displays with custom icons
- Display SVG icons with complex paths or specific styling requirements
- Create namespaced icons to prevent collisions between different micro frontends

NeonIconCustom is a container component that registers SVG content with the Neon icon system. Once registered, these icons can be used by NeonIcon and other components by referencing them with the "|custom" suffix.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the icon. This will be the name of the icon used when referencing it. Must be namespaced (e.g., "__mfe__example-icon") |
| children | React.ReactNode | No | - | SVG content to be registered as a custom icon |

## Examples

Simple custom icon registration:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonIcon, NeonIconCustom } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function IconCustomExampleSimple() {
  return (
    <>
      {/* Register the custom SVGs once somewhere in your MFE */}
      <NeonIconCustom id="__mfe__schoology-external-tool">
        <svg viewBox="0 0 26 26" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" >
          <rect width="20" height="20" x="3" y="3" rx="2" fill="#0080A8" />
          <path d="M15.9635 9.01807L11.06399 9.01807C10.51167 9.018 10.06393 9.46574 10.064 10.01806C10.064 10.57031 10.51174 11.01805 11.06399 11.01805L13.5593 11.00801L9.35689 15.2104C8.96642 15.6009 8.96635 16.2341 9.35689 16.6247C9.74742 17.0152 10.38064 17.0151 10.7711 16.6247L14.9735 12.42222L14.9635 14.9176C14.9635 15.4698 15.4112 15.9175 15.9635 15.9175C16.5158 15.9176 16.9635 15.4699 16.9635 14.9176V10.01806C16.9635 9.46574 16.5158 9.018 15.9635 9.01807Z" fill="#FFFFFF" />
        </svg>
      </NeonIconCustom>

      {/* Now that the custom element has been registered, you can use it in Neon components */}
      <NeonIcon dataIcon="__mfe__schoology-external-tool|custom" dataSize="4x-large"/>
    </>
  );
}
```

Using custom icons in select fields:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonIcon, NeonIconCustom, NeonSelectField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function IconCustomExampleSelect() {
  const [modelValue, setModelValue] = useState(undefined);

  return (
    <>
      {/* Register custom icons */}
      <NeonIconCustom id="__mfe__schoology-external-tool">
        <svg viewBox="0 0 26 26" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" >
          <rect width="20" height="20" x="3" y="3" rx="2" fill="#0080A8" />
          <path d="M15.9635 9.01807L11.06399 9.01807C10.51167 9.018 10.06393 9.46574 10.064 10.01806C10.064 10.57031 10.51174 11.01805 11.06399 11.01805L13.5593 11.00801L9.35689 15.2104C8.96642 15.6009 8.96635 16.2341 9.35689 16.6247C9.74742 17.0152 10.38064 17.0151 10.7711 16.6247L14.9735 12.42222L14.9635 14.9176C14.9635 15.4698 15.4112 15.9175 15.9635 15.9175C16.5158 15.9176 16.9635 15.4699 16.9635 14.9176V10.01806C16.9635 9.46574 16.5158 9.018 15.9635 9.01807Z" fill="#FFFFFF" />
        </svg>
      </NeonIconCustom>

      <NeonIconCustom id="__mfe__naviance-tallo">
        <svg width="18" height="18" viewBox="0 0 18 18" fill="none" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
          {/* SVG content here */}
        </svg>
      </NeonIconCustom>

      {/* Use custom icons in a select field */}
      <NeonSelectField
        id="__mfe__custom-icon-select"
        dataLabelText="Select an option"
        modelValue={modelValue}
        modelValueChange={(value) => { setModelValue(value); }}
        options={[
          {value: 'external-tool', text: 'External Tool', icon: '__mfe__schoology-external-tool|custom'},
          {value: 'naviance-tallo', text: 'Naviance Tallo', icon: '__mfe__naviance-tallo|custom'},
        ]}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

Dynamically adding a custom icon:
```jsx
import React, { useRef } from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonIcon, NeonIconCustom } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function IconCustomExampleDynamic() {
  const elementRef = useRef(null);
  const dynamicSvg = `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="100%" height="100%" viewBox="0 0 300 300">
    <title>SVG Logo</title>
    <desc>A sample SVG logo</desc>
    <!-- SVG content here -->
  </svg>`;

  return (
    <>
      <NeonButton
        id="dynamic-icon-button"
        dataText="Dynamically load icon"
        onClick={() => {
          const element = document.createElement('__neon__icon-custom');
          element.setAttribute('id', '__mfe__svg-logo');
          if (elementRef.current) {
            elementRef.current.replaceChildren(element);
            element.innerHTML = dynamicSvg;
          }
        }}
      />

      <div ref={elementRef}></div>
      <NeonIcon dataIcon="__mfe__svg-logo|custom" />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Important Usage Notes

1. Icon names must be namespaced using a unique identifier to your project such as `__mfe__` to prevent icon name collisions between different micro frontends.

2. When setting an icon for a neon component, postfix the name with "|custom":
   ```jsx
   <NeonIcon dataIcon="__mfe__custom-icon-name|custom"></NeonIcon>
   ```

3. SVG exports from design tools like Figma may require adjustment:
   - Export as SVG
   - Depending on the SVG, you may need to set "Simplify Stroke" to either true or false
   - SVGs are sometimes unpredictable and may require manual editing

4. You only need to register custom icons once, and then they are available throughout your application.

5. For RTL (Right-to-Left) language support, add the "rtl-flip" modifier to your icon reference:
   ```jsx
   <NeonIcon dataIcon="__mfe__custom-icon|custom|rtl-flip" />
   ```


# NeonIconStack

A component that displays an icon with a background shape, creating a visually distinctive stacked icon experience.

## When To Use

Use the NeonIconStack component when you need to:

- Create visually distinctive icons with background shapes
- Highlight important actions or features with decorated icons
- Add visual hierarchy to your interface with styled icons
- Create consistent icon treatments across your application
- Provide visual categorization through color-coded icon backgrounds
- Draw attention to specific icon elements
- Emphasize key functionalities with enhanced visual treatment
- Add a decorative element to simple iconography

NeonIconStack combines a background shape with a foreground icon to create a layered effect. It's useful for creating visual interest and drawing attention to specific functionality in your interface.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| dataIcon | string | Yes | - | The icon name for the foreground icon |
| dataShape | string | No | 'circle' | The background shape. Options: 'circle', 'square', 'diamond', 'hexagon' |
| dataSize | string | No | 'large' | Size of the icon stack. Options: 'x-small', 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'x-large', 'xx-large', 'xxx-large' |
| dataColor | string | No | 'gray' | Color of the icon stack. Options: 'magenta', 'red', 'orange', 'yellow', 'green', 'teal', 'cyan', 'purple', 'gray' |
| id | string | No | - | Unique identifier for the component |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |

## Examples

# NeonIcon

A versatile icon component that displays SVG icons from the Neon Design System icon library.

## When To Use

Use the NeonIcon component when you need to:

- Display standard icons that are part of the Neon Design System
- Add visual indicators or actions to UI elements
- Create visual consistency across your application with standardized iconography
- Enhance user experience with recognizable visual elements
- Add intuitive visual cues for actions, statuses, or information types
- Provide compact visual representation where text would be too verbose
- Support RTL (right-to-left) layouts with automatically flipping icons
- Apply consistent styling to icons throughout your application

NeonIcon provides access to the complete Neon icon library, with options for sizing, coloring, and RTL support. It serves as the foundation for icon display across all Neon components.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | No | - | The html id for the component, must be unique |
| dataIcon | string | Yes | - | The name of the icon to display from the Neon icon library |
| dataSize | string | No | 'medium' | The size of the icon. Options: 'xx-small', 'x-small', 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'x-large', 'xx-large', 'xxx-large', 'xxxx-large', '5x-large', '6x-large', '7x-large' |
| dataSizeMobile | string | No | - | The size to make the icon at mobile screen sizes. If not specified, it defaults to dataSize |
| dataColor | string | No | - | The color family for the icon. Options: 'magenta', 'red', 'orange', 'yellow', 'green', 'teal', 'cyan', 'navy', 'purple', 'gray', 'ai' |
| dataColorWeight | string | No | '700' | The color weight for the icon. Options: '100', '200', '300', '400', '500', '600', '700', '800'. Requires dataColor to be set |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |

## Special Features

### RTL Support
To make an icon flip automatically in right-to-left (RTL) mode, add `|rtl-flip` to the end of the icon name:
```jsx
<NeonIcon dataIcon="caret-left|rtl-flip" />
```

### Icon Categories
The Neon icon library has several categories of icons:
- General icons: Available for general use throughout the application
- App nav icons (`app-nav-*`): Specifically for use with NeonAppNav components
- App header icons (`app-header-*`): Specifically for use in the app header
- Status icons: Have specific colors associated with them for status indication
- PS app icons: Have explicit colors that should not be modified
- US state icons: Icons representing each US state

## Examples

Basic icon usage:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonIcon } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function IconExampleBasic() {
  return <NeonIcon dataIcon="flag" />;
}
```

```jsx

      <NeonIcon dataIcon="flag" dataSize="small" />
      <NeonIcon dataIcon="flag" dataSize="medium" />
      <NeonIcon dataIcon="flag" dataSize="large" />
      <NeonIcon dataIcon="flag" dataSize="x-large" />
      <NeonIcon dataIcon="flag" dataSize="xx-large" />
      <NeonIcon dataIcon="flag" dataSize="xxx-large" />
      <NeonIcon dataIcon="flag" dataSize="xxxx-large" />
      <NeonIcon dataIcon="flag" dataSize="5x-large" />
      <NeonIcon dataIcon="flag" dataSize="6x-large" />
      <NeonIcon dataIcon="flag" dataSize="7x-large" />
```

# NeonIllustrationSimple

A streamlined component for displaying simple SVG illustrations with consistent styling and sizing options.

## When To Use

Use the NeonIllustrationSimple component when you need to:

- Display simple, flat SVG illustrations throughout your application
- Present visual elements with consistent styling and sizing
- Add visual cues or graphical elements to enhance user experience
- Provide visual context alongside content
- Create visual indicators or status representations
- Maintain brand-consistent iconography across your interface
- Add visual elements that need to be responsive to different container sizes
- Include decorative graphics that should adapt to various display sizes

NeonIllustrationSimple is designed for simple, lightweight SVG illustrations that load dynamically from a CDN. For more complex illustration needs with background options and additional features, consider the standard NeonIllustration component.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| dataIllustration | string | Yes | - | The name of the illustration to display |
| dataSize | string | No | - | The size of the illustration. When undefined, the illustration is responsive (between 40px and 112px) |

### Size Options
- `3x-small`
- `2x-small`
- `x-small`
- `small`
- `medium`
- `large`
- `x-large`
- `2x-large`
- `3x-large`
- `4x-large`

## Examples

Simple illustration with defined size:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonIllustrationSimple } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function IllustrationSimpleExampleBasic() {
  return (
    <NeonIllustrationSimple dataIllustration="star" dataSize="medium" />
  );
}
```

Demonstration of all available sizes:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonIllustrationSimple } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function IllustrationSimpleExampleSizes() {
  const illustrationSimpleSizes = [
    '3x-small', '2x-small', 'x-small', 'small', 'medium',
    'large', 'x-large', '2x-large', '3x-large', '4x-large'
  ];

  return (
    <table>
      <tbody>
        {illustrationSimpleSizes.map((size) => (
          <tr key={size}>
            <th>{size}</th>
            <td>
              <NeonIllustrationSimple dataIllustration="star" dataSize={size} />
            </td>
          </tr>
        ))}
      </tbody>
    </table>
  );
}
```

Responsive illustration that adapts to container size:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonIllustrationSimple } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function IllustrationSimpleExampleResponsive() {
  return (
    <div className="resizable-container">
      <NeonIllustrationSimple dataIllustration="star" />
    </div>
  );
}
```


# NeonIllustration

A versatile component for displaying SVG illustrations with customizable colors, backgrounds, and other styling options.

## When To Use

Use the NeonIllustration component when you need to:

- Add visual appeal to empty states, error pages, or confirmation screens
- Convey complex concepts through visual representation
- Create a consistent visual language throughout your application
- Provide visual cues for different sections or features
- Enhance user experience with engaging graphics
- Add thematic elements that align with your application's color scheme
- Create focal points or visual hierarchy in your layouts
- Illustrate processes, concepts, or ideas visually

NeonIllustration offers a wide range of pre-designed illustrations that can be customized with different colors, backgrounds, and other properties to match your application's design requirements.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| dataIllustration | string | Yes | - | Sets the illustration to display (see available illustrations in the component explorer) |
| dataColor | string | No | 'navy' | Sets the primary color of the illustration. Options: 'yellow', 'green', 'teal', 'orange', 'red', 'purple', 'magenta', 'cyan', 'navy' |
| dataBackground | string | No | 'none' | Sets the background layer style. Options: 'none', 'simple', 'complex' |
| dataShowPeople | boolean | No | true | Controls visibility of people in illustrations when applicable |
| dataAspectRatio | string | No | - | Forces a specific aspect ratio. Options: '1:1', '3:2' |

## Examples

Basic usage with default styling:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonIllustration } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function IllustrationBasicExample() {
  return (
    <NeonIllustration dataIllustration="happy-students" />
  );
}
```

Customizing color:
```jsx

    <div className="__neon__grid-container">

        <NeonIllustration dataIllustration="happy-students" dataColor="yellow" />
      </div>
      <div className="__neon__grid-col-2 __neon__grid-col-md-4 __neon__grid-col-lg-4">
        <NeonIllustration dataIllustration="happy-students" dataColor="green" />
      </div>
      <div className="__neon__grid-col-2 __neon__grid-col-md-4 __neon__grid-col-lg-4">
        <NeonIllustration dataIllustration="happy-students" dataColor="teal" />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Different background styles:
```jsx

  return (
    <>
      <NeonIllustration dataIllustration="location" />
      <NeonIllustration dataIllustration="location" dataBackground="simple" />

  );
}
```

Toggling people visibility:
```jsx

  return (

      <div>
        <h3>With People</h3>
        <NeonIllustration dataIllustration="location" />
      </div>

```

Using illustrations for empty states:
```jsx

  return (
    <div className="__neon__grid-container">
```

Setting a specific aspect ratio:

```jsx
    </>

```




# NeonImage

A component for displaying images with support for fallbacks, alternative text, and object-fit options.

## When To Use

Use the NeonImage component when you need to:

- Display images within your application with proper accessibility
- Handle image loading failures gracefully with automatic fallbacks
- Control how images fit within their container (cover or contain)
- Display images with consistent styling across your application
- Ensure images have appropriate alt text for accessibility
- Implement responsive images that scale appropriately

NeonImage is designed to provide a standardized way to display images with built-in error handling and accessibility features. Use it whenever you need to display images in your application.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | No | - | Unique identifier for the image |
| dataSrc | string | Yes | - | The URL source for the image |
| dataAlt | string | Yes | - | Alt text for the image. Empty string is appropriate when image is not content and used for decoration or illustrative purposes |
| dataObjectFit | string | No | 'cover' | How the object should fit in the container. Options: 'cover', 'contain' |

## Examples

Simple image usage:

```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonImage } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ImageExampleSimple() {
  return (
    <NeonImage
      dataSrc="example-files/img/people-in-hallway.png"
      dataAlt="People walking in a hallway"
    />
  );
}
```

Image with object-fit contain:

```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonImage } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ImageExampleContain() {
  return (
    <div style={{ width: '300px', height: '200px' }}>
      <NeonImage
        dataSrc="example-files/img/quad-walking-path.jpeg"
        dataAlt="Concrete walking path surrounded by trees"
        dataObjectFit="contain"
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

Image with fallback:

```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonImage } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ImageExampleWithFallback() {
  return (
    <div>
      <NeonImage
        dataSrc="non-existent-image.jpg"
        dataAlt="This image will fall back to the default fallback image"
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

Image with decorative purpose (empty alt text):

```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonImage } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ImageExampleDecorative() {
  return (
    <NeonImage
      dataSrc="example-files/img/flower-1.jpg"
      dataAlt=""
    />
  );
}
```


# NeonItemPicker

A customizable component for displaying and selecting items from a list or dropdown with search filtering and pagination capabilities.

## When To Use

Use the NeonItemPicker component when you need to:

- Display a selectable list of items in a popper, dialog, or drawer
- Allow users to search and filter through a large number of options
- Enable single or multiple item selection with checkbox controls
- Show a list of options with various visual elements (icons, tags, etc.)
- Implement a "Select All" functionality for multiple selections
- Display selected items as chips that can be removed individually
- Create custom dropdowns that require filtering capabilities
- Handle large datasets with pagination support
- Provide a rich interactive experience for item selection

NeonItemPicker is particularly useful for creating advanced dropdown menus and selection interfaces in the Neon Design System. It's often used internally by other components like MultiSelectField and SelectField to handle their dropdown functionality.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the item picker |
| dataControlType | string | Yes | - | Display mode for the item picker. Options: 'popper', 'dialog', 'drawer', 'app-nav-mobile' |
| dataShowFilter | string | No | 'auto' | Whether to show the search filter. Options: 'true', 'false', 'auto' (shows when 10+ items) |
| dataConstrainWidth | string | No | 'true' | Whether to constrain the width of the item picker |
| dataShowSelectAll | string | No | 'false' | Whether to show the "Select All" checkbox |
| dataSelectAllText | string | No | - | Custom text for the "Select All" option |
| dataSelectAllSubtextMessageKey | string | No | - | Message key for the select all subtext |
| dataShowChipSet | string | No | 'false' | Whether to show selected items as chips |
| dataChipSetClearAllThreshold | string | No | - | Number of chips to show before displaying a "Clear All" button |
| dataChipSetEnableClearAll | string | No | 'auto' | Whether to show the "Clear All" button in chip set |
| dataPopperMaxHeight | string | No | - | Maximum height of the popper. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large' |
| dataHeaderText | string | No | - | Text to display in the header |
| dataShowHeaderText | string | No | 'false' | Whether to show the header text |
| dataItemTooltipPlacement | string | No | 'right' | Tooltip placement for items |
| dataItemMenuSize | string | No | - | Size of the menu items. Options: 'auto', etc. |
| dataEmptyResultsHelperText | string | No | - | Helper text to display when no results are found |
| dataUseArrow | string | No | 'false' | Whether to display an arrow on the popper |
| menuOptions | Array<MenuOption \| 'DIVIDER'> | No | [] | Array of menu options to display |
| filterString | string | No | '' | Initial filter string for searching items |
| value | Record<string, boolean> | No | {} | Selected values as an object map of item ID to boolean |
| context | any | No | - | Context object to pass to option click handlers |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| item-picker-footer | No | Content to display in the footer of the item picker |

## Examples

Basic item picker with search:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonItemPicker } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ItemPickerExampleSimple() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState({});

  const options = [
    { id: 'option1', text: 'Option 1' },
    { id: 'option2', text: 'Option 2' },
    { id: 'option3', text: 'Option 3' },
    { id: 'option4', text: 'Option 4' }
  ];

  return (
    <NeonItemPicker
      id="simple-item-picker"
      dataControlType="popper"
      dataShowFilter="true"
      menuOptions={options}
      value={value}
      onValueChange={(newValue) => setValue(newValue)}
    />
  );
}
```

Item picker with select all option:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonItemPicker } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ItemPickerExampleSelectAll() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState({});

  const options = [
    { id: 'option1', text: 'Option 1' },
    { id: 'option2', text: 'Option 2' },
    { id: 'option3', text: 'Option 3' },
    { id: 'option4', text: 'Option 4' },
    { id: 'option5', text: 'Option 5' },
    { id: 'option6', text: 'Option 6' }
  ];

  return (
    <NeonItemPicker
      id="select-all-item-picker"
      dataControlType="popper"
      dataShowFilter="true"
      dataShowSelectAll="true"
      dataSelectAllText="Select All Options"
      menuOptions={options}
      value={value}
      onValueChange={(newValue) => setValue(newValue)}
    />
  );
}
```

Item picker with chips showing selected values:

```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';

export function ItemPickerExampleWithChips() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState({
    option1: true,
    option3: true
  });

  const options = [
    { id: 'option1', text: 'Option 1' },
    { id: 'option2', text: 'Option 2' },
    { id: 'option3', text: 'Option 3' },
    { id: 'option4', text: 'Option 4' }
  ];

  return (
    <NeonItemPicker
      id="chip-item-picker"
      dataControlType="dialog"
      dataShowFilter="true"
      dataShowChipSet="true"
      dataChipSetEnableClearAll="true"
      menuOptions={options}
      value={value}
      onValueChange={(newValue) => setValue(newValue)}
    />
  );
}
```

# NeonJsObject

A utility component for displaying JavaScript objects in a formatted, readable way with syntax highlighting.

## When To Use

Use the NeonJsObject component when you need to:

- Display JSON or JavaScript objects during development and debugging
- Show object structures in a readable format with proper indentation and highlighting
- Debug complex data structures in internal tools or administration interfaces
- Visualize API responses or state data during development
- Create development tools or debugging interfaces

NeonJsObject is designed primarily as a development and debugging tool. It is not intended for customer-facing interfaces and its styles may change between Neon versions without notice.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the component |
| value | any | Yes | undefined | The JavaScript object to display. Must be compatible with JSON.stringify() |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |

## Examples

Simple object display:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonJsObject } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function JsObjectExampleSimple() {
  return (
    <NeonJsObject value={{
      firstName: 'pac',
      lastName: 'man',
      address: {
        street: '1234 blue maze',
        city: 'Cyber City',
        state: 'CA',
        zip: '12345'
      },
      enemies: [
        'Inky',
        'Blinky',
        'Pinky',
        'Clyde'
      ]
    }} />
  );
}
```

Displaying API response data:
```jsx
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
import { NeonJsObject } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function JsObjectExampleApiData() {
  const [userData, setUserData] = useState({});

  useEffect(() => {
    // Simulating API call
    setTimeout(() => {
      setUserData({
        id: 123,
        name: 'John Doe',
        email: 'john.doe@example.com',
        permissions: ['read', 'write', 'admin'],
        metadata: {
          lastLogin: '2023-04-15T14:30:45Z',
          loginCount: 27,
          preferences: {
            theme: 'dark',
            notifications: true
          }
        }
      });
    }, 1000);
  }, []);

  return (
    <div>
      <h3>User Data</h3>
      <NeonJsObject value={userData} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

Dynamic state display for debugging:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonJsObject, NeonButton } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function JsObjectExampleStateDebug() {
  const [counter, setCounter] = useState(0);
  const [lastClickTime, setLastClickTime] = useState(null);
  const [clickHistory, setClickHistory] = useState([]);

  const handleClick = () => {
    const now = new Date().toISOString();
    setCounter(counter + 1);
    setLastClickTime(now);
    setClickHistory([...clickHistory, now]);
  };

  const debugState = {
    counter,
    lastClickTime,
    clickHistory
  };

  return (
    <div>
      <NeonButton
        id="increment-button"
        dataText="Increment Counter"
        onClick={handleClick}
      />
      <div style={{ marginTop: '20px' }}>
        <h4>Component State:</h4>
        <NeonJsObject value={debugState} />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```


# NeonLabeledWidget

An abstract component that provides standardized labeling structure for form fields and UI widgets in the Neon Design System, featuring consistent label presentation, helper text, badges for required/optional fields, and tooltips.

## When To Use

Use the NeonLabeledWidget component when you need to:

- Create custom form field components with consistent label styling
- Display form elements with standard labeling, helper text, and tooltips
- Implement accessible form controls with proper labeling
- Add required/optional indicators to input fields
- Create widget interfaces that need explanatory text and tooltips
- Ensure form components follow the Neon Design System's accessibility guidelines
- Build custom input components that maintain visual consistency with other form elements
- Implement form components that need supporting/helper text

NeonLabeledWidget is an abstract component that serves as a foundation for other form components in the Neon Design System. It's not used directly but extended by various input field components to provide consistent labeling functionality. It handles proper accessibility relationships between labels and inputs, provides tooltip support, and manages the display of helper text and required/optional indicators.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the component |
| dataLabelText | string | No | - | The text to display as the component's label |
| dataShowLabel | boolean | No | true | Whether to show the label text |
| dataAriaLabel | string | No | - | Custom accessible label for the component |
| dataHelperText | string | No | - | Supporting text displayed below the component |
| dataShowOptionalBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to show an "Optional" badge next to the label |
| dataHideRequiredBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to hide the "Required" badge for required fields |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Text to display in a tooltip when hovering over the help icon |
| dataConstrainDescription | boolean | No | false | Whether to constrain the width of description text |
| children | React.ReactNode | No | - | Content to display inside the widget |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |

## Examples

Basic labeled widget with helper text:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonTextField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function LabeledWidgetExampleBasic() {
  return (
    <NeonTextField
      id="text-field-example"
      dataLabelText="Username"
      dataHelperText="Enter your username or email address"
    />
  );
}
```

Widget with tooltip and optional badge:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonTextField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function LabeledWidgetExampleWithTooltip() {
  return (
    <NeonTextField
      id="text-field-with-tooltip"
      dataLabelText="Business ID"
      dataHelperText="Your unique business identifier"
      dataTooltipText="The Business ID can be found on your registration documents"
      dataShowOptionalBadge={true}
    />
  );
}
```

Required field with hidden label:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonTextField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function LabeledWidgetExampleHiddenLabel() {
  return (
    <NeonTextField
      id="required-hidden-label"
      dataLabelText="Email Address"
      dataShowLabel={false}
      dataAriaLabel="Email Address"
      dataRequired={true}
    />
  );
}
```

Field with constrained description:

```jsx
  return (
    <NeonTextareaField
      id="textarea-constrained"
      dataLabelText="Comments"
      dataHelperText="Please provide any additional information that might help us process your request"

  );

```

Multiple labeled fields in a form:
```jsx

  return (
    <div className="neon-form-group">
      <NeonTextField
        id="user-first-name"

        dataRequired={true}
      />

      <NeonTextField
        id="user-last-name"
        dataLabelText="Last Name"
        dataRequired={true}
      />

      <NeonTextField
        id="user-phone"
        dataLabelText="Phone Number"
        dataHelperText="We'll only use this to contact you about your account"
        dataShowOptionalBadge={true}
      />

        id="user-terms"

        dataHelperText="You must accept the terms to continue"
        dataRequired={true}
```

# NeonLastUpdated

A component for displaying the last updated date and time with customizable formatting options.

## When To Use

Use the NeonLastUpdated component when you need to:

- Indicate when content was last refreshed or modified
- Display timestamp information in a consistent, accessible format
- Show the recency of information to establish credibility and relevance
- Provide users with context about data freshness
- Comply with requirements to show when data was last updated
- Add time and date information in card footers or at the bottom of content areas
- Show timestamp information with optional timezone indication
- Create a standardized way to represent temporal information across your application

NeonLastUpdated is typically placed at the bottom of content containers to provide users with information about when the content was last modified or updated.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the component |
| lastUpdated | Date | No | - | The last updated Date object |
| dataDate | string | No | - | Format: MM/DD/YYYY. The last updated date |
| dataTime | string | No | - | Format: HH:mm. The last updated time in 24-hour format |
| dataColor | string | No | 'light' | Sets the color of the component. Options: 'light', 'dark' |
| dataText | string | No | 'Last Updated' | The text that is shown before the date |
| dataTimeZoneString | string | No | - | The time zone string shown after the date. Does not convert the date |

## Examples

Basic usage with a Date object:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonLastUpdated } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function LastUpdatedExample() {
  const yesterday = new Date();
  yesterday.setDate(yesterday.getDate() - 1);
  
  return (
    <NeonLastUpdated lastUpdated={yesterday} />
  );
}
```

Using date and time attributes:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonLastUpdated } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function LastUpdatedAttributeExample() {
  return (
    <NeonLastUpdated dataDate="07/02/2023" dataTime="19:06" />
  );
}
```

Color variants:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonLastUpdated } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function LastUpdatedColorExample() {
  const today = new Date();
  
  return (
    <>
      {/* Default (light) */}
      <NeonLastUpdated lastUpdated={today} />
      
      {/* Dark variant - for use on light backgrounds */}
      <NeonLastUpdated lastUpdated={today} dataColor="dark" />
    </>
  );
}
```

Custom text and timezone:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonLastUpdated } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function LastUpdatedCustomTextExample() {
  const today = new Date();
  
  return (
    <>
      {/* Standard usage */}
      <NeonLastUpdated lastUpdated={today} />
      
      {/* With timezone */}
      <NeonLastUpdated lastUpdated={today} dataTimeZoneString="EST" />
      
      {/* With custom prefix text */}
      <NeonLastUpdated dataText="The last update occurred at" lastUpdated={today} />
    </>
  );
}
```




# NeonLayoutDetail

A versatile layout component for creating detail panels with consistent structure, navigation, and responsive behavior.

## When To Use

Use the NeonLayoutDetail component when you need to:

- Create a detail view or panel with a standardized structure
- Implement a navigable panel with a back button
- Display content with consistent layout and spacing
- Create modals or flyout panels with standard navigation
- Organize content with header, body, and footer sections
- Implement split-pane layouts with responsive behavior for mobile devices
- Create detail views that overlay the main content
- Build layouts with optional scrollable regions
- Support complex content organization with pre-body and post-body areas
- Implement custom button footers for actions

NeonLayoutDetail is the foundation for building structured detail views in the Neon Design System. It provides a standard layout with navigation capabilities, responsive behavior, and support for various content organization patterns.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the layout |
| dataBackButtonText | string | No | 'neon\|layoutdetail\|Go Back To Previous Page' | Text displayed on the back button |
| dataBodyScroll | boolean | No | true | Whether the body should scroll when content overflows |
| dataInjectionSpacing | boolean | No | true | When false, removes left and right spacing |
| dataBodyFullHeight | boolean | No | false | When true, the body and its wrappers are full height |
| dataShowHeaderDivider | boolean | No | true | When false, hides the bottom divider for the header |
| dataShowPreBodyDivider | boolean | No | true | When false, hides the bottom divider for the pre-body |
| dataShowPostBodyDivider | boolean | No | true | When false, hides the top divider for the post-body |
| dataShowFooterDivider | boolean | No | true | When false, hides the top divider for the footer |
| dataAnimate | boolean | No | false | Enables animation for the detail layout |
| dataBypassFocusTrap | boolean | No | false | When true, disables the focus trap (use only for bug workarounds) |
| dataMobileLandingPane | string | No | 'left' | Determines which pane is displayed on mobile ('left' or 'right') |
| preCloseCallback | function | No | - | Called before closing; return true to prevent closing |
| neonLayoutDetailHasClosed | function | No | - | Event handler for when layout detail is closed |
| neonLayoutDetailMobilePaneClose | function | No | - | Event handler for when mobile secondary pane is closed |
| dataShowMobileSecondaryPane | boolean | No | false | Controls visibility of the secondary pane on mobile |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| header-content | No | Section in the top right of header for buttons or other components |
| body | No | Main content area that scrolls vertically when content overflows |
| pre-body | No | Static section above the scrolling body |
| post-body | No | Static section below the scrolling body, anchored to the top of the footer |
| footer-start | No | (Deprecated) Left side of the footer |
| footer-end | No | (Deprecated) Right side of the footer |
| layout-detail-button-footer | No | Contains a single NeonButtonFooter component |
| layout-detail-left-pane | No | Left side of a split-pane layout |
| layout-detail-right-pane | No | Right side of a split-pane layout |

## CSS Classes

| Class | Applied To | Description |
|-------|-----------|-------------|
| __neon__layout-detail-fixed-pane | div[data-slot="layout-detail-left-pane"] or div[data-slot="layout-detail-right-pane"] | Sets one slot to be fixed width with the other dynamic |
| __neon__layout-detail-header-border | div | Adds a border to the bottom of a header within a pane |
| __neon__layout-detail-footer-border | div | Adds a border to the top of a footer within a pane |
| __neon__layout | div | Container for layout structure within panes |
| __neon__layout-scrollable | div | Creates a scrollable area within a layout |

## Examples

Simple layout detail:

```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonLayoutDetail } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function LayoutDetailExampleSimple() {
  const [showLayout, setShowLayout] = useState(false);

  return (
    <>
      <NeonButton
        id="open-layout-btn"
        dataText="Open Layout"
        onClick={() => { setShowLayout(true) }}
      />
      {showLayout &&
        <NeonLayoutDetail
          id="view-layout"
          dataAnimate="true"
          dataBackButtonText="Check out this custom back button text!"
          neonLayoutDetailHasClosed={() => { setShowLayout(false) }}
          dataInjectionSpacing="true"
        >
          <div data-slot="header-content">
            <div>Header content goes here</div>
          </div>
          <div data-slot="pre-body">
            <div>Pre-body content goes here</div>
          </div>
          <div data-slot="body">
            <div>Main content goes here</div>
          </div>
          <div data-slot="post-body">
            <div>Post-body content goes here</div>
          </div>
          <div data-slot="footer-start">
            <div>Footer start content</div>
          </div>
          <div data-slot="footer-end">
            <div>Footer end content</div>
          </div>
        </NeonLayoutDetail>
      }
    </>
  );
}
```

Layout detail with button footer:

```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonButtonFooter, NeonLayoutDetail } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function LayoutDetailExampleButtonFooter() {
  const [showLayout, setShowLayout] = useState(false);

  return (
    <>
      <NeonButton
        id="layout-button-footer"
        dataText="Open layout with button footer"
        onClick={() => { setShowLayout(true) }}
      />
      {showLayout &&
        <NeonLayoutDetail
          id="layout-detail"
          dataAnimate="true"
          neonLayoutDetailHasClosed={() => { setShowLayout(false) }}
        >
          <div data-slot="body">
            <p>This is an example that uses the button footer</p>
          </div>
          <div data-slot="layout-detail-button-footer">
            <NeonButtonFooter
              id="button-footer"
              primaryButton={{
                id: 'primary-button',
                text: 'Save',
                onClick: (event) => { 
                  document.getElementById('button-footer')?.dispatchEvent(
                    new Event('neonLayoutDetailClose', {bubbles: true})
                  );
                },
              }}
              tertiaryButton={{
                id: 'tertiary-button',
                text: 'Cancel',
                onClick: (event) => {
                  document.getElementById('button-footer')?.dispatchEvent(
                    new Event('neonLayoutDetailClose', {bubbles: true})
                  );
                },
              }}
              buttons={[
                {
                  id: 'button-1',
                  text: 'Button 1',
                  onClick: () => { console.log('Button 1 clicked') },
                },
                {
                  id: 'button-2',
                  text: 'Button 2',
                  onClick: () => { console.log('Button 2 clicked') },
                },
              ]}
            />
          </div>
        </NeonLayoutDetail>
      }
    </>
  );
}
```

Split-pane layout:

```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonLayoutDetail } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function LayoutDetailExampleSplitPane() {

  const [showMobilePane, setShowMobilePane] = useState(false);

      <NeonButton
        id="split-pane-button"

          id="split-layout"
          dataAnimate="true"

          dataMobileLandingPane="left"

              </div>

                  id="mobile-toggle"
                  dataText="Show Right Pane"
                  onClick={() => { setShowMobilePane(true) }}
                />
              </div>
              <div className="__neon__layout-detail-footer-border">
                <p>Left pane footer</p>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>
          <div data-slot="layout-detail-right-pane">
            <div className="__neon__layout">
              <div className="__neon__layout-detail-header-border">
                <p>Right pane header</p>
              </div>
              <div className="__neon__layout-scrollable">
                <p>Right pane scrollable content</p>
              </div>
              <div className="__neon__layout-detail-footer-border">
                <p>Right pane footer</p>
              </div>
            </div>
          </div>
        </NeonLayoutDetail>
      }
    </>
  );
}
```

Full-height body example:

```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonLayoutDetail } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function LayoutDetailExampleFullHeight() {
```
