With pre-close callback:

```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonLayoutDetail } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function LayoutDetailExamplePreCloseCallback() {
  const [showLayout, setShowLayout] = useState(false);

  // This callback is called before closing
  const handlePreClose = () => {
    const shouldPreventClose = confirm("Are you sure you want to close?");
    return shouldPreventClose; // Return true to prevent closing, false to allow
  };

  return (
    <>
      <NeonButton
        id="pre-close-button"
        dataText="Open Layout With Confirmation"
        onClick={() => { setShowLayout(true) }}
      />
      {showLayout &&
        <NeonLayoutDetail
          id="pre-close-layout"
          dataAnimate="true"
          dataBackButtonText="Try to close (will prompt)"
          neonLayoutDetailHasClosed={() => { setShowLayout(false) }}
          preCloseCallback={handlePreClose}
        >
          <div data-slot="body">
            <p>Click the back button to see the pre-close callback in action</p>
          </div>
        </NeonLayoutDetail>
      }
    </>
  );
}
```


# NeonListItem

A versatile list item component used to display structured content with various controls, icons, avatars, and interactive elements.

## When To Use

Use the NeonListItem component when you need to:

- Create interactive list interfaces with consistent styling
- Display structured content in lists or menus with primary text and optional subtext
- Implement list-based navigation with links or buttons
- Create selectable lists with checkbox or radio button functionality
- Display user information with integrated avatars
- Build hierarchical navigation menus with nested items
- Show content with supporting icons, tags, or illustrations
- Implement list items with specific interactive behaviors based on type

NeonListItem is a fundamental building block for creating list-based interfaces in the Neon Design System. It offers multiple control types to adapt to various interaction patterns, from simple text display to interactive controls like checkboxes and buttons.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the list item |
| dataText | string | Yes | - | Primary text displayed in the list item |
| dataSubtext | string | No | - | Secondary text displayed below the primary text |
| dataBody | string | No | - | Additional paragraph text displayed below the subtext |
| dataTextRight | string | No | - | Text displayed at the right end of the list item |
| dataHighlightText | string | No | - | Text to be highlighted within the primary text, subtext, or body |
| dataIsNested | boolean | No | false | Adds indentation to indicate nesting |
| dataIsSelected | boolean | No | false | Visually indicates the item is selected |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Disables the list item |
| dataAriaLabel | string | No | - | Accessible label for screen readers |
| dataBorderType | string | No | 'on-white' | Sets the border style. Options: 'on-white', 'on-gray' |
| dataConstrainWidth | boolean | No | true | When false, removes max-width constraints |
| dataControlType | string | No | 'text' | Type of control behavior. Options: 'text', 'button', 'checkbox', 'radio', 'link', 'heading', 'reset' |
| value | string \| boolean | No | - | Current value of the list item (for checkbox/radio types) |
| valueChange | function | No | - | Callback when item value changes |
| onClick | function | No | - | Callback when item is clicked (for button type) |
| name | string | No | - | Used for grouping radio buttons |
| dataIcon | string | No | - | Icon name to display on the left |
| dataIconColor | string | No | - | Color of the left icon |
| dataIconColorWeight | string | No | - | Color weight of the left icon |
| dataIconRight | string | No | - | Icon name to display on the right |
| dataIconRightColor | string | No | - | Color of the right icon |
| dataIconRightColorWeight | string | No | - | Color weight of the right icon |
| dataShowAvatar | boolean | No | false | Forces display of avatar placeholder |
| dataAvatarFirstName | string | No | - | First name for avatar |
| dataAvatarLastName | string | No | - | Last name for avatar |
| dataAvatarProfilePictureSrc | string | No | - | Image URL for avatar |
| dataAvatarSize | string | No | - | Size of the avatar. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large' |
| dataAvatarBackgroundOption | string | No | - | Avatar background style. Options: '0', '1', '2', '3', '4', 'high-contrast', 'theme', 'default' |
| dataUrl | string | No | - | URL for link type |
| dataOpenInNewTab | boolean | No | false | Opens link in new tab |
| dataTagText | string | No | - | Text displayed in the tag |
| dataTagSubtext | string | No | - | Subtext displayed in the tag |
| dataTagPosition | string | No | 'right' | Position of the tag. Options: 'left', 'right' |
| dataTagType | string | No | - | Visual style of the tag (e.g., 'teal') |
| dataCheckboxPosition | string | No | 'left' | Position of checkbox control. Options: 'left', 'right' |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Text displayed in the tooltip |
| dataTooltipPlacement | string | No | - | Tooltip position |
| dataPopperPlacement | string | No | - | Deprecated, use dataTooltipPlacement instead |
| dataChildrenIcon | string | No | - | Icon for child menu items |
| dataMenuPopperPlacement | string | No | - | Position of the menu popper |
| dataMenuSize | string | No | 'default' | Size behavior of the menu. Options: 'auto', 'default' |
| menuOptionChildren | Array | No | - | Child menu options |
| dataIllustrationSimple | string | No | - | Name of the simple illustration to display |
| dataIllustrationSimpleSize | string | No | 'medium' | Size of the illustration. Options: 'medium', 'large' |
| dataImageSrc | string | No | - | URL of an image to display |

## Examples

Basic text item:
```jsx
import React from 'react';

      dataSubtext="Secondary Text"
    />
  );
}
```

# NeonLoadingIndicator

A component that provides a visual indication when content is loading or an operation is in progress.

## When To Use

Use the NeonLoadingIndicator component when you need to:

- Show that content is being loaded or processed
- Indicate that a background operation is in progress
- Provide feedback to users during asynchronous operations
- Improve user experience during waiting periods
- Fill empty spaces while content is being fetched
- Create a consistent loading experience throughout your application

NeonLoadingIndicator helps improve user experience by providing visual feedback during processes that take time to complete. It can be used standalone or embedded within other components like buttons, select fields, and form elements that support loading states.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | No | - | Unique identifier for the component |
| dataSize | string | No | 'medium' | The size of the loading indicator. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'x-large' |
| dataSizeMobile | string | No | 'medium' | The size of the loading indicator on mobile and small screens. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'x-large' |
| dataInverse | boolean | No | false | Provides a visual that contrasts against dark backgrounds |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |

## Examples

Basic loading indicator:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonLoadingIndicator } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function BasicLoadingIndicator() {
  return (
    <NeonLoadingIndicator />
  );
}
```

Different sizes:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonLoadingIndicator } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function LoadingIndicatorSizes() {
  return (
    <>
      <NeonLoadingIndicator dataSize="small" />
      <NeonLoadingIndicator dataSize="medium" />
      <NeonLoadingIndicator dataSize="large" />
      <NeonLoadingIndicator dataSize="x-large" />
    </>
  );
}
```

Inverse loading indicator for dark backgrounds:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonLoadingIndicator } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function InverseLoadingIndicator() {
  return (
    <div style={{ background: 'var(--__neon__color-navy-600' }}>
      <NeonLoadingIndicator dataInverse="true" />
    </div>
  );
}
```

Inside other components:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonSelectField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function LoadingComponentsExample() {
  const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(true);

  return (
    <div className="__neon__form">
      <NeonButton
        id="loading-button"
        dataType="primary"
        dataText="Loading Button"
        dataIsLoading={isLoading}
      />

      <NeonSelectField
        id="loading-select"
        dataLabelText="Loading Select"
        dataIsLoading={isLoading}
        options={[]}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```


# NeonMasonryGrid

A responsive grid layout component that arranges items in a masonry-style pattern, optimizing space by positioning items based on available vertical space rather than forcing them into strict rows.

## When To Use

Use the NeonMasonryGrid component when you need to:

- Display a collection of content items of varying heights in a space-efficient layout
- Create a Pinterest-style or card-based dashboard layout
- Present multiple content cards in a visually appealing grid that adjusts to different screen sizes
- Display content in a dynamic layout that prioritizes efficient use of vertical space
- Create responsive dashboards with content blocks of differing heights
- Present information cards, tiles, or panels in a clean, organized manner
- Optimize space utilization when displaying items with irregular heights
- Implement modern, visually engaging content displays without uniform heights

NeonMasonryGrid is particularly useful for dashboard interfaces where multiple content cards or widgets need to be displayed efficiently without wasting vertical space. It provides a clean, organized way to present information while maximizing screen real estate.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | No | - | Unique identifier for the masonry grid |
| dataColumns | number (2 or 3) | No | 3 | The number of columns to display in the grid on desktop |
| dataPreserveOrder | boolean | No | false | If true, the order of the children will be preserved |
| children | React.ReactNode | No | - | Content elements to be arranged in the masonry grid |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |

## Utility Classes

| Class | Applied To | Description |
|-------|------------|-------------|
| neon-masonry-grid-intrinsic-width | direct child | When set on the first child, the grid will create columns based on the first item's width |

## Examples

Basic masonry grid:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonCardStandard, NeonMasonryGrid } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function MasonryGridExampleSimple() {
  return (
    <NeonMasonryGrid>
      <NeonCardStandard
        id="card-1"
        dataHeading="Card 1"
        dataHeaderIcon="article"
      >
        <div data-slot="body">
          <p className="__neon__text">Content for card 1</p>
        </div>
      </NeonCardStandard>

      <NeonCardStandard
        id="card-2"
        dataHeading="Card 2"
        dataHeaderIcon="calendar"
      >
        <div data-slot="body">
          <p className="__neon__text">Content for card 2</p>
        </div>
      </NeonCardStandard>

      <NeonCardStandard
        id="card-3"
        dataHeading="Card 3"
        dataHeaderIcon="info"
      >
        <div data-slot="body">
          <p className="__neon__text">Content for card 3</p>
        </div>
      </NeonCardStandard>
    </NeonMasonryGrid>
  );
}
```

Masonry grid with custom columns and preserved order:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonCardStandard, NeonMasonryGrid } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function MasonryGridExampleCustom() {
  return (
    <NeonMasonryGrid
      dataColumns={2}
      dataPreserveOrder={true}
    >
      <NeonCardStandard
        dataHeading="High Priority"
        dataHeaderIcon="priority_high"
        style={{ height: '400px' }}
      >
        <div data-slot="body">
          <p className="__neon__text">This card will maintain its position as the first item</p>
        </div>
      </NeonCardStandard>

      <NeonCardStandard
        dataHeading="Secondary Item"
        dataHeaderIcon="list"
        style={{ height: '300px' }}
      >
        <div data-slot="body">
          <p className="__neon__text">This card will always be positioned second</p>
        </div>
      </NeonCardStandard>

      <NeonCardStandard
        dataHeading="Third Item"
        dataHeaderIcon="check_circle"
        style={{ height: '500px' }}
      >
        <div data-slot="body">
          <p className="__neon__text">This card will always be positioned third</p>
        </div>
      </NeonCardStandard>
    </NeonMasonryGrid>
  );
}
```

Dashboard layout with masonry grid:

# NeonMenu

A dropdown menu component that displays a list of options when triggered.

## When To Use

Use the NeonMenu component when you need to:

- Create dropdown menus attached to buttons or other trigger elements
- Provide a list of selectable options in a compact, space-saving format
- Group related actions together under a single interactive control
- Implement navigation menus with links and submenus
- Create context menus for actions related to a specific element
- Present a list of selectable items that should only appear when requested
- Build hierarchical menu structures with nested submenus
- Provide a clean interface for options that don't need to be visible at all times

NeonMenu is designed to be versatile and can be used in conjunction with various trigger elements like buttons or icons. It supports simple lists, dividers, icons, hierarchical submenus, and various customization options.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the menu |
| dataHeaderText | string | Yes | - | Text displayed in the menu header |
| dataShowHeaderText | boolean | No | false | Whether to show the header text |
| dataLabelText | string | No | - | Label text for the menu |
| dataShowLabel | boolean | No | false | Whether to show the label |
| dataHelperText | string | No | - | Helper text for additional information |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Text for the tooltip |
| dataPopperPlacement | string | No | 'bottom-start' | Position where the menu appears relative to the trigger. Options include: 'top', 'top-start', 'top-end', 'right', 'right-start', 'right-end', 'bottom', 'bottom-start', 'bottom-end', 'left', 'left-start', 'left-end' |
| dataAriaLabel | string | No | - | Accessible label for the menu |
| dataTabbableElementsSelector | string | No | - | Selector for tabbable elements within the menu |
| dataIsLabeledWidget | boolean | No | false | Whether the menu is a labeled widget |
| dataPopperMaxHeight | string | No | - | Maximum height of the popper. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large', or a custom value |
| dataRestrictPopperWidth | boolean | No | false | Whether to restrict the popper width to the width of its trigger |
| options | Array<MenuOption \| 'DIVIDER'> | No | - | Array of menu options or dividers |
| context | any | No | - | Context object passed to option callbacks |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Whether the menu is disabled |
| children | React.ReactNode | No | - | Content to display inside the menu |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles for the menu |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| popper-trigger | Yes | Content that triggers the menu to open when clicked |

## MenuOption Interface

The `options` prop accepts an array of `MenuOption` objects or the string 'DIVIDER'. Each `MenuOption` can have these properties:

| Name | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| id | string | Unique identifier for the option |
| text | string | The main text for the menu option |
| textRight | string | Text displayed on the right side |
| subtext | string | Subtitle text displayed below the main text |
| body | string | Additional text content |
| controlType | 'none' \| 'button' \| 'link' \| 'heading' \| 'checkbox' \| 'reset' | Type of control the option represents (default: 'button') |
| url | string | URL for link options |
| openInNewTab | boolean | Whether to open links in a new tab |
| onClickCallback | function | Callback function when the option is clicked |
| menuOptionChildren | Array<MenuOption \| 'DIVIDER'> | Nested submenu options |
| tooltipText | string | Tooltip text for the option |
| isDisabled | function | Function that returns whether the option is disabled |
| disabledTooltipText | string | Tooltip text shown when option is disabled |
| isNested | boolean | Whether the option appears indented |
| isSelected | function | Function that returns whether the option is selected |
| childrenIcon | 'caret-right' \| 'more-horiz' | Icon for indicating children options |
| imageSrc | string | Source URL for an image |
| checkboxPosition | 'left' \| 'right' | Position for checkbox in checkbox options |
| icon | string | Name of the icon to display on the left |
| iconColor | string | Color of the left icon |
| iconColorWeight | number | Weight of the left icon color (default: 500) |
| iconRight | string | Name of the icon to display on the right |
| iconRightColor | string | Color of the right icon |
| iconRightColorWeight | number | Weight of the right icon color (default: 500) |
| showAvatar | boolean | Whether to show an avatar |
| avatarFirstName | string | First name for the avatar |
| avatarLastName | string | Last name for the avatar |
| avatarProfilePictureSrc | string | Image source for the avatar |
| avatarBackgroundOption | string | Background style for the avatar |
| avatarSize | string | Size of the avatar |
| tagText | string | Text for a tag |
| tagSubtext | string | Subtext for the tag |
| tagType | string | Color/type for the tag |
| tagPosition | 'left' \| 'right' | Position of the tag |
| additionalInfo | any | Additional information to store with the option |

## Examples

Simple menu with basic options:

```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonMenu, NeonButton } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function MenuExampleSimple() {
  const menuOptions = [
    {
      id: 'menu-option-1',
      text: 'Option One',
    },
    'DIVIDER',
    {
      id: 'menu-option-2',
      text: 'Option Two',
      icon: 'calendar-note'
    },
    {
      id: 'menu-option-3',
      text: 'Option Three',
      icon: 'build'
    }
  ];

  return (
    <NeonMenu
      id="simple-menu"
      dataHeaderText="Menu Options"
      dataShowHeaderText="false"
      options={menuOptions}
    >
      <div data-slot="popper-trigger">
        <NeonButton
          id="simple-menu-button"
          dataText="Menu"
          dataType="secondary"
          dataIcon="more-vert"
          dataShowText="false"
        />
      </div>
    </NeonMenu>
  );
}
```

Complex menu with nested options and callbacks:

```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonMenu, NeonButton } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function MenuExampleComplex() {
  const menuOptions = [
    {
      id: 'complex-option-1',
      text: 'Option One',
    },
    'DIVIDER',
    {
      id: 'complex-option-2',
      text: 'Option Two',
      icon: 'calendar-note'
    },
    {
      id: 'complex-option-3',
      text: 'Option Three',
      icon: 'build',
      onClickCallback: () => {
        alert('Option Three clicked.');
      },
      menuOptionChildren: [
        {
          icon: 'open-in-new|rtl-flip',
          id: 'child-item-1',
          text: 'Open Google',
          onClickCallback: (menuOption) => {
            window.open(menuOption.url);
          },
          url: 'https://www.google.com/'
        },
        {
          icon: 'clipboard-edit',
          id: 'child-item-2',
          text: 'Edit Document'
        }
      ],
    },
    {
      id: 'complex-option-4',
      text: 'Option Disabled',
      icon: 'build',
      isDisabled: () => true
    }
  ];

  return (
    <NeonMenu
      id="complex-menu"
      dataLabelText="My Menu"
      dataHelperText="Select an option"
      dataTooltipText="Menu options"
      dataShowLabel="true"
      dataPopperPlacement="right"
      dataHeaderText="Available Options"
      dataShowHeaderText="true"
      options={menuOptions}
    >
      <div data-slot="popper-trigger">
        <NeonButton
          id="complex-menu-button"
          dataText="Menu"
          dataType="secondary"
          dataIcon="more-vert"
          dataShowText="true"
        />
      </div>
    </NeonMenu>
  );
}
```

Menu with controlled popper width:

```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonMenu, NeonButton, NeonCheckboxSingle } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function MenuExamplePopperWidth() {
  const [restrictWidth, setRestrictWidth] = useState(true);

  const menuOptions = [
    {
      id: 'width-option-1',
      text: 'Option One with Potentially Long Text',
    },
    'DIVIDER',
    {
      id: 'width-option-2',
      text: 'Option Two',
      icon: 'calendar-note'
    },
    {
      id: 'width-option-3',
      text: 'Option Three with Submenu',
      icon: 'multiplechoice',
      menuOptionChildren: [
        {
          id: 'width-option-3-1',
          text: 'Nested Option 1',
          icon: 'bolt'
        },
        {
          id: 'width-option-3-2',
          text: 'Nested Option 2 with Long Text',
          icon: 'bolt'
        }
      ]
    }
  ];

  return (
    <>
      <NeonMenu
        id="width-menu"
        dataHeaderText="Header Text"
        dataShowHeaderText="false"
        dataRestrictPopperWidth={restrictWidth}
        options={menuOptions}
      >
        <div data-slot="popper-trigger">
          <NeonButton
            id="width-menu-button"
            dataText="Menu"
            dataType="secondary"
            dataIcon="more-vert"
            dataShowText="false"
          />
        </div>
      </NeonMenu>

      <NeonCheckboxSingle
        id="restrict-width"
        dataLabelText="Restrict menu width"
        value={restrictWidth}
        onInput={(event) => {
          setRestrictWidth(event.target.getValue());
        }}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

Menu with customized max height:

```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonMenu, NeonButton, NeonSelectField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function MenuExampleMaxHeight() {
  const [maxHeight, setMaxHeight] = useState();

  const menuOptions = Array.from({ length: 20 }, (_, i) => ({
    id: `height-option-${i+1}`,
    text: `Option ${i+1}`,
    icon: i % 2 === 0 ? 'check' : 'close'
  }));

  return (
    <div className="__neon__form">
      <div className="__neon__form-row">
        <NeonMenu
          id="height-menu"
          dataHeaderText="Many Options"
          dataShowHeaderText="true"
          options={menuOptions}
          dataPopperMaxHeight={maxHeight}
          dataPopperPlacement="bottom-start"
        >
          <div data-slot="popper-trigger">
            <NeonButton
              id="height-menu-button"
              dataText="Menu"
              dataType="secondary"
              dataIcon="more-vert"
              dataShowText="false"
            />
          </div>
        </NeonMenu>

        <NeonSelectField
          id="max-height-select"
          dataLabelText="Menu Max Height"
          options={[
            {text: 'Default', value: ''},
            {text: 'Small', value: 'small'},
            {text: 'Medium', value: 'medium'},
            {text: 'Large', value: 'large'},
          ]}
          modelValue={maxHeight}
          modelValueChange={(newValue) => setMaxHeight(newValue)}
        />
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```


# NeonMessages

A container component for displaying notifications such as toasts and system messages in designated locations on the page.

## When To Use

Use the NeonMessages component when you need to:

- Create a container for system messages that appear at the top of the page
- Create a container for toast notifications that appear within the main content area
- Set up proper notification areas in your application layout
- Establish target containers for programmatically displayed messages
- Ensure notifications are displayed in consistent, accessible locations
- Handle different types of notifications in their appropriate positions

NeonMessages serves as a container that holds notification components (toasts and system messages) in the page chrome. It does not generate notifications itself but provides designated areas where notifications will appear when triggered through their respective APIs.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the messages container. Use DEFAULT_SYSTEM_MESSAGES_FLOATING_ID or DEFAULT_TOAST_MESSAGE_FLOATING_ID constants from exported utils |
| dataType | string | Yes | - | Sets the message target type. Options: 'toast', 'system-floating' |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles for the container |
| children | React.ReactNode | No | - | Content to display inside the messages container (rarely used) |

## Examples

System message container:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonMessages, DEFAULT_SYSTEM_MESSAGES_FLOATING_ID } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function MessagesSystemExample() {
  return (
    <NeonMessages
      id={DEFAULT_SYSTEM_MESSAGES_FLOATING_ID}
      dataType="system-floating"
    />
  );
}
```

Toast message container:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonMessages, DEFAULT_TOAST_MESSAGE_FLOATING_ID } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function MessagesToastExample() {
  return (
    <NeonMessages
      id={DEFAULT_TOAST_MESSAGE_FLOATING_ID}
      dataType="toast"
    />
  );
}
```

Page layout with proper message containers:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import {
  NeonMessages,
  DEFAULT_SYSTEM_MESSAGES_FLOATING_ID,
  DEFAULT_TOAST_MESSAGE_FLOATING_ID
} from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function AppLayout({ children }) {
  return (
    <>
      <header className="__neon__app-header">
        {/* Header content */}
      </header>

      {/* System messages appear above the main content */}
      <NeonMessages
        id={DEFAULT_SYSTEM_MESSAGES_FLOATING_ID}
        dataType="system-floating"
      />

      <main className="__neon__app-layout-main-content">
        {/* Toast messages appear within the main content */}
        <NeonMessages
          id={DEFAULT_TOAST_MESSAGE_FLOATING_ID}
          dataType="toast"
        />

        {children}
      </main>

      <footer className="__neon__app-footer">
        {/* Footer content */}
      </footer>
    </>
  );
}
```

Triggering a system message (to be shown in the system-floating container):
```jsx
import { addSystemMessage } from '@neon/exported-utils';
import { DEFAULT_SYSTEM_MESSAGES_FLOATING_ID } from '@neon/react-adapters';

function showSuccessMessage() {
  addSystemMessage({
    controlConfig: {
      sendTo: DEFAULT_SYSTEM_MESSAGES_FLOATING_ID,
      messageType: 'success',
      title: 'Success',
      autoDismiss: true,
      autoDismissTime: 5000
    },
    message: 'Your changes have been saved successfully.'
  });
}
```

Triggering a toast message (to be shown in the toast container):
```jsx
import { addToastMessage } from '@neon/exported-utils';
import { DEFAULT_TOAST_MESSAGE_FLOATING_ID } from '@neon/react-adapters';

function showInfoToast() {
  addToastMessage({
    controlConfig: {
      sendTo: DEFAULT_TOAST_MESSAGE_FLOATING_ID,
      messageType: 'info',
      autoDismiss: true,
      autoDismissTime: 5000
    },
    message: {
      heading: 'Information',
      subheading: 'This is additional information',
      buttons: [
        {
          id: 'dismiss-btn',
          text: 'Dismiss',
          showText: 'true',
          type: 'borderless',
          click: () => console.log('Toast dismissed')
        }
      ]
    }
  });
}
```


# NeonModalDialog

A dialog component that presents content in a layer that appears above the application, requiring user interaction before returning to the main interface.

## When To Use

Use the NeonModalDialog component when you need to:

- Focus user attention on critical information or actions
- Collect user input through a form without navigating away from the current page
- Confirm a user action before proceeding with a potentially destructive operation
- Display detailed information without cluttering the main interface
- Show warnings or errors that require acknowledgment
- Present a self-contained workflow that must be completed or dismissed
- Create a temporary overlay that blocks interaction with the underlying page
- Request user confirmation or decision while maintaining context of the current page

NeonModalDialog is ideal for important interactions that require full user attention and should interrupt the normal workflow. For less disruptive interactions or side panels, consider using NeonModalDrawer instead. For simple notifications that don't require user action, NeonToast would be more appropriate.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the modal dialog |
| isOpen | boolean | Yes | - | Whether the modal dialog is visible |
| onClose | function | Yes | - | Handler for when the modal is requested to close |
| title | string | No | - | Title text for the modal header |
| size | string | No | 'medium' | Size of the modal. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'x-large' |
| children | React.ReactNode | No | - | Content to display inside the modal body |
| footer | React.ReactNode | No | - | Content to display in the modal footer |
| hideCloseButton | boolean | No | false | Whether to hide the close button in the header |
| closeOnEscape | boolean | No | true | Whether to close the modal when the Escape key is pressed |
| closeOnBackdropClick | boolean | No | true | Whether to close the modal when clicking on the backdrop |
| backdropOpacity | number | No | 0.5 | Opacity level of the background overlay (0-1) |
| zIndex | number | No | 1000 | Z-index level for the modal |
| showScrollbar | boolean | No | false | Whether to show scrollbar for modal content |
| disableBackdrop | boolean | No | false | Whether to disable the backdrop overlay |
| fullWidth | boolean | No | false | Whether the modal should take up the full available width |
| fullHeight | boolean | No | false | Whether the modal should take up the full available height |
| centerContent | boolean | No | false | Whether to center the content vertically and horizontally |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name for the modal |
| headerClassName | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name for the modal header |
| bodyClassName | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name for the modal body |
| footerClassName | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name for the modal footer |
| onAfterClose | function | No | - | Handler called after the modal has closed and transitions are complete |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |
| ariaLabelledBy | string | No | - | ID of the element that labels the modal for accessibility |
| ariaDescribedBy | string | No | - | ID of the element that describes the modal for accessibility |

## Examples

Basic modal dialog:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonModalDialog, NeonButton } from '@neon/react-adapters';

function BasicModalDialogExample() {
  const [isModalOpen, setIsModalOpen] = useState(false);
  
  return (
    <>
      <NeonButton
        id="open-modal-button"
        onClick={() => setIsModalOpen(true)}
        dataLabel="Open Modal"
      />
      
      <NeonModalDialog
        id="basic-modal"
        isOpen={isModalOpen}
        onClose={() => setIsModalOpen(false)}
        title="Important Information"
      >
        <p>This is a basic modal dialog with important information for the user.</p>
        <p>The user must close this modal to continue using the application.</p>
      </NeonModalDialog>
    </>
  );
}
```

Confirmation modal with custom footer:
```jsx

  size="small"

      />
      <NeonButton
        id="confirm-button"
        dataLabel="Delete"
        dataVariant="danger"

>

</NeonModalDialog>
```


# NeonModalDrawer

A slide-in panel component that displays content and controls on the side of the screen without navigating away from the current page.

## When To Use

Use the NeonModalDrawer component when you need to:

- Display supplementary content without leaving the current page
- Show forms or detailed information that requires more space than a popup
- Create multi-step workflows that should remain in context of the current page
- Collect user input without a full page transition
- Present detailed information that doesn't warrant a full page
- Provide temporary navigation or filtering options
- Show contextual details for an item from a list or table
- Create a temporary workspace that doesn't interrupt the main workflow
- Allow users to perform secondary tasks while maintaining their current context
- Implement progressive disclosure of complex interfaces

NeonModalDrawer is designed for displaying content that complements the main page. For modals that should appear centered on the screen, consider using NeonModalDialog instead.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the drawer |
| children | React.ReactNode | No | - | Content to display inside the drawer |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| dataAnimate | boolean | No | true | If set to true, will have the drawer slide or fade in |
| dataInjectionSpacing | boolean | No | true | Adds padding to the drawer-body slot when true |
| dataCloseOnBackdropClick | boolean | No | false | When true, closes the drawer on backdrop click |
| dataBypassFocusTrap | boolean | No | false | When true, disables the focus trap. Only use for specific bugs |
| neonDrawerHasClosed | function | Yes | - | Function called after the close animation completes |
| dataResponsiveImage | boolean | No | true | When true, images in the drawer will be responsive |
| dataShowHeaderDivider | boolean | No | true | Shows a divider below the header when true |
| dataShowPreBodyDivider | boolean | No | true | Shows a divider below the pre-body when true |
| dataShowPostBodyDivider | boolean | No | true | Shows a divider above the post-body when true |
| dataShowFooterDivider | boolean | No | true | Shows a divider above the footer when true |
| dataSize | string | No | 'auto' | Size of the drawer. Options: 'x-small', 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'x-large', 'auto' |
| preCloseCallback | function | No | - | Function called before closing. Return true to prevent closing |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| drawer-header-title | No | The space where the drawer header text will be displayed |
| drawer-pre-body | No | The slot for custom content right above the drawer-body |
| drawer-body | Yes | The slot for the main drawer custom content |
| drawer-post-body | No | The slot for custom content right below the drawer-body |
| drawer-footer-content | No | (Deprecated) Use drawer-button-footer with NeonButtonFooter instead |
| drawer-button-footer | No | Contains a single NeonButtonFooter |

## Examples

Basic modal drawer:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonModalDrawer } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ModalDrawerExample() {
  const [showDrawer, setShowDrawer] = useState(false);

  return (
    <>
      <NeonButton
        id="open-drawer-button"
        dataText="Open Drawer"
        onClick={() => setShowDrawer(true)}
      />

      {showDrawer && (
        <NeonModalDrawer
          id="example-drawer"
          dataAnimate="true"
          neonDrawerHasClosed={() => {
            setShowDrawer(false);
          }}
        >
          <div data-slot="drawer-header-title">
            Drawer Title
          </div>
          <div data-slot="drawer-body">
            <p className="__neon__text">This is the main content of the drawer.</p>
            <p className="__neon__text">You can put any content here.</p>
          </div>
          <div data-slot="drawer-footer-content">
            <div className="__neon__button-layout">
              <NeonButton
                id="close-dialog-button"
                dataText="Close"
                dataType="primary"
                onClick={(event) => {
                  event.target.dispatchEvent(new Event('neonDrawerClose', {bubbles: true}));
                }}
              />
            </div>
          </div>
        </NeonModalDrawer>
      )}
    </>
  );
}
```

Drawer with button footer:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonModalDrawer, NeonButton, NeonButtonFooter } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ModalDrawerExampleButtonFooter() {
  const [showDrawer, setShowDrawer] = useState(false);

  return (
    <>
      <NeonButton
        id="open-drawer-button"
        dataText="Launch modal drawer"
        onClick={() => setShowDrawer(true)}
      />

      {showDrawer && (
        <NeonModalDrawer
          id="example-drawer"
          dataAnimate="true"
          neonDrawerHasClosed={() => {
            setShowDrawer(false);
          }}
        >
          <div data-slot="drawer-header-title">
            Drawer with Button Footer
          </div>
          <div data-slot="drawer-body">
            <p className="__neon__text">This example uses the recommended drawer-button-footer slot with NeonButtonFooter.</p>
          </div>
          <div data-slot="drawer-button-footer">
            <NeonButtonFooter
              id="button-footer"
              tertiaryButton={{
                id: 'previous-button',
                text: 'Previous',
                type: 'tertiary',
                onClick: (event) => console.log(event)
              }}
              buttons={[
                {
                  id: 'cancel-button',
                  text: 'Cancel',
                  type: 'borderless',
                  onClick: (event) => {
                    event.target.dispatchEvent(new Event('neonDrawerClose', {bubbles: true}));
                  }
                },
              ]}
              primaryButton={{
                id: 'save-button',
                text: 'Save',
                type: 'primary',
                onClick: (event) => {
                  event.target.dispatchEvent(new Event('neonDrawerClose', {bubbles: true}));
                }
              }}
            />
          </div>
        </NeonModalDrawer>
      )}
    </>
  );
}
```

Drawer with pre-close callback:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonCheckboxSingle, NeonModalDrawer } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ModalDrawerExamplePreCloseCallback() {
  const [showDrawer, setShowDrawer] = useState(false);
  const [preventClosing, setPreventClosing] = useState(true);

  return (
    <>
      <NeonButton
        id="open-drawer-button"
        dataText="Open Drawer"
        onClick={() => setShowDrawer(true)}
      />

      {showDrawer && (
        <NeonModalDrawer
          id="example-drawer"
          neonDrawerHasClosed={() => {
            setShowDrawer(false);
          }}
          preCloseCallback={() => {
            return preventClosing; // Return true to prevent closing
          }}
        >
          <div data-slot="drawer-header-title">
            Pre-Close Callback Example
          </div>
          <div data-slot="drawer-body">
            <p className="__neon__text">
              You can stop the drawer from closing using the preCloseCallback.
              You can also have the function return a Promise that resolves to a boolean
              if you need asynchronous behavior. Return, or resolve, true to prevent
              the drawer from closing.
            </p>

            <NeonCheckboxSingle
              id="prevent-closing"
              dataLabelText="Prevent Closing"
              value={preventClosing}
              onInput={(event) => {
                setPreventClosing(event.target.getValue());
              }}
            />
          </div>
          <div data-slot="drawer-footer-content">
            <div className="__neon__button-layout">
              <NeonButton
                id="close-drawer-button"
                dataText="Close"
                dataType="primary"
                onClick={(event) => {
                  if (!preventClosing) {
                    event.target.dispatchEvent(new Event('neonDrawerClose', {bubbles: true}));
                  }
                }}
              />
            </div>
          </div>
        </NeonModalDrawer>
      )}
    </>
  );
}
```

Drawer with multiple slots:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonModalDrawer } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ModalDrawerExampleAllSlots() {
  const [showDrawer, setShowDrawer] = useState(false);

  return (
    <>
      <NeonButton
        id="open-drawer-button"
        dataText="Open Drawer"
        onClick={() => setShowDrawer(true)}
      />

      {showDrawer && (
        <NeonModalDrawer
          id="all-slots-drawer"
          dataAnimate="true"
          neonDrawerHasClosed={() => {
            setShowDrawer(false);
          }}
        >
          <div data-slot="drawer-header-title">
            Drawer with Multiple Slots
          </div>
          <div data-slot="drawer-pre-body">
            <p className="__neon__text">This content appears in the drawer-pre-body slot.</p>
          </div>
          <div data-slot="drawer-body">
            <p className="__neon__text">This is the main content in the drawer-body slot.</p>
            <p className="__neon__text">The drawer-body slot is required and contains the primary content.</p>
          </div>
          <div data-slot="drawer-post-body">
            <p className="__neon__text">This content appears in the drawer-post-body slot.</p>
          </div>
          <div data-slot="drawer-button-footer">
            <NeonButtonFooter
              id="button-footer"
              buttons={[
                {
                  id: 'cancel-button',
                  text: 'Cancel',
                  type: 'borderless',
                  onClick: (event) => {
                    event.target.dispatchEvent(new Event('neonDrawerClose', {bubbles: true}));
                  }
                }
              ]}
              primaryButton={{
                id: 'primary-button',
                text: 'Primary',
                type: 'primary',
                onClick: () => console.log('Primary clicked')
              }}
            />
          </div>
        </NeonModalDrawer>
      )}
    </>
  );
}
```




# NeonMultiSelectField

A form component that allows users to select multiple options from a dropdown list, with advanced filtering and grouping capabilities.

## When To Use

Use the NeonMultiSelectField component when you need to:

- Allow users to select multiple items from a predefined list of options
- Present a large number of options in a compact dropdown format
- Group related options hierarchically with nested selections
- Enable quick filtering of available options
- Display selected options as interactive chips
- Provide a select-all capability for efficient bulk selection
- Create forms that require multi-option selection fields
- Support complex selection scenarios with intermediate selection states
- Implement searchable dropdowns for finding specific options quickly
- Present option lists that may include avatars or helper text

NeonMultiSelectField is the preferred component for any form that requires users to select multiple items from a predefined set of options. For single selection scenarios, consider using NeonSelectField instead.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the field |
| dataLabelText | string | Yes | - | Label text for the field |
| options | Array<MultiSelectOption> | Yes | - | Array of options to display in the dropdown |
| modelValue | Array<string> \| undefined | Yes | - | Currently selected option values |
| modelValueChange | (value: Array<string> \| undefined) => void | Yes | - | Callback when selected options change |
| dataSize | string | No | 'auto' | Sets the width of field. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'x-large', 'auto' |
| dataChipSetIsDisableOverflowMenu | boolean | No | false | Disables the overflow menu and lets chips overflow |
| dataShowSelectedItemsList | boolean | No | true | Shows/hides the selected option chips |
| dataDropDownText | string | No | 'Select' | Text displayed on the dropdown button |
| dataUseIntermediateSelection | boolean | No | false | Provides an intermediate selection state with Apply and Cancel buttons |
| dataPopperPlacement | string | No | 'bottom-start' | Sets the popover position. Options: 'top-start', 'top-end', 'bottom-start', 'bottom-end', 'left-start', 'left', 'left-end', 'right-start', 'right', 'right-end' |
| dataShowFilter | boolean | No | false | Shows a filter input box to filter the options |
| dataShowSelectAll | boolean | No | false | Shows a select-all checkbox |
| dataIsLoading | boolean | No | false | Shows the loading indicator and disables the field |
| dataPopperMaxHeight | string | No | - | Sets the max height of the popper. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large', or CSS length |
| dataModalType | string | No | 'auto' | Determines if options show as drawer or dialog. Options: 'auto', 'drawer', 'dialog' |
| dataModalThreshold | number | No | 100 | Number of options that triggers the modal display instead of popper |
| dataChipSetEnableClearAll | boolean \| 'auto' | No | 'auto' | Controls when the clear-all button shows in the chip-set |
| dataChipSetClearAllThreshold | number | No | 100 | When chips exceed this number, clear-all button appears (when enabled) |
| dataSelectAllText | string | No | - | Sets the "Select All" text for the multi-select popper |
| dataSelectAllSubtextMessageKey | string | No | - | Message key for translating options count text |
| dataShowLabel | boolean | No | true | Whether to show the label |
| dataHelperText | string | No | - | Explanatory text below the field |
| dataIsRequired | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is required |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Text to show in tooltip |
| dataIsFieldOnly | boolean | No | false | When true, hides the label and other surroundings |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is disabled |
| dataIsReadOnly | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is read-only |
| onBlur | (event: Event) => void | No | - | Callback when field loses focus |
| neonPopperClose | (event: Event) => void | No | - | Callback when the popper is closed |
| customValidationFunction | Function | No | - | Custom function for field validation |

## Examples

Simple multi-select field example:
```jsx
import React, {useState, useMemo} from 'react';
import {NeonMultiSelectField} from '@neon/react-adapters';
import {type MultiSelectOption} from '@neon/interfaces';

export function MultiSelectFieldExample() {
  // Pre-populate the selected options
  const [selectedBrands, setSelectedBrands] = useState(['guitar-brand-1', 'guitar-brand-3']);

  // Define the options
  const guitarBrands = useMemo(() => {
    return [{
      id: '__mfe__gb-1',
      name: 'guitar-brand-1',
      labelText: 'Fender'
    }, {
      id: '__mfe__gb-2',
      name: 'guitar-brand-2',
      labelText: 'Gibson'
    }, {
      id: '__mfe__bg-3',
      name: 'guitar-brand-3',
      labelText: 'Ibanez'
    }];
  }, []);

  return (
    <NeonMultiSelectField
      id="__mfe__select-guitar-brand"
      dataLabelText="Choose Guitar Brand"
      options={guitarBrands}
      modelValue={selectedBrands}
      modelValueChange={(brand) => { setSelectedBrands(brand); }}
    />
  );
}
```

Complex multi-select field with additional options:
```jsx
import React, {useState, useMemo} from 'react';
import {NeonMultiSelectField} from '@neon/react-adapters';
import {type MultiSelectOption} from '@neon/interfaces';

export function MultiSelectFieldExampleComplex() {
  // Pre-populate selected options
  const [selectedMakes, setSelectedMakes] = useState(['111111', '222222']);

  // Define options with helper text
  const makes = useMemo(() => {
    return [{
      id: '__mfe__make-1',
      name: '111111',
      labelText: 'Toyota',
      helperText: 'You Got It!'
    }, {
      id: '__mfe__make-2',
      name: '222222',
      labelText: 'Honda',
      helperText: 'The Power of Dreams'
    }, {
      id: '__mfe__make-4',
      name: '333333',
      labelText: 'Ford'
    }, {
      id: '__mfe__make-5',
      name: '444444',
      labelText: 'Ferrari'
    }];
  }, []);

  return (
    <NeonMultiSelectField
      id="__mfe__multi-select-complex-1"
      dataLabelText="Select Make"
      dataDropDownText="Make"
      dataTooltipText="Please select the automobile manufacturer"
      dataShowLabel="true"
      dataIsRequired="true"
      dataIsFieldOnly="true"
      dataHelperText="This is the helper text"
      options={makes}
      modelValue={selectedMakes}
      modelValueChange={(make) => { setSelectedMakes(make); }}
    />
  );
}
```

Multi-select field with select-all and hierarchical options:
```jsx
import React, {useState, useMemo} from 'react';
import {NeonMultiSelectField} from '@neon/react-adapters';
import {type MultiSelectOption} from '@neon/interfaces';

export function MultiSelectFieldSelectAllExample() {
  // Pre-populate selected options
  const [selectedBrands, setSelectedBrands] = useState(['guitar-brand-1', 'guitar-brand-3']);

  // Define hierarchical options
  const options = useMemo(() => {
    return [{
      id: '__mfe__item-1',
      name: 'guitar',
      labelText: 'Guitar',
      children: [{
        id: '__mfe__gt-1',
        name: 'guitar-brand-1',
        labelText: 'Fender'
      }, {
        id: '__mfe__gt-2',
        name: 'guitar-brand-2',
        labelText: 'Gibson'
      }, {
        id: '__mfe__gt-3',
        name: 'guitar-brand-3',
        labelText: 'Ibanez'
      }]
    }, {
      id: '__mfe__item-2',
      name: 'cars',
      labelText: 'Cars',
      children: [{
        id: '__mfe__cb-1',
        name: 'car-brand-1',
        labelText: 'Toyota'
      }, {
        id: '__mfe__cb-2',
        name: 'car-brand-2',
        labelText: 'Honda'
      }, {
        id: '__mfe__cb-3',
        name: 'car-brand-3',
        labelText: 'Ford'
      }]
    }];
  }, []);

  return (
    <NeonMultiSelectField
      id="__mfe__select-guitar-brand"
      dataLabelText="Choose Brand"
      options={options}
      modelValue={selectedBrands}
      dataShowSelectAll="true"
      dataShowFilter="true"
      modelValueChange={(brand) => { setSelectedBrands(brand); }}
    />
  );
}
```

Multi-select field with intermediate selection:
```jsx
import React, {useState, useMemo} from 'react';
import {NeonMultiSelectField} from '@neon/react-adapters';
import {type MultiSelectOption} from '@neon/interfaces';

export function MultiSelectFieldExampleIntermediateSelection() {
  const [selectedOptions, setSelectedOptions] = useState(['option1', 'option3']);
  
  const options = useMemo(() => [
    { id: 'opt1', name: 'option1', labelText: 'Option 1' },
    { id: 'opt2', name: 'option2', labelText: 'Option 2' },
    { id: 'opt3', name: 'option3', labelText: 'Option 3' },
    { id: 'opt4', name: 'option4', labelText: 'Option 4' }
  ], []);

  return (
    <NeonMultiSelectField
      id="intermediate-selection-field"
      dataLabelText="Select Options"
      options={options}
      modelValue={selectedOptions}
      dataUseIntermediateSelection="true"
      modelValueChange={(value) => setSelectedOptions(value)}
    />
  );
}
```


# NeonNumberField

A form input component for capturing and validating numeric values with support for integers, decimals, and various validation constraints.

## When To Use

Use the NeonNumberField component when you need to:

- Collect numeric input from users in forms
- Restrict input to numeric values only (integers or decimals)
- Apply validation rules for number ranges (min/max values)
- Control the number of decimal places allowed
- Set constraints on the length of numeric input
- Create accessible numeric form fields with appropriate labeling
- Integrate numeric validation into larger forms
- Display validation feedback for numeric values
- Handle empty, null, or undefined number values appropriately

NeonNumberField is ideal for scenarios like quantity inputs, financial values, measurements, ages, counts, and other numeric data entry needs. For text input that shouldn't be restricted to numbers, use NeonTextField instead.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the field |
| modelValue | number \| undefined | Yes | - | The current value of the field |
| modelValueChange | (value: number \| undefined) => void | Yes | - | Callback function called when the value changes |
| dataLabelText | string | Yes | - | The label text for the field |
| dataHelperText | string | No | - | Helper text displayed below the field |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Text displayed in a tooltip when hovering over the field |
| dataIsRequired | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is required |
| dataHideRequiredBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to hide the required indicator |
| dataShowOptionalBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to show an optional indicator |
| dataShowLabel | boolean | No | true | Whether to display the label |
| dataAriaLabel | string | No | - | Accessible label for screen readers |
| dataPlaceholderText | string | No | - | Placeholder text shown when field is empty |
| autocomplete | string | No | - | HTML autocomplete attribute value |
| dataIsInteger | boolean | No | false | When true, forces the value to be an integer |
| dataMinLength | number | No | - | Minimum number of digits required |
| dataMaxLength | number | No | - | Maximum number of digits allowed |
| dataMinValue | number | No | - | Minimum value allowed (inclusive) |
| dataMaxValue | number | No | - | Maximum value allowed (inclusive) |
| dataMinValueExclusive | number | No | - | Minimum value allowed (exclusive) |
| dataMaxValueExclusive | number | No | - | Maximum value allowed (exclusive) |
| dataMaxDecimals | number | No | - | Maximum number of decimal places allowed |
| dataSize | string | No | 'auto' | Field width. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'x-large', 'auto' |
| dataIsReadOnly | boolean | No | false | When true, field is read-only |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | When true, field is disabled |
| dataSuccessMessage | string | No | - | Message displayed on successful validation |
| onBlur | function | No | - | Function called when the field loses focus |
| customValidationFunction | function | No | - | Custom validation function for advanced validation rules |
| blurInterceptor | function | No | - | Function called before the blur event is processed |

## Examples

Simple number field:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonNumberField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function NumberFieldExampleSimple() {
  const [bookCount, setBookCount] = useState();

  return (
    <NeonNumberField
      id="book-count"
      dataLabelText="How many books are there?"
      dataShowLabel="false"
      modelValue={bookCount}
      modelValueChange={(count) => { setBookCount(count); }}
    />
  );
}
```

Form field with validation:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonNumberField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function NumberFieldExampleFormField() {
  const [studentCount, setStudentCount] = useState();

  return (
    <NeonNumberField
      id="number-of-students"
      dataLabelText="Number of Students"
      dataShowLabel="true"
      dataHelperText="How many students do you have?"
      dataIsInteger="true"
      dataIsRequired="true"
      modelValue={studentCount}
      modelValueChange={(count) => { setStudentCount(count); }}
    />
  );
}
```

Field with number constraints:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonNumberField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function NumberFieldExampleConstraints() {
  const [temperature, setTemperature] = useState(98.6);

  return (
    <NeonNumberField
      id="temperature"
      dataLabelText="Body Temperature (°F)"
      dataHelperText="Enter temperature between 97.0 and 104.0"
      dataMinValue={97.0}
      dataMaxValue={104.0}
      dataMaxDecimals={1}
      modelValue={temperature}
      modelValueChange={(value) => { setTemperature(value); }}
    />
  );
}
```

Field with custom validation:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonNumberField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function NumberFieldExampleCustomValidation() {
  const [evenNumber, setEvenNumber] = useState();

  // Custom validation to ensure only even numbers are allowed
  const validateEvenNumber = (value, condition, context) => {
    const num = Number(String(context.parsedNumber).split('.')[0]);
    const isValid = num % 2 === 0;

    return {
      isValid,
      errorMessage: isValid ? undefined : 'Please enter an even number'
    };
  };

  return (
    <NeonNumberField
      id="even-number"
      dataLabelText="Enter an even number"
      dataIsInteger="true"
      dataIsRequired="true"
      modelValue={evenNumber}
      modelValueChange={(value) => { setEvenNumber(value); }}
      customValidationFunction={validateEvenNumber}
    />
  );
}
```


# NeonPageHeader

A component for displaying page headers with customizable elements like headings, subheadings, icons, avatars, and more.

## When To Use

Use the NeonPageHeader component when you need to:

- Create a consistent heading section at the top of your pages
- Display a page title with optional subheading
- Include interactive elements alongside page titles
- Add visual elements like avatars, icons, or illustrations to your page headers
- Provide clear page context and navigation options
- Create a branded and visually appealing page introduction
- Include action buttons or tags related to the page's content
- Establish a visual hierarchy between different sections of your application

NeonPageHeader is the primary component for creating consistent page headers throughout your application. It provides a standardized way to display page titles along with supporting visuals and actions.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the page header |
| dataHeading | string | Yes | - | The primary heading of the page |
| dataSubheading | string | No | - | The optional page subheading |
| dataTextColor | string | No | - | Set to 'white' when using the themed gradient background on primary pages |
| dataUseComponentSpacingInline | boolean | No | true | Removes inline (left, right) spacing when false |
| dataUseComponentSpacingBlock | boolean | No | true | Removes block (top, bottom) spacing when false |
| dataShowAvatar | boolean | No | false | When true will force the avatar to render in its placeholder state |
| dataAvatarFirstName | string | No | - | The first name of the user for the avatar |
| dataAvatarLastName | string | No | - | The last name of the user for the avatar |
| dataAvatarBackgroundOption | string | No | - | Sets the background color manually when using only initials. Options: '0', '1', '3', '4', 'high-contrast', 'theme' |
| dataAvatarProfilePictureSrc | string | No | - | The profile picture source for the avatar |
| dataIllustrationSimple | string | No | - | The name of the illustration to display |
| dataIconStackIcon | string | No | - | The icon to display in the icon stack |
| dataIconStackColor | string | No | 'gray' | The color of the icon stack. Options: 'magenta', 'red', 'orange', 'yellow', 'green', 'teal', 'cyan', 'purple', 'gray' |
| dataIconStackShape | string | No | 'circle' | The background shape of the Icon Stack. Options: 'square', 'circle', 'diamond', 'hexagon' |
| dataImgSrc | string | No | - | The image source for the page header |
| children | React.ReactNode | No | - | Content to display in the slots |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| page-header-left | No | This slot's content is placed after the heading |
| page-header-right | No | This slot's content is placed on the right |

## Examples

Basic page header with heading:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonPageHeader } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function PageHeaderExample() {
  return (
    <NeonPageHeader
      dataHeading="A Heading is required for the page-header component"
    />
  );
}
```

Page header with heading and subheading:
```jsx

import { NeonPageHeader } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function PageHeaderWithSubheadingExample() {
  return (
    <NeonPageHeader
      dataHeading="A Heading is required for the page-header component"
      dataSubheading="The subheading is optional"
    />
  );
}
```

Page header with slots for additional content:
```jsx

export function PageHeaderWithSlotsExample() {
  return (
    <NeonPageHeader
      dataHeading="This is an example heading"
      dataSubheading="This is an optional subheading">
      <div data-slot="page-header-left">
        <div className="__neon__wrapper" data-gap="small">
          <NeonTag dataText="Example" dataType="green"></NeonTag>
          <NeonTag dataText="Tags"></NeonTag>
        </div>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="page-header-right">
        <div className="__neon__wrapper" data-gap="small">
          <NeonButton id="share-button" dataText="Share" dataIcon="send" dataShowTextMobile="false"></NeonButton>
          <NeonButton id="download-button" dataText="Download" dataIcon="cloud-download" dataShowTextMobile="false"></NeonButton>
        </div>
      </div>
    </NeonPageHeader>
  );
}
```
