# NeonPagination

A pagination component that allows users to navigate through large sets of data by splitting content into separate pages.

## When To Use

Use the NeonPagination component when you need to:

- Break large datasets into manageable, discrete pages
- Improve user experience by limiting the amount of data displayed at one time
- Allow users to navigate between pages of content
- Display navigation controls for moving between pages of data
- Enable users to select how many items to display per page
- Provide a way to jump directly to a specific page
- Show the current page position relative to the total dataset
- Create data tables with page-by-page navigation
- Implement search result pages with multiple entries
- Build interfaces for large collections of items that should be displayed in chunks

NeonPagination is a flexible component that provides various configuration options for controlling how users navigate through data. It automatically adapts to available space, making it suitable for responsive layouts.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the pagination component |
| dataArrayLength | number | Yes | - | The total length of data to paginate over |
| dataCurrentPage | number | No | 1 | Sets the initial/current page |
| dataPageLength | number | No | 25 | Sets the number of items displayed per page |
| dataUseComponentSpacing | boolean | No | true | When true, applies padding to the component. Set to false to remove padding |
| dataShowJumpTo | boolean | No | true | Controls display of the "Jump to Page" input |
| dataShowResults | boolean | No | true | Controls display of the result information string |
| dataShowPageSizeSelect | boolean | No | true | Controls display of the page size selection dropdown |
| dataShowPageNumbers | boolean | No | true | Controls display of page numbers. When false, only shows results between navigation buttons |
| dataShowSinglePage | boolean | No | true | When false, hides all controls when there is only one page of data |
| dataPageSizeOptions | string | No | "25,50,75,100" | Comma-separated list of page size options |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles |
| neonPaginationChange | function | No | - | Callback triggered when page or page size changes: `(newPage: number, newPageLength: number, getPaginatedData: (data: Array<any>) => Array<any>) => void` |

## Events

| Name | Description |
|------|-------------|
| neonPaginationChange | Fires when the page size, current page, or page size selection changes. The event detail contains page number, page length, and a helper function to paginate data |

## Examples

Basic pagination with data binding:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonPagination } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function PaginationExample() {
  const myData = Array.from({ length: 100 }, (_, i) => `Item ${i + 1}`);
  const [currentPage, setCurrentPage] = useState(1);
  const [pageLength, setPageLength] = useState(25);
  const [paginatedData, setPaginatedData] = useState(myData.slice(0, pageLength));

  return (
    <div>
      <ul>
        {paginatedData.map((item, index) => (
          <li key={index}>{item}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>

      <NeonPagination
        id="pagination-example"
        dataArrayLength={myData.length}
        dataCurrentPage={currentPage}
        dataPageLength={pageLength}
        neonPaginationChange={(newPage, newPageLength, getPaginatedData) => {
          setCurrentPage(newPage);
          setPageLength(newPageLength);
          setPaginatedData(getPaginatedData(myData));
        }}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

Customized pagination with hidden elements:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonPagination } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CustomizedPaginationExample() {
  const totalItems = 500;
  const [currentPage, setCurrentPage] = useState(1);
  const [pageLength, setPageLength] = useState(25);

  return (
    <NeonPagination
      id="customized-pagination"
      dataArrayLength={totalItems}
      dataCurrentPage={currentPage}
      dataPageLength={pageLength}
      dataShowJumpTo={false}
      dataShowPageSizeSelect={true}
      dataShowResults={true}
      dataShowPageNumbers={true}
      dataUseComponentSpacing={false}
      neonPaginationChange={(newPage, newPageLength) => {
        setCurrentPage(newPage);
        setPageLength(newPageLength);
        // Fetch or update data based on new page parameters
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Pagination with custom page size options:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonPagination } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function CustomPageSizeOptionsExample() {
  const [currentPage, setCurrentPage] = useState(1);
  const [pageLength, setPageLength] = useState(10);

  return (
    <NeonPagination
      id="custom-page-sizes"
      dataArrayLength={200}
      dataCurrentPage={currentPage}
      dataPageLength={pageLength}
      dataPageSizeOptions="5,10,20,50"
      neonPaginationChange={(newPage, newPageLength) => {
        setCurrentPage(newPage);
        setPageLength(newPageLength);
        // Update your data based on the new parameters
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Hiding pagination when only one page is present:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonPagination } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function SinglePageHideExample() {
  // Only 10 items, with 25 per page means only one page will be needed
  const smallDataset = 10;

  return (
    <NeonPagination
      id="hide-single-page-example"
      dataArrayLength={smallDataset}
      dataPageLength={25}
      dataShowSinglePage={false}
      neonPaginationChange={(newPage, newPageLength) => {
        // Handle page change (won't be triggered if controls are hidden)
      }}
    />
  );
}
```


# NeonPopover

A versatile popover component that displays content in a floating container triggered by user interaction, with support for various positioning options and customizable behavior.

## When To Use

Use the NeonPopover component when you need to:

- Display additional information or controls when a user interacts with a trigger element
- Create dropdown menus or context menus
- Show tooltips with rich content
- Implement advanced form controls like date pickers or color selectors
- Display supplementary content without navigating away from the current view
- Reveal information on-demand to reduce initial visual complexity
- Create interactive overlays that appear above the main content
- Implement multi-level navigation or option selection
- Display additional options or actions that don't fit in the primary UI

NeonPopover is a flexible overlay component that can be positioned around a trigger element. It provides a container for displaying any content, from simple text to complex interactive elements like forms, while maintaining proper positioning and focus management.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the popover |
| dataLabelText | string | No | - | Label text for the popover |
| dataHelperText | string | No | - | Helper text shown below the popover |
| dataShowHeaderText | boolean | No | true | Whether to show the header section text |
| dataPopperPlacement | string | No | 'bottom' | Placement of the popup when it opens. Options: 'top', 'top-start', 'top-end', 'right', 'right-start', 'right-end', 'bottom', 'bottom-start', 'bottom-end', 'left', 'left-start', 'left-end' |
| dataShowLabel | boolean | No | - | Whether to show the label |
| dataAriaLabel | string | No | - | ARIA label for accessibility |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Text for the tooltip |
| dataTabbableElementsSelector | string | No | - | CSS selector for tabbable elements within the popover |
| dataInjectionSpacing | boolean | No | true | When set to false, removes the left and right spacing |
| dataConstrainPopper | boolean | No | true | When set to false, sets the popper max-width and max-height to the screen width and height |
| dataRestrictPopperWidth | boolean | No | false | When true, the popper will be as wide as the popover trigger |
| dataPopperClass | string | No | - | Adds the given class to the popper element for custom styling |
| dataShowPopperArrow | boolean | No | true | Controls the visibility of the arrow on the popper |
| dataCloseOnPopperClick | boolean | No | true | When true, the popper closes when popover content is clicked |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Whether the popover is disabled |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| children | React.ReactNode | No | - | Content for the popover slots |
| neonPopperOpen | function | No | - | Event fired when the popper is opened |
| neonPopperClose | function | No | - | Event fired when the popper is closed |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| popper-body | Yes | The main content of the popover |
| popper-header | No | The header content of the popover |
| popper-trigger | No | The element that triggers the popover to open |

## Examples

Simple popover example:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonPopover } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function PopoverExampleSimple() {
  return (
    <NeonPopover id="example-popover" dataShowHeaderText="false">
      <h2 data-slot="popper-header">This is a header</h2>
      <div data-slot="popper-body">
        <p className="__neon__text">
          This is the content of the popover. It can contain any type of content,
          from simple text to complex interactive elements.
        </p>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="popper-trigger">
        <NeonButton
          id="popover-trigger-button"
          dataIcon="menu-book"
          dataText="Open Popover" />
      </div>
    </NeonPopover>
  );
}
```

Popover with interactive content:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonPopover } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function PopoverExampleWithButton() {
  return (
    <NeonPopover id="popover-with-button">
      <h2 data-slot="popper-header">Interactive Content</h2>
      <div data-slot="popper-body">
        <div data-neon-prevent-closing>
          <NeonButton
            id="popover-inner-button"
            dataText="This Won't Close The Popover"
            onClick={() => {
              alert('Button clicked!');
            }}
          />
        </div>
        <p className="__neon__text">
          The button above has data-neon-prevent-closing so it won't close the popover when clicked.
        </p>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="popper-trigger">
        <NeonButton
          id="popover-trigger-button"
          dataText="Show Popover With Button"
        />
      </div>
    </NeonPopover>
  );
}
```

Popover with date picker:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonPopover, NeonDatePicker } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function PopoverExampleDatePicker() {
  const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState();

  return (
    <NeonPopover
      id="date-picker-popover"
      dataConstrainPopper="false"
      dataShowHeaderText="false"
    >
      <div data-slot="popper-body">
        <div data-neon-prevent-closing>
          <NeonDatePicker
            id="popover-date-picker"
            dataMonth={1}
            dataYear={2023}
            dataMode="single"
            singleModeValue={selectedDate}
            neonDatePickerSingleDateChanged={(date) => {
              setSelectedDate(date);
            }}
          />
        </div>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="popper-trigger">
        <NeonButton
          id="date-picker-trigger"
          dataIcon="calendar"
          dataText="Select Date"
        />
      </div>
    </NeonPopover>
  );
}
```

External closing of popover:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonPopover, NeonDatePicker } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { closePopperById } from '@neon/exported-utils';

export function PopoverExampleExternalClose() {
  const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState();

  return (
    <NeonPopover
      id="external-close-popover"
      dataShowHeaderText="false"
      dataConstrainPopper="false"
    >
      <div data-slot="popper-body">
        <div data-neon-prevent-closing>
          <NeonDatePicker
            id="external-close-date-picker"
            dataMode="single"
            singleModeValue={selectedDate}
            neonDatePickerSingleDateChanged={(date) => {
              setSelectedDate(date);
              // Close the popover programmatically
              closePopperById('external-close-popover');
            }}
          />
        </div>
      </div>
      <div data-slot="popper-trigger">
        <NeonButton
          id="external-close-trigger"
          dataIcon="calendar"
          dataText="Select Date"
        />
      </div>
    </NeonPopover>
  );
}
```


# NeonProfileHeaderGreeting

A component that displays a personalized greeting with user information, including an avatar and optional text elements.

## When To Use

Use the NeonProfileHeaderGreeting component when you need to:

- Display a personalized greeting to a user
- Show user profile information in a header section
- Present a user's avatar alongside greeting text
- Display user identification information such as ID numbers
- Provide contextual information like date and time
- Create a welcoming message for dashboards or profile pages
- Indicate the logged-in user with their profile details

NeonProfileHeaderGreeting is designed to work in conjunction with the NeonProfileHeader component, typically placed in its "start" slot for a consistent layout.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | No | - | Unique identifier for the component |
| dataHeading | string | Yes | - | The primary text content, typically a greeting (e.g., "Good Morning") |
| dataSubheading | string | No | - | Secondary text that appears below the heading, often used for user identification info |
| dataBody | string | No | - | Additional text that appears below the subheading, such as date/time information |
| dataFirstName | string | Yes | - | First name of the user to be displayed on the avatar |
| dataLastName | string | Yes | - | Last name of the user to be displayed on the avatar |
| dataProfilePictureSrc | string | No | - | URL to the user's profile picture for the avatar |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class names |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles for the component |

## Examples

Basic usage with NeonProfileHeader:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonProfileHeader, NeonProfileHeaderGreeting } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ProfileHeaderGreetingExample() {
  return (
    <NeonProfileHeader>
      <div data-slot="start">
        <NeonProfileHeaderGreeting
          dataHeading="Good Morning"
          dataSubheading="Student Number: 31415926535"
          dataBody="It's Thursday, November 10th 2023"
          dataFirstName="Cory"
          dataLastName="Matthews"
          dataProfilePictureSrc="example-files/cory-matthews.jpg"
        />
      </div>
      <div data-slot="end">
        {/* Additional content for the end slot */}
      </div>
    </NeonProfileHeader>
  );
}
```

Simple greeting with minimal information:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonProfileHeader, NeonProfileHeaderGreeting } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function SimpleGreetingExample() {
  return (
    <NeonProfileHeader>
      <div data-slot="start">
        <NeonProfileHeaderGreeting
          dataHeading="Welcome back"
          dataFirstName="Jane"
          dataLastName="Smith"
        />
      </div>
    </NeonProfileHeader>
  );
}
```

With dynamic time-based greeting:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonProfileHeader, NeonProfileHeaderGreeting } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function DynamicGreetingExample() {
  // Example of determining greeting based on time of day
  const getTimeBasedGreeting = () => {
    const hour = new Date().getHours();
    if (hour < 12) return 'Good Morning';
    if (hour < 18) return 'Good Afternoon';
    return 'Good Evening';
  };

  // Get current date as formatted string
  const getFormattedDate = () => {
    return new Date().toLocaleDateString('en-US', {
      weekday: 'long',
      month: 'long',
      day: 'numeric',
      year: 'numeric'
    });
  };

  return (
    <NeonProfileHeader>
      <div data-slot="start">
        <NeonProfileHeaderGreeting
          dataHeading={getTimeBasedGreeting()}
          dataSubheading="Employee ID: 1234567"
          dataBody={`Today is ${getFormattedDate()}`}
          dataFirstName="Alex"
          dataLastName="Johnson"
          dataProfilePictureSrc="path/to/profile-image.jpg"
        />
      </div>
    </NeonProfileHeader>
  );
}
```




# NeonProfileHeader

A flexible component for displaying user profile information with customizable content areas, designed for creating consistent page headers with user information.

## When To Use

Use the NeonProfileHeader component when you need to:

- Display personalized greeting information at the top of a page
- Show user profile information in a prominent location
- Create a consistent header area for user-specific dashboards or profile pages
- Separate the header region from the main content of a page
- Display user profile information with an optional avatar
- Provide a designated area for contextual actions related to user profile
- Create a visually distinct area for user information and related actions

NeonProfileHeader is typically paired with NeonProfileHeaderGreeting in the "start" slot to display personalized user information, while the "end" slot can be used for contextual actions or additional information.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| dataHeight | string | No | - | Controls the height of the profile header. Options: 'short', default |
| dataSkeleton | boolean | No | false | Enables skeleton/loading state |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles for the component |
| id | string | No | - | Unique identifier for the component |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| start | Yes | Content displayed at the left section of the profile header (typically NeonProfileHeaderGreeting) |
| end | No | Content displayed at the right section of the profile header (grows to fill available space) |

## Examples

Basic profile header with greeting:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonProfileHeader, NeonProfileHeaderGreeting } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ProfileHeaderExample() {
  return (
    <NeonProfileHeader>
      <div data-slot="start">
        <NeonProfileHeaderGreeting
          dataHeading="Good Morning"
          dataSubheading="Student Number: 31415926535"
          dataBody="It's Thursday, November 10th 2023"
          dataFirstName="Cory"
          dataLastName="Matthews"
          dataProfilePictureSrc="example-files/cory-matthews.jpg"
        />
      </div>
      <div data-slot="end">
        <p>Additional content</p>
      </div>
    </NeonProfileHeader>
  );
}
```

Short profile header:
```jsx
import React from 'react';

          dataHeading="Good Morning Cory!"
          dataSubheading="It's Thursday, November 10th 2022"
          dataFirstName="Cory"
          dataLastName="Matthews"
        />
      </div>
    </NeonProfileHeader>
  );
}
```

# NeonProgressCircle

A circular progress indicator component that visualizes progress or completion percentage with an animated circular display.

## When To Use

Use the NeonProgressCircle component when you need to:

- Display completion percentage or progress in a circular format
- Show the status of an operation with visual feedback
- Indicate progress through steps in a multi-step process
- Provide feedback on file uploads, downloads, or processing tasks
- Present a compact, visual representation of completion status
- Indicate success, error, or indeterminate states
- Display progress on colored backgrounds with high contrast mode
- Show progress with accompanying text in the center
- Create consistent progress indicators across different sizes

NeonProgressCircle is ideal for visually communicating progress in a more engaging way than traditional progress bars, especially when space is limited or when you want to draw attention to completion status.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the progress circle |
| dataSize | string | No | 'medium' | The size of the progress circle. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'x-large' |
| dataHighContrast | boolean | No | false | When true displays the component in a white high contrast mode |
| dataValue | number | No | - | Used with dataMaxValue to calculate the percentage |
| dataMaxValue | number | No | - | Used with dataValue to calculate the percentage |
| dataPercentage | number | No | - | A number between 0 and 1. If this is set, it will override the value and max value |
| dataText | string | No | - | The text to display in the center of the progress circle |
| dataState | string | No | 'in-progress' | The state of the progress circle. Options: 'in-progress', 'success', 'error', 'undetermined' |

## Examples

Simple progress circle with different sizes:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonProgressCircle } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ProgressCircleExampleSimple() {
  const [percentage, setPercentage] = useState(0);

  return (
    <>
      <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: '16px' }}>
        <NeonProgressCircle
          dataPercentage={percentage}
          dataText="Progress"
          dataSize="small"
        />
        <NeonProgressCircle
          dataPercentage={percentage}
          dataText="Progress"
          dataSize="medium"
        />
        <NeonProgressCircle
          dataPercentage={percentage}
          dataText="Progress"
          dataSize="large"
        />
        <NeonProgressCircle
          dataPercentage={percentage}
          dataText="Progress"
          dataSize="x-large"
        />
      </div>
      <label>
        Input percentage:
        <input
          type="range"
          min="0"
          max="1"
          step="0.01"
          value={percentage}
          onChange={(e) => setPercentage(Number(e.target.value))}
        />
      </label>
    </>
  );
}
```

Progress circle with value and max value:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonProgressCircle } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ProgressCircleExampleValues() {
  const [currentStep, setCurrentStep] = useState(0);

  return (
    <>
      <NeonProgressCircle
        id="progress-circle"
        dataValue={currentStep}
        dataMaxValue={5}
        dataText={'Step ' + currentStep + ' of 5'}
        dataSize="x-large"
      />
      <NeonButton
        id="next-step-button"
        dataText="Next Step"
        onClick={() => setCurrentStep((currentStep + 1) % 6)}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

Progress circle with different states:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonProgressCircle } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ProgressCircleExampleStates() {
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: '16px' }}>
      <NeonProgressCircle
        dataText="Progress"
        dataSize="medium"
      />
      <NeonProgressCircle
        dataState="success"
        dataText="Success"
        dataSize="medium"
      />
      <NeonProgressCircle
        dataState="error"
        dataText="Error"
        dataSize="medium"
      />
      <NeonProgressCircle
        dataState="undetermined"
        dataText="Loading"
        dataSize="medium"
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

High contrast progress circle:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonProgressCircle } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ProgressCircleExampleHighContrast() {
  const [percentage, setPercentage] = useState(0);

  return (
    <>
      <div style={{
        display: 'flex',
        gap: '16px',
        backgroundColor: 'var(--neon-theme-primary-co-brand, #087EB4)'
      }}>
        <NeonProgressCircle
          dataPercentage={percentage}
          dataText="Progress"
          dataSize="medium"
          dataHighContrast={true}
        />
      </div>
      <label>
        Input percentage:
        <input
          type="range"
          min="0"
          max="1"
          step="0.01"
          value={percentage}
          onChange={(e) => setPercentage(Number(e.target.value))}
        />
      </label>
    </>
  );
}
```


# NeonProgressIndicator

A versatile progress indicator component for displaying completion or progress status with customizable layouts, colors, and styles.

## When To Use

Use the NeonProgressIndicator component when you need to:

- Show the completion status of a task or process
- Provide visual feedback on the progress of an operation
- Display a ratio or percentage of completion
- Indicate loading or processing states in your application
- Show the user how much of a multi-step process has been completed
- Visualize data metrics in a simple horizontal bar format
- Create progress tracking elements with consistent styling
- Show progress toward a goal or target value

NeonProgressIndicator is flexible and can be configured in different layouts to fit various UI contexts. Choose from simple, wide, condensed, or bar-only layouts depending on your space constraints and design requirements.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the progress indicator |
| value | number | Yes | 0 | The current value that describes the progress (numerator) |
| dataTotal | number | Yes | - | The target number to reach (denominator) |
| dataLabelText | string | No | - | The label text for the progress bar |
| dataLayout | string | No | 'simple' | Layout style of the progress indicator. Options: 'simple', 'wide', 'condensed', 'bar-only' |
| dataColor | string | No | 'navy' | The color of the progress bar. Options: 'magenta', 'orange', 'green', 'teal', 'cyan', 'navy', 'purple' |
| dataBarHeight | string | No | 'medium' | The height of the progress bar. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large' |
| dataIsPercent | boolean | No | false | When true, shows percentage instead of "value of total" |
| dataMaxDecimals | number | No | 0 | Maximum decimal places to show when displaying percentages |
| dataTextSize | string | No | 'medium' | Size of the text. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large' |

## Examples

Basic progress indicator:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonProgressIndicator } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function BasicProgressIndicator() {
  return (
    <NeonProgressIndicator
      id="basic-progress"
      dataLabelText="Task Progress"
      value={7}
      dataTotal={10}
    />
  );
}
```

Different layout options:
```jsx

  return (
    <>
      <NeonProgressIndicator
        id="bar-only-example"
        dataLayout="bar-only"
        dataLabelText="Bar only"
        value={7}
        dataTotal={10}
      />

      <NeonProgressIndicator
        id="simple-example"
        dataLabelText="Simple layout"
        value={7}
        dataTotal={10}
      />

      <NeonProgressIndicator
        id="wide-example"
        dataLayout="wide"
        dataLabelText="Wide layout"
        value={7}
        dataTotal={10}
      />

      <NeonProgressIndicator
        id="condensed-example"
        dataLayout="condensed"
        dataLabelText="Condensed layout"
        value={7}
        dataTotal={10}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

Custom colors and bar heights:
```jsx

  return (
    <>
      <NeonProgressIndicator

      />

      <NeonProgressIndicator
        id="purple-progress"

    </>
  );
```

```jsx
    />
  );
```

# NeonRadioField

A form field component for selecting a single option from a list of radio buttons.

## When To Use

Use the NeonRadioField component when you need to:

- Present users with a list of mutually exclusive options where only one can be selected
- Make all options visible to the user at once (unlike a dropdown that hides options)
- Provide a clearer visual indication of the selected option compared to a select field
- Create a group of related radio buttons with consistent styling
- Implement a form field where seeing all available options helps users make better decisions
- Present a small to medium number of options (typically 2-7)
- Organize options horizontally or vertically depending on space constraints

NeonRadioField is ideal when users need to see all available options simultaneously to make a clear choice between mutually exclusive items. For large numbers of options, consider using NeonSelectField instead.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the radio field |
| dataLabelText | string | Yes | - | Label text for the field |
| dataOptions | Array<RadioOption> | Yes | - | Array of radio options to display |
| modelValue | string \| undefined | Yes | - | Current selected value |
| modelValueChange | function | Yes | - | Handler for value changes: (value: string \| undefined) => void |
| dataShowLabel | boolean | No | true | Whether to show the label |
| dataOrientation | string | No | 'vertical' | Orientation of the radio options. Options: 'vertical', 'horizontal' |
| dataHelperText | string | No | - | Helper text displayed below the field |
| dataIsRequired | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is required |
| dataHideRequiredBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to hide the required indicator |
| dataShowOptionalBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to show an optional indicator |
| dataSuccessMessage | string | No | - | Message to display when validation succeeds |
| dataLabelTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Whether to add space for label text alignment |
| dataHelperTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Whether to add space for helper text alignment |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is disabled |
| customValidationFunction | function | No | - | Custom validation function |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |

### RadioOption Interface

```typescript
interface RadioOption {
  label: string;
  value: string;
  description?: string;
  disabled?: boolean;
}
```

## Examples

Basic radio field:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonRadioField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

function BasicRadioFieldExample() {
  const [selectedColor, setSelectedColor] = useState('');
  
  const colorOptions = [
    { label: 'Red', value: 'red' },
    { label: 'Green', value: 'green' },
    { label: 'Blue', value: 'blue' }
  ];
  
  return (
    <NeonRadioField
      id="color-selection"
      dataLabelText="Select a Color"
      dataOptions={colorOptions}
      modelValue={selectedColor}
      modelValueChange={(value) => setSelectedColor(value)}
    />
  );
}
```

Horizontal radio field with descriptions:
```jsx
<NeonRadioField
  id="shipping-options"
  dataLabelText="Shipping Method"
  dataOrientation="horizontal"
  dataIsRequired={true}
  dataOptions={[
    { 
      label: 'Standard', 
      value: 'standard', 
      description: 'Delivery in 5-7 business days (Free)'
    },
    { 
      label: 'Express', 
      value: 'express', 
      description: 'Delivery in 2-3 business days ($9.99)'
    },
    { 
      label: 'Priority', 
      value: 'priority', 
      description: 'Delivery in 1 business day ($19.99)',
      disabled: !isPriorityAvailable
    }
  ]}
  modelValue={shippingMethod}
  modelValueChange={setShippingMethod}
  dataHelperText="Select the shipping method for your order"
/>
```

Required radio field with validation:
```jsx
<NeonRadioField
  id="payment-method"
  dataLabelText="Payment Method"
  dataIsRequired={true}
  dataOptions={[
    { label: 'Credit Card', value: 'credit' },
    { label: 'PayPal', value: 'paypal' },
    { label: 'Bank Transfer', value: 'bank' }
  ]}
  modelValue={paymentMethod}
  modelValueChange={setPaymentMethod}
  customValidationFunction={(value) => {
    if (value === 'bank' && !bankAccountVerified) {
      return { isValid: false, errorMessage: 'Bank account must be verified first' };
    }
    return { isValid: true };
  }}
/>
```

Disabled radio field:
```jsx
<NeonRadioField
  id="subscription-type"
  dataLabelText="Subscription Type"
  dataOptions={[
    { label: 'Monthly', value: 'monthly' },
    { label: 'Annual', value: 'annual' },
    { label: 'Lifetime', value: 'lifetime' }
  ]}
  modelValue="annual"
  modelValueChange={() => {}} // No-op since field is disabled
  disabled={true}
  dataHelperText="Your subscription type cannot be changed at this time"
/>
```

Radio field with individual disabled options:
```jsx
<NeonRadioField
  id="account-type"
  dataLabelText="Account Type"
  dataOptions={[
    { label: 'Basic', value: 'basic' },
    { label: 'Premium', value: 'premium' },
    { label: 'Enterprise', value: 'enterprise', disabled: !hasEnterpriseAccess }
  ]}
  modelValue={accountType}
  modelValueChange={setAccountType}
/>
```


# NeonRadioSingle

A standalone radio button component for individual selection controls with customizable appearance and behavior.

## When To Use

Use the NeonRadioSingle component when you need to:

- Create individual radio button controls outside of a radio group
- Implement custom selection indicators with different icons or colors
- Display radio options with helper text or additional information
- Create visually distinct radio buttons for specific interactive patterns
- Implement radio buttons with tooltip support for compact interfaces
- Create custom radio interfaces like heart/star ratings or specialized toggles
- Display radio options in standalone mode for icon-based selection
- Create accessible radio controls that require screen reader support

NeonRadioSingle provides a single radio button input. For grouped radio buttons with related options, consider using the NeonRadioField component which manages multiple radio options as a cohesive group.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the radio button |
| dataLabelText | string | Yes | - | The text label for the radio button |
| name | string | No | - | The value that will be set for <input name=""> |
| dataOptionValue | string | No | - | The value of the radio button |
| value | boolean | No | false | Sets whether the radio is selected or unselected |
| dataShowLabel | boolean | No | true | Controls visibility of the label text |
| dataSize | string | No | 'auto' | Sets the width of the label. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'x-large', 'auto' |
| dataLabelTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Adds space above the radio button |
| dataHelperTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Adds space above the radio button |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | When true, disables the component |
| dataIsReadOnly | boolean | No | false | When true, puts the radio into read-only mode |
| dataHelperText | string | No | - | Additional help text displayed below the label |
| dataIsIndented | boolean | No | false | When true, indents the radio button |
| dataIconSelected | string | No | - | Icon to use when radio is in selected state |
| dataIconUnselected | string | No | - | Icon to use when radio is in unselected state |
| dataIconIndeterminate | string | No | - | Icon to use when radio is in indeterminate state |
| dataIconColor | string | No | 'navy' | Color of custom icons. Options: 'navy', 'purple', 'magenta', 'red', 'orange', 'yellow', 'green', 'teal', 'cyan', 'gray' |
| dataStandAlone | boolean | No | false | When true, displays a larger icon and click box, hides label, and ignores helper text |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Tooltip text shown on hover (only works when label is hidden or in stand alone mode) |
| onInput | function | No | - | Event handler for when the radio state changes |

## Examples

Simple radio button group:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonRadioSingle } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function RadioSingleExampleSimple() {
  const [selectedPerson, setSelectedPerson] = useState('user-2');

  return (
    <>
      <NeonRadioSingle
        id="person-1"
        name="selected-person"
        dataOptionValue="user-1"
        dataLabelText="Albert Einstein"
        value={selectedPerson === 'user-1'}
        onInput={() => {
          setSelectedPerson('user-1');
        }}
      />
      <NeonRadioSingle
        id="person-2"
        name="selected-person"
        dataOptionValue="user-2"
        dataLabelText="Marie Curie"
        value={selectedPerson === 'user-2'}
        onInput={() => {
          setSelectedPerson('user-2');
        }}
      />
      <NeonRadioSingle
        id="person-3"
        name="selected-person"
        dataOptionValue="user-3"
        dataLabelText="Stephen Hawking"
        value={selectedPerson === 'user-3'}
        onInput={() => {
          setSelectedPerson('user-3');
        }}
      />
    </>
  );
}
```

# NeonRatingField

A form control component for collecting user feedback through various rating systems like star ratings and satisfaction indicators.

## When To Use

Use the NeonRatingField component when you need to:

- Collect user feedback about their experience with a product or service
- Allow users to rate the quality of content, products, or experiences
- Implement hotel, restaurant, or product rating systems
- Include satisfaction surveys or feedback forms in your application
- Provide visual feedback mechanisms for user sentiment
- Create a simple, intuitive way for users to express their level of satisfaction
- Implement customer review functionality
- Gather quantifiable feedback data through clear visual choices

NeonRatingField supports different rating types, including 5-star ratings, 3-star ratings, and various satisfaction rating styles, making it versatile for different feedback collection needs.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the rating field |
| dataLabelText | string | Yes | - | Label text for the rating field |
| dataHelperText | string | No | - | Additional helper text |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Text for tooltip |
| dataIsRequired | BooleanAttribute | No | false | Whether the field is required |
| dataHideRequiredBadge | BooleanAttribute | No | false | Whether to hide the required badge |
| dataShowOptionalBadge | BooleanAttribute | No | false | Whether to show optional badge |
| dataShowLabel | BooleanAttribute | No | true | Whether to show the label |
| dataAriaLabel | string | No | - | Accessible label for screen readers |
| dataLabelTextSpace | string | No | - | Custom spacing for the label |
| dataHelperTextSpace | string | No | - | Custom spacing for helper text |
| dataSuccessMessage | string | No | - | Success message to display |
| dataSize | string | No | - | Size of the rating field |
| modelValue | number \| undefined | Yes | - | Current rating value |
| modelValueChange | function | Yes | - | Handler for when rating changes |
| dataType | string | No | '5-star-rating' | Rating type to display |
| dataIsReadOnly | BooleanAttribute | No | false | Whether the field is read-only |
| disabled | BooleanAttribute | No | false | Whether the field is disabled |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| customValidationFunction | function | No | - | Custom validation function |
| blurInterceptor | function | No | - | Function to intercept blur events |
| onBlur | function | No | - | Handler for blur events |

## Available Rating Types

| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| 5-star-rating | Traditional 5-star rating system |
| 3-star-rating | Simplified 3-star rating system |
| expanded-satisfaction-rating | Detailed satisfaction rating with multiple options |
| simple-satisfaction-rating | Basic satisfaction rating with facial expressions |
| simple-satisfaction-rating-2 | Alternative simple satisfaction rating |

## Examples

Simple rating fields:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonRatingField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function RatingFieldExampleSimple() {
  const [typeScriptStarRating, setTypeScriptStarRating] = useState();
  const [neonSatisfactionRating, setNeonSatisfactionRating] = useState();

  return (
    <>
      <div>
        <NeonRatingField
          id="expanded-satisfaction-id"
          dataLabelText="How Satisfied With Neon Are you"
          dataType="expanded-satisfaction-rating"
          dataShowLabel="false"
          modelValue={neonSatisfactionRating}
          modelValueChange={(value) => { setNeonSatisfactionRating(value); }}
        />
      </div>
      <div>
        <NeonRatingField
          id="star-rating-id"
          dataLabelText="How Awesome is TypeScript"
          dataShowLabel="false"
          dataType="5-star-rating"
          modelValue={typeScriptStarRating}
          modelValueChange={(value) => { setTypeScriptStarRating(value); }}
        />
      </div>
    </>
  );
}
```

Rating fields in a form:
```jsx

export function RatingFieldExampleForm() {
  const [hotelRating, setHotelRating] = useState(1);
  const [happinessToday, setHappinessToday] = useState(2);

  return (
    <>
      <div>
        <NeonRatingField
          id="star-rating"
          dataLabelText="Hotel Rating"
          dataHelperText="Please rate your experience at our hotel"
          dataTooltipText="Up to 3 stars"
          dataType="3-star-rating"
          modelValue={hotelRating}
          modelValueChange={(value) => { setHotelRating(value); }}
        />
      </div>
      <div>
        <NeonRatingField
          id="satisfaction-simple"
          dataLabelText="How do you feel today?"
          dataHelperText="Select one of the 3 emotions"
          dataTooltipText="We hope you are happy today."
          dataType="simple-satisfaction-rating"
          dataSuccessMessage="Your Ratings has been saved"
          dataIsRequired="true"
          modelValue={happinessToday}
          modelValueChange={(value) => { setHappinessToday(value); }}
        />
      </div>
    </>
  );
}
```

Rating field with a textarea for additional comments:
```jsx

          dataTooltipText="Up to 3 stars"

        />

          id="description"
          dataLabelText="Comments"
          dataShowLabel="false"
          dataMaxLength={250}
          dataShowCount="true"
          modelValue={description}
          modelValueChange={(desc) => { setDescription(desc); }}
        />
      </div>
    </>
  );
}
```


# NeonRichTextEditor

A versatile WYSIWYG rich text editor component that allows users to create and edit formatted content with various styling options, embedded media, and more.

## When To Use

Use the NeonRichTextEditor component when you need to:

- Allow users to create or edit formatted text content
- Provide text formatting capabilities like bold, italic, underline, etc.
- Enable insertion of media like images and videos into text content
- Create forms that require rich text input fields
- Build content management interfaces
- Allow users to create content with headings, lists, tables, and other formatting
- Display rich text content in a read-only view
- Implement interfaces where users need to format text similar to a word processor
- Create documentation or description fields that support HTML formatting
- Provide a standardized text editing experience across applications

NeonRichTextEditor is built on top of SunEditor and provides a consistent, accessible interface for editing rich text content within the Neon Design System.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the rich text editor |
| dataLabelText | string | Yes | - | Text label for the editor |
| modelValue | string \| undefined | Yes | - | The HTML contents of the rich text |
| modelValueChange | function | Yes | - | Callback function called when content changes |
| dataShowLabel | boolean | No | true | Whether to show the field label |
| dataAriaLabel | string | No | - | Accessible label for screen readers |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Text to display in the tooltip |
| dataHelperText | string | No | - | Helper text displayed below the editor |
| dataSize | string | No | - | Size of the input field |
| dataSuccessMessage | string | No | - | Success message to display when validation passes |
| dataIsRequired | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is required |
| dataHideRequiredBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to hide the required badge |
| dataShowOptionalBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to show an optional badge |
| dataLabelTextSpace | boolean | No | true | Whether to reserve space for label text |
| dataHelperTextSpace | boolean | No | true | Whether to reserve space for helper text |
| dataConstrainDescription | boolean | No | false | Whether to constrain the description text |
| dataPlaceholderText | string | No | - | Placeholder text shown when editor is empty |
| dataMinLength | number | No | - | Minimum required character length |
| dataMaxLength | number | No | - | Maximum allowed character length |
| dataSelectImageFromFiles | boolean | No | false | Whether to allow image selection from local files |
| dataShowBorder | boolean | No | true | Whether to show a border around the editor |
| dataIsReadOnly | boolean | No | false | Whether the editor is in read-only mode |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Whether the editor is disabled |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| sunEditorOptions | SunEditorOptions | No | - | Configuration options for the SunEditor instance |
| onImageUploadBeforeCallback | function | No | - | Callback before image upload to handle custom logic |
| customValidationFunction | function | No | - | Custom validation function |
| blurInterceptor | function | No | - | Function called before blur event handling |

## Examples

Simple rich text editor:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonRichTextEditor } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function RichTextEditorExampleSimple() {
  const [message, setMessage] = useState();

  return (
    <NeonRichTextEditor id="message-rte"
      dataLabelText="Message"
      dataShowLabel="false"
      modelValue={message}
      modelValueChange={(value) => {
        setMessage(value);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Rich text editor as a form field:
```jsx

    <NeonRichTextEditor id="course-description-rte"
      dataLabelText="Course Description"
      dataHelperText="Enter course description"
      dataTooltipText="Something about a course."
      dataIsRequired="true"
      modelValue={courseDescription}
      modelValueChange={(value) => {
        setCourseDescription(value);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Customizing editor toolbar options:
```jsx
import React, { useState, useMemo } from 'react';
import { NeonRichTextEditor } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function RichTextEditorExampleCustomOptions() {
  const [content, setContent] = useState();

  // Note: Always use useMemo to prevent editor reinitializing on re-renders
  const customSunEditorOptions = useMemo(() => {
    return {
      buttonList: [
        ['undo', 'redo'],
        ['font', 'fontSize', 'formatBlock'],
        ['bold', 'underline', 'italic', 'strike'],
        ['fontColor', 'hiliteColor'],
        ['removeFormat'],
        ['outdent', 'indent'],
        ['align', 'list'],
        ['table', 'link', 'image'],
        ['fullScreen']
      ]
    };
  }, []);

  return (
    <NeonRichTextEditor id="custom-options-rte"
      dataLabelText="Custom Editor Options"
      sunEditorOptions={customSunEditorOptions}
      modelValue={content}
      modelValueChange={(value) => {
        setContent(value);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Read-only rich text display:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonRichTextEditor } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function RichTextEditorExampleReadOnly() {
  const htmlContent = '<h2>Hello World!</h2><p>This is sample content displayed in read-only mode.</p>';

  return (
    <NeonRichTextEditor id="read-only-rte"
      dataLabelText="Read Only Content"
      dataIsReadOnly="true"
      modelValue={htmlContent}
      modelValueChange={() => {}}
      dataShowBorder="false"
    />
  );
}
```

Custom image upload handling:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonRichTextEditor } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function RichTextEditorExampleImageUpload() {
  const [content, setContent] = useState();

  return (
    <NeonRichTextEditor id="image-upload-rte"
      dataLabelText="Editor with Image Upload"
      dataSelectImageFromFiles="true"
      modelValue={content}
      modelValueChange={(value) => {
        setContent(value);
      }}
      onImageUploadBeforeCallback={(files, info, core, uploadHandler) => {
        // Custom image handling logic
        console.log('Image upload initiated', files);

        // Return true to proceed with default upload
        // Return false to cancel the upload
        // Return modified file array to upload different files
        return true;
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Custom validation:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonRichTextEditor } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function RichTextEditorExampleCustomValidation() {
  const [content, setContent] = useState();

  return (
    <NeonRichTextEditor id="validation-rte"
      dataLabelText="Editor with Custom Validation"
      dataIsRequired="true"
      modelValue={content}
      modelValueChange={(value) => {
        setContent(value);
      }}
      customValidationFunction={(value, condition, context) => {
        // Require content to have at least 20 characters
        const isValid = value && value.length >= 20;

        return {
          isValid,
          errorMessage: isValid ? undefined : 'Content must be at least 20 characters long'
        };
      }}
    />
  );
}
```


# NeonSelectField

A dropdown selection component that allows users to select a single option from a list of choices.

## When To Use

Use the NeonSelectField component when you need to:

- Allow users to select a single option from a list of multiple choices
- Conserve space when the number of options would take up too much real estate
- Organize options into logical groups or categories
- Provide filtering capabilities for large option lists
- Create structured selection interfaces with parent-child relationships
- Implement a dropdown menu with searchable options
- Display rich content within selection options (like icons or badges)
- Replace native HTML select elements with a consistent, customizable alternative

NeonSelectField works well when you have a predefined set of options where users should select exactly one value. For multiple selections, consider using NeonMultiSelectField instead. For very short option lists (2-3 options), consider using radio buttons for better visibility and accessibility.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the select field |
| dataLabelText | string | Yes | - | Label text for the field |
| modelValue | string \| undefined | Yes | - | Currently selected value |
| modelValueChange | function | Yes | - | Handler for value changes: (value: string \| undefined) => void |
| options | Array<SelectOptionWithDividers \| SelectOptionWithDividersGroup \| 'DIVIDER'> | Yes | - | Array of options to display in the dropdown |
| dataShowLabel | boolean | No | true | Whether to show the label |
| dataAriaLabel | string | No | - | Accessibility label for screen readers |
| dataHelperText | string | No | - | Helper text displayed below the field |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Text to show in a tooltip |
| dataPlaceholderText | string | No | - | Text to display when no option is selected |
| dataSize | string | No | 'auto' | Width of the field. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'x-large', 'auto' |
| dataIsRequired | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is required |
| dataHideRequiredBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to hide the required indicator |
| dataShowOptionalBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to show an optional indicator |
| dataShowFilter | boolean | No | false | Whether to show a search filter input |
| dataIsLoading | boolean | No | false | Whether to show a loading indicator |
| dataIsReadOnly | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is read-only |
| dataPopperPlacement | string | No | 'bottom-start' | Placement of the dropdown. Options: 'top-start', 'top-end', 'bottom-start', 'bottom-end', 'left-start', 'left', 'left-end', 'right-start', 'right', 'right-end' |
| dataPopperMaxHeight | string | No | - | Maximum height of the dropdown. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large', or a custom value |
| dataUndefinedOption | boolean | No | false | Whether to include a special option for clearing the selection |
| dataUndefinedOptionText | string | No | - | Text for the undefined option |
| dataUndefinedOptionSubtext | string | No | - | Subtext for the undefined option |
| dataSuccessMessage | string | No | - | Message to display when validation succeeds |
| dataLabelTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Whether to add space for label text alignment |
| dataHelperTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Whether to add space for helper text alignment |
| dataConstrainDescription | boolean | No | false | Whether to constrain description width to match the field |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is disabled |
| neonPopperClose | function | No | - | Handler for popper close events |
| customValidationFunction | function | No | - | Custom validation function |
| onBlur | function | No | - | Handler for blur events |
| blurInterceptor | function | No | - | Function called before blur processing |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |

## Option Interface

### SelectOptionWithDividers
| Property | Type | Required | Description |
|----------|------|----------|-------------|
| text | string | Yes | Text to display for this option |
| value | string \| number | Yes | Value associated with this option |
| subText | string | No | Secondary text to display |
| disabled | boolean | No | Whether this option is disabled |
| icon | string | No | Icon name to display with this option |

### SelectOptionWithDividersGroup
| Property | Type | Required | Description |
|----------|------|----------|-------------|
| text | string | Yes | Text to display for this group header |
| value | Array<SelectOptionWithDividers \| 'DIVIDER'> | Yes | Array of options in this group |

## Examples

Basic select field:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonSelectField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

function SelectFieldExample() {
  const [selectedCar, setSelectedCar] = useState('auto-222');
  
  return (
    <NeonSelectField
      id="car-select"
      dataLabelText="Select a Car"
      options={[
        { text: 'Ferrari', value: 'auto-111' },
        { text: 'Ford', value: 'auto-222' },
        { text: 'Honda', value: 'auto-333' }
      ]}
      modelValue={selectedCar}
      modelValueChange={(value) => setSelectedCar(value)}
    />
  );
}
```

Select with option groups:

```jsx
    {
      text: 'Marketing',
      value: [
        { text: 'Digital Marketing', value: 'digital-marketing' },

      text: 'Engineering',
      value: [
        { text: 'Frontend', value: 'frontend' },

      ]
    }
  ]}
  modelValue={department}
  modelValueChange={setDepartment}

```

# NeonSessionTimeoutWarning

A security component that warns users about session timeouts after periods of inactivity and provides options to stay signed in or sign out.

## When To Use

Use the NeonSessionTimeoutWarning component when you need to:

- Implement session timeout management for security purposes
- Notify users about impending automatic logouts due to inactivity
- Provide users with the option to extend their session or sign out manually
- Comply with security requirements for automatic session termination
- Create a consistent session timeout experience across your application
- Automatically monitor user activity and trigger appropriate timeout warnings
- Implement cross-tab session timeout coordination using localStorage
- Provide a user-friendly way to handle security-based session expirations

NeonSessionTimeoutWarning is designed to enhance application security while maintaining a good user experience. It monitors user activity (clicks and key presses) and displays a warning dialog after a period of inactivity, followed by automatic logout if the user doesn't respond.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the component |
| dataDialogHeaderText | string | No | 'Session Timeout' | The dialog header text |
| dataWarningHeaderText | string | No | 'Your session will expire soon' | The warning header text |
| dataWarningMessageText | string | No | 'You will be signed out in five minutes due to inactivity.' | The warning message text |
| dataSignOutButtonText | string | No | 'Sign out' | Text used for the sign out button |
| dataStaySignedInButtonText | string | No | 'Stay signed in' | Text used for the stay signed in button |
| dataWarningTime | number | No | 25 | Duration of time until warning dialog is shown (in minutes) |
| dataLogoutTime | number | No | 5 | Duration of time the warning modal is visible until logout (in minutes) |
| neonSessionTimeoutWarningLogout | function | No | - | Callback function when automatic logout occurs |
| neonSessionTimeoutWarningLogoutWarningTimerStart | function | No | - | Callback function when warning timer starts |

## Events

| Name | Description |
|------|-------------|
| neonSessionTimeoutWarningLogout | Fired after the logout timer has expired, indicating a session timeout |
| neonSessionTimeoutWarningLogoutWarningTimerStart | Fired when the warning dialog is displayed |

## Examples

Basic example with logout handler:
```jsx
import React from 'react';

export function SessionTimeoutWarningExample() {
  function logout() {
    console.log('You have been logged out!');
    // Implement actual logout logic here
  }

  return <NeonSessionTimeoutWarning neonSessionTimeoutWarningLogout={logout} />;
}
```

Customized example with modified timeouts and text:
```jsx

  }

  }

    dataWarningTime={15}
    dataLogoutTime={2}
    dataWarningMessageText="You will be signed out in two minutes due to inactivity."
```

Implementation with detailed warning text and callback functions:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonSessionTimeoutWarning, showSystemMessage } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function SessionTimeoutWarningAdvancedExample() {
  // Handle logout action
  function handleLogout() {
    // Show a system message
    showSystemMessage('You have been logged out', {
      messageType: 'error',
      autoDismiss: false
    });

    // Redirect to login page
    window.location.href = '/login';
  }

  // Handle warning display
  function handleWarningStart() {
    // Show an info message when the warning displays
    showSystemMessage('Your session will expire soon. Please save your work.', {
      messageType: 'info',
      autoDismissTime: 120000 // 2 minutes
    });

    // Play a notification sound
    const audio = new Audio('/assets/notification.mp3');
    audio.play();
  }

  return (
    <NeonSessionTimeoutWarning
      dataWarningTime={30}
      dataLogoutTime={3}
      dataWarningHeaderText="Session Timeout Imminent"
      dataWarningMessageText="Due to inactivity, your session will expire in 3 minutes. Any unsaved changes will be lost."
      dataStaySignedInButtonText="Continue Working"
      neonSessionTimeoutWarningLogout={handleLogout}
      neonSessionTimeoutWarningLogoutWarningTimerStart={handleWarningStart}
    />
  );
}
```


# NeonStepperNavigation

A step-based navigation component for guiding users through multi-step processes, workflows, or forms.

## When To Use

Use the NeonStepperNavigation component when you need to:

- Create guided, multi-step processes or wizards
- Break complex tasks into manageable steps
- Show users their progress through a workflow
- Create sequential or non-sequential step navigation
- Implement form wizards with validation between steps
- Track completion status of each step in a process
- Guide users through a complex workflow
- Maintain process flow with clear navigation between steps
- Show relationships between different steps in a workflow
- Organize related content into logical steps

NeonStepperNavigation provides a structured way to navigate through multi-step processes. It can be displayed in horizontal or vertical layouts, with numbered or unnumbered steps, and supports sequential or non-sequential navigation patterns.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the stepper navigation component |
| dataIsHorizontal | boolean | No | false | Whether to display steps horizontally (true) or vertically (false) |
| dataIsNumbered | boolean | No | false | Whether to display step numbers |
| dataIsSequential | boolean | No | false | Whether to enforce sequential navigation between steps |

## API

The NeonStepperNavigation component exposes a JavaScript API for programmatic control through the `getStepperNavigation(id)` function.

### Getters

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| getActiveStep() | Returns the currently active step or undefined |
| getStepState(stepId) | Returns the state of the specified step ('complete', 'in-progress', 'error', or undefined) |
| getNonCompleteSteps(stepIds?) | Returns IDs of all incomplete steps, or from the provided subset of step IDs |
| getStepIndexById(stepId) | Returns the index of the specified step or undefined if not found |
| getSteps() | Returns an array of all step objects |
| getChangeStream() | Returns an observable stream of stepper navigation change events |
| getIsStepDisabled(stepId) | Returns whether the specified step is disabled |
| getIsSequential() | Returns whether sequential navigation is enforced |
| getIsFirstStepActive() | Returns whether the first step is currently active |
| getIsLastStepActive() | Returns whether the last step is currently active |
| getId() | Returns the ID of the stepper navigation component |

### Setters

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| setSteps(steps) | Sets the steps array and redraws the component |
| setStepToActive(step) | Sets the specified step to the active state |
| setStepToComplete(step) | Sets the specified step to the complete state |
| setStepToInProgress(step) | Sets the specified step to the in-progress state |
| setStepToError(step) | Sets the specified step to the error state |
| setStepToDefault(step) | Removes any state from the specified step |
| setStepState(step, state?) | Sets the specified step to the given state |
| setStepToDisabled(step) | Disables the specified step |
| setIsSequential(isSequential) | Sets whether sequential navigation is enforced |

### Navigation Functions

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| nextStep() | Activates the next step, or the first step if none is active |
| previousStep() | Activates the previous step if available |

## Examples

Basic vertical stepper:

```jsx
import React, { useEffect } from 'react';
import { NeonStepperNavigation, getStepperNavigation } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function StepperNavigationBasic() {
  const id = 'basic-stepper-navigation';

  useEffect(() => {
    getStepperNavigation(id).then((stepperNav) => {
      stepperNav.setSteps([
        { id: 'step-1', text: 'Step 1', subtext: 'First step', getStateBeforeLeavingStep: () => 'complete' },
        { id: 'step-2', text: 'Step 2', subtext: 'Second step', getStateBeforeLeavingStep: () => 'complete' },
        { id: 'step-3', text: 'Step 3', subtext: 'Final step', getStateBeforeLeavingStep: () => 'complete' }
      ]);
    });
  }, []);

  return <NeonStepperNavigation id={id} />;
}
```

Horizontal stepper with step events:

```jsx
import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { NeonStepperNavigation, getStepperNavigation } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function StepperNavigationHorizontal() {
  const id = 'horizontal-stepper';
  const [activeStepId, setActiveStepId] = useState('step-1');

  useEffect(() => {
    getStepperNavigation(id).then((stepperNav) => {
      stepperNav.setSteps([
        { id: 'step-1', text: 'Personal Info', subtext: 'Name and contact', getStateBeforeLeavingStep: () => 'complete' },
        { id: 'step-2', text: 'Account Details', subtext: 'Preferences', getStateBeforeLeavingStep: () => 'complete' },
        { id: 'step-3', text: 'Confirmation', subtext: 'Review and submit', getStateBeforeLeavingStep: () => 'complete' }
      ]);

      stepperNav.getChangeStream().subscribe((event) => {
        if (event.name === 'active-step-change') {
          setActiveStepId(stepperNav.getActiveStep()?.id || 'step-1');
        }
      });
    });
  }, []);

  return (
    <div>
      <NeonStepperNavigation id={id} dataIsHorizontal={true} />
      <div>
        <h2>Content for: {activeStepId}</h2>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Sequential stepper with validation:

```jsx
import React, { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
import {
  NeonStepperNavigation,
  getStepperNavigation,
  NeonTextField,
  NeonButtonFooter
} from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { validateFields } from '@neon/exported-utils';

export function SequentialStepperWithValidation() {
  const id = 'sequential-stepper';
  const formRef = useRef(null);
  const [activeStepId, setActiveStepId] = useState('step-1');
  const [stepperNav, setStepperNav] = useState(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    getStepperNavigation(id).then((stepperNavigation) => {
      setStepperNav(stepperNavigation);

      stepperNavigation.setSteps([
        {
          id: 'step-1',
          text: 'Step 1',
          getStateBeforeLeavingStep: (current, next) => {
            if (formRef.current) {
              const isValid = validateFields(formRef.current);
              return isValid ? 'complete' : 'prevent-step-change';
            }
            return 'complete';
          }
        },
        {
          id: 'step-2',
          text: 'Step 2',
          getStateBeforeLeavingStep: (current, next) => {
            if (formRef.current) {
              const isValid = validateFields(formRef.current);
              return isValid ? 'complete' : 'prevent-step-change';
            }
            return 'complete';
          }
        },
        {
          id: 'step-3',
          text: 'Complete',
          getStateBeforeLeavingStep: () => 'complete'
        }
      ]);

      stepperNavigation.getChangeStream().subscribe((event) => {
        if (event.name === 'active-step-change') {
          setActiveStepId(stepperNavigation.getActiveStep()?.id || 'step-1');
        }
      });
    });
  }, []);

  const handleNext = () => {
    stepperNav?.nextStep();
  };

  const handlePrevious = () => {
    stepperNav?.previousStep();
  };

  return (
    <div>
      <NeonStepperNavigation id={id} dataIsSequential={true} />

      <div className="__neon__form" ref={formRef}>
        {activeStepId === 'step-1' && (
          <NeonTextField
            id="field-1"
            dataLabelText="Field 1"
            dataIsRequired="true"
          />
        )}

        {activeStepId === 'step-2' && (
          <NeonTextField
            id="field-2"
            dataLabelText="Field 2"
            dataIsRequired="true"
          />
        )}

        {activeStepId === 'step-3' && (
          <div>Completed all steps!</div>
        )}
      </div>

      <NeonButtonFooter
        id="stepper-buttons"
        buttons={[{
          id: 'previous-button',
          text: 'Previous',
          type: 'secondary',
          onClick: handlePrevious,
          disabled: activeStepId === 'step-1'
        }]}
        primaryButton={{
          id: 'next-button',
          text: activeStepId === 'step-3' ? 'Finish' : 'Next',
          onClick: handleNext
        }}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

Numbered horizontal stepper:

```jsx
import React, { useEffect } from 'react';
import { NeonStepperNavigation, getStepperNavigation } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function NumberedStepperNavigation() {
  const id = 'numbered-stepper';

  useEffect(() => {
    getStepperNavigation(id).then((stepperNav) => {
      stepperNav.setSteps([
        { id: 'step-1', text: 'Select Plan', getStateBeforeLeavingStep: () => 'complete' },
        { id: 'step-2', text: 'Create Account', getStateBeforeLeavingStep: () => 'complete' },
        { id: 'step-3', text: 'Payment Details', getStateBeforeLeavingStep: () => 'complete' },
        { id: 'step-4', text: 'Confirmation', getStateBeforeLeavingStep: () => 'complete' }
      ]);

      // Set initial step states
      stepperNav.setStepState('step-1', 'complete');
      stepperNav.setStepToActive('step-2');
    });
  }, []);

  return <NeonStepperNavigation id={id} dataIsHorizontal={true} dataIsNumbered={true} />;
}
```

Step with various states:

```jsx
import React, { useEffect } from 'react';
import { NeonStepperNavigation, getStepperNavigation, NeonButtonFooter } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function StepperNavigationWithStates() {
  const id = 'stepper-with-states';

  useEffect(() => {
    getStepperNavigation(id).then((stepperNav) => {
      stepperNav.setSteps([
        { id: 'step-1', text: 'Complete Step', subtext: 'This step is complete', getStateBeforeLeavingStep: () => 'complete' },
        { id: 'step-2', text: 'In-Progress Step', subtext: 'This step is in progress', getStateBeforeLeavingStep: () => 'in-progress' },
        { id: 'step-3', text: 'Error Step', subtext: 'This step has an error', getStateBeforeLeavingStep: () => 'error' },
        { id: 'step-4', text: 'Default Step', subtext: 'This step has no state', getStateBeforeLeavingStep: () => 'untouched' },
        { id: 'step-5', text: 'Disabled Step', subtext: 'This step is disabled', getStateBeforeLeavingStep: () => 'untouched' }
      ]);

      // Apply states
      stepperNav.setStepState('step-1', 'complete');
      stepperNav.setStepState('step-2', 'in-progress');
      stepperNav.setStepState('step-3', 'error');
      stepperNav.setStepToDisabled('step-5');
    });
  }, []);

  return <NeonStepperNavigation id={id} />;
}
```


# NeonSystemBanner

A system-wide banner component for displaying important announcements, notifications, or alerts to users across an application.

## When To Use

Use the NeonSystemBanner component when you need to:

- Display important system-wide announcements or notifications
- Alert users about maintenance, outages, or critical updates
- Provide time-sensitive information that applies to the entire application
- Create a consistent notification system across your application
- Display warnings or alerts that require immediate attention
- Include actionable buttons related to the announcement
- Show information that should appear at the top of the application
- Implement application-wide messaging that persists across navigation

NeonSystemBanner is designed to be prominently displayed, typically at the top of an application, to ensure users see important information. Use it for critical announcements that require visibility across the entire application. For less urgent or localized notifications, consider using NeonSystemMessage or NeonToast components instead.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the system banner |
| dataText | string | Yes | - | The main text to show in the system banner |
| dataIcon | string | No | undefined | The icon to show in the system banner |
| children | React.ReactNode | No | - | Content to display inside the banner |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles for the banner |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| neon-system-banner-buttons | No | This slot contains the buttons that show up in the system banner |

## Examples

Simple system banner with text and icon:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonSystemBanner, NeonButton } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function SystemBannerExampleSimple() {
  return (
    <NeonSystemBanner dataText="This is some text" dataIcon="face">
      <div data-slot="neon-system-banner-buttons">
        <NeonButton
          id="system-banner-button"
          dataText="Action"
          onClick={() => {
            console.log('Button clicked');
          }}
        />
      </div>
    </NeonSystemBanner>
  );
}
```

System banner with application shell integration:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonButton } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { showSystemBanner, hideTopSystemBanner, hideSystemBanner } from '@neon/exported-utils';

export function SystemBannerExampleAppShell() {
  return <div>
    <NeonButton
      id="show-system-banner"
      dataText="Show system banner"
      onClick={() => {
        // NOTE: This only works when your MFE is injected into an application setup to listen for
        // 'application-shell.system-banner.show' mfe events.
        // It will already be in place if your application is using the ApplicationShell React component.
        showSystemBanner('my-mfe', 'mock-remote', 'mock-url', 'mock-module');
      }}
    />
    <NeonButton
      id="hide-top-system-banner"
      dataText="Hide top system banner"
      onClick={() => {
        // NOTE: This only works when your MFE is injected into an application setup to listen for
        // 'application-shell.system-banner.hide-top' mfe events.
        // It will already be in place if your application is using the ApplicationShell React component.
        hideTopSystemBanner('my-mfe');
      }}
    />
    <NeonButton
      id="hide-specific-system-banner"
      dataText="Hide example system banner"
      onClick={() => {
        // NOTE: This only works when your MFE is injected into an application setup to listen for
        // 'application-shell.system-banner.hide' mfe events.
        // It will already be in place if your application is using the ApplicationShell React component.
        hideSystemBanner('my-mfe', 'mock-remote', 'mock-url', 'mock-module');
      }}
    />
  </div>;
}
```

Custom system banner with multiple action buttons:

# NeonSystemMessage

A versatile alert component to display different types of messages with consistent styling and behavior across the application.

## When To Use

Use the NeonSystemMessage component when you need to:

- Display feedback to users about their actions (success, error, etc.)
- Provide warnings about potential issues or important information
- Show validation errors for forms or inputs
- Give users updates or notices about system status
- Present critical alerts that require attention
- Display dismissable notifications
- Show both persistent and temporary messages
- Provide contextual information inline within content areas

NeonSystemMessage supports different severity levels (success, info, warning, error) and can be displayed either inline within content or as floating notifications. For application-wide message management, consider using it with NeonMessages as a container for multiple notifications.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the message |
| dataType | string | No | 'info' | Type of message. Options: 'success', 'info', 'warning', 'error' |
| dataPosition | string | No | 'inline' | Position of the message. Options: 'inline', 'floating' |
| dataIsDismissable | boolean | No | false | Whether the user can dismiss the message |
| dataTitle | string | No | - | Optional title or heading for the message |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |
| ariaLabel | string | No | - | Accessible label for the message |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| message-content | Yes | The main content of the message (text, links, etc.) |

## Events

| Name | Description |
|------|-------------|
| neonSystemMessageClose | Fired when the user dismisses a message with the close button |

## Examples

Basic inline message:

```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { showSystemMessage, closeSystemMessageById } from '@neon/exported-utils';

export function SystemMessageUtilityExample() {
  const showMessage = () => {
    showSystemMessage('This is a temporary notification', {
      messageType: 'info',
      title: 'Notification',
      autoDismiss: true,
      autoDismissTime: 5000,
      sendTo: 'messages-container'
    });
  };

  const showPersistentMessage = () => {
    showSystemMessage('This message requires manual dismissal', {
      messageType: 'warning',
      title: 'Important',
      autoDismiss: false,
      dismissable: true,
      sendTo: 'messages-container'
    });
  };

  const closeMessage = (id) => {
    closeSystemMessageById(id);
  };

  return (
    <div>
      <button onClick={showMessage}>Show Temporary Message</button>
      <button onClick={showPersistentMessage}>Show Persistent Message</button>
      <div id="messages-container"></div>
    </div>
  );
}
```
