# NeonTableHeader

A component for creating sortable table column headers that provides both visual indicators and accessibility features for table sorting functionality.

## When To Use

Use the NeonTableHeader component when you need to:

- Create sortable tables with interactive column headers
- Provide visual indication of sort direction (ascending/descending)
- Implement accessible table sorting functionality
- Create consistent table header styling across your application
- Support responsive tables that work well on both desktop and mobile
- Allow users to sort tabular data by different columns
- Implement tables where multiple columns can be sortable
- Combine sorting functionality with other table features like filtering or pagination

NeonTableHeader integrates with tables to provide intuitive sorting capabilities while maintaining accessibility standards. It can be combined with other components like NeonSelectField to provide mobile-friendly sorting interfaces.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the table header |
| dataText | string | Yes | - | Text displayed in the table header |
| dataSortControllerId | string | No | - | ID of the sort controller for linking multiple headers |
| dataHeaderName | string | No | - | Alternative name for the header when using with sort controller |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Tooltip text to show on hover |
| dataTooltipIcon | string | No | 'circle-info' | Icon to use for tooltip |
| dataHorizontalAlign | string | No | 'left' | Alignment of header content. Options: 'left', 'center', 'right' |
| dataAutoAriaSort | boolean | No | true | Whether to automatically set aria-sort attributes |
| dataAutoTableCaption | boolean | No | true | Whether to add a table caption automatically |
| dataButtonAriaLabel | string | No | - | Aria label for the sort button |

## Utility Functions

The NeonTableHeader component provides utility functions for managing sort controllers:

- `getSortController(sortControllerId: string)`: Gets or creates a sort controller instance
- `deleteSortController(sortControllerId: string)`: Removes a sort controller (for cleanup)

## Examples

Simple sortable table:
```jsx
import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { NeonTableHeader, getSortController, deleteSortController } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { type SortController } from '@neon/interfaces';
import { naturalSort } from '@neon/exported-utils';

const unsortedData = [
  {product: 'Nintendo Switch', cost: 299.99, quantity: 2},
  {product: 'Xbox Series X', cost: 499.99, quantity: 0},
  {product: 'Playstation 5', cost: 499.99, quantity: 0},
];

export function TableHeaderExampleSimple() {
  const [ currentSort, setCurrentSort ] = useState('');
  const [ tableRows, setTableRows ] = useState(unsortedData);
  let unsubscribe;

  useEffect(() => {
    getSortController('table-1-sort-controller').then((sortController) => {
      unsubscribe = sortController.getChangeStream().subscribe(() => {
        if (sortController.getSortDirection() == null || sortController.getCurrentSort() == null) {
          setCurrentSort('');
          setTableRows(unsortedData);
        } else {
          setCurrentSort(sortController.getCurrentSort() + '|' + sortController.getSortDirection());

          switch (sortController.getCurrentSort()) {
            case 'product-column':
              setTableRows(naturalSort.sortObjects(unsortedData, ['product'], sortController.getSortDirection() === 'descending'));
              break;
            case 'cost-column':
              setTableRows(naturalSort.sortObjects(unsortedData, ['cost'], sortController.getSortDirection() === 'descending'));
              break;
            case 'quantity-column':
              setTableRows(naturalSort.sortObjects(unsortedData, ['quantity'], sortController.getSortDirection() === 'descending'));
              break;
          }
        }
      });
    });

    return () => {
      if (unsubscribe != null) {
        unsubscribe();
        deleteSortController('table-1-sort-controller');
      }
    };
  }, []);

  return (
    <table className="__neon__table-full-width __neon__table-on-white-background __neon__table-simple">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>
            <NeonTableHeader
              id="product-column"
              dataSortControllerId="table-1-sort-controller"
              dataText="Product"
            />
          </th>
          <th className="__neon__table-simple-cell-is-numeric">
            <NeonTableHeader
              id="cost-column"
              dataSortControllerId="table-1-sort-controller"
              dataText="Cost"
            />
          </th>
          <th className="__neon__table-simple-cell-is-numeric">
            <NeonTableHeader
              id="quantity-column"
              dataSortControllerId="table-1-sort-controller"
              dataText="Quantity"
              dataTooltipText="Number of items in stock"
            />
          </th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {tableRows.map((row, index) => (
          <tr key={index}>
            <td data-label="Product">{row.product}</td>
            <td data-label="Cost">{row.cost}</td>
            <td data-label="Quantity">{row.quantity}</td>
          </tr>
        ))}
      </tbody>
    </table>
  );
}
```

Table with responsive mobile sorting:
```jsx
import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { NeonSelectField, NeonTableHeader, getSortController, deleteSortController } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { type SortController } from '@neon/interfaces';
import { naturalSort } from '@neon/exported-utils';

const unsortedData = [
  {product: 'Nintendo Switch', cost: 299.99, quantity: 2},
  {product: 'Xbox Series X', cost: 499.99, quantity: 0},
  {product: 'Playstation 5', cost: 499.99, quantity: 0},
];

export function TableHeaderExampleWithMobileSorting() {
  const [ currentSort, setCurrentSort ] = useState('');
  const [ tableRows, setTableRows ] = useState(unsortedData);
  let unsubscribe;

  useEffect(() => {
    getSortController('table-1-sort-controller').then((sortController) => {
      unsubscribe = sortController.getChangeStream().subscribe(() => {
        if (sortController.getSortDirection() == null || sortController.getCurrentSort() == null) {
          setCurrentSort('');
          setTableRows(unsortedData);
        } else {
          setCurrentSort(sortController.getCurrentSort() + '|' + sortController.getSortDirection());

          switch (sortController.getCurrentSort()) {
            case 'product-column':
              setTableRows(naturalSort.sortObjects(unsortedData, ['product'], sortController.getSortDirection() === 'descending'));
              break;
            case 'cost-column':
              setTableRows(naturalSort.sortObjects(unsortedData, ['cost'], sortController.getSortDirection() === 'descending'));
              break;
            case 'quantity-column':
              setTableRows(naturalSort.sortObjects(unsortedData, ['quantity'], sortController.getSortDirection() === 'descending'));
              break;
          }
        }
      });
    });

    return () => {
      if (unsubscribe != null) {
        unsubscribe();
        deleteSortController('table-1-sort-controller');
      }
    };
  }, []);

  return (
    <div className="__neon__table-responsive-container-wrapper">
      <div className="__neon__table-control-container-md">
        <NeonSelectField
          id="mobile-sort-select"
          dataLabelText="Sort By"
          options={[
            {text: 'Product (ascending)', value: 'product-column|ascending'},
            {text: 'Product (descending)', value: 'product-column|descending'},
            {text: 'Cost (ascending)', value: 'cost-column|ascending'},
            {text: 'Cost (descending)', value: 'cost-column|descending'},
            {text: 'Quantity (ascending)', value: 'quantity-column|ascending'},
            {text: 'Quantity (descending)', value: 'quantity-column|descending'},
          ]}
          modelValue={currentSort}
          modelValueChange={(value) => {
            const valueToSet = value || '';
            setCurrentSort(valueToSet);
            getSortController('table-1-sort-controller').then((sortController) => {
              sortController.setSortAndDirection(...valueToSet.split('|'));
            });
          }}
        />
      </div>
      <table className="__neon__table-full-width __neon__table-on-white-background __neon__table-simple __neon__table-responsive-container-md">
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th>
              <NeonTableHeader
                id="product-column"
                dataSortControllerId="table-1-sort-controller"
                dataText="Product"
              />
            </th>
            <th className="__neon__table-simple-cell-is-numeric">
              <NeonTableHeader
                id="cost-column"
                dataSortControllerId="table-1-sort-controller"
                dataText="Cost"
              />
            </th>
            <th className="__neon__table-simple-cell-is-numeric">
              <NeonTableHeader
                id="quantity-column"
                dataSortControllerId="table-1-sort-controller"
                dataText="Quantity"
                dataTooltipText="Number of items in stock"
              />
            </th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {tableRows.map((row, index) => (
            <tr key={index}>
              <td data-label="Product">{row.product}</td>
              <td data-label="Cost">{row.cost}</td>
              <td data-label="Quantity">{row.quantity}</td>
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Table with filtering and sorting:
```jsx
import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
import { NeonSelectField, NeonTableHeader, NeonTextField, getSortController, deleteSortController } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { type SortController } from '@neon/interfaces';
import { naturalSort } from '@neon/exported-utils';

const unsortedData = [
  {firstName: 'Harry', lastName: 'Potter'},
  {firstName: 'Hermione', lastName: 'Granger'},
  {firstName: 'Ron', lastName: 'Weasley'},
  {firstName: 'Draco', lastName: 'Malfoy'},
];

const sortMap = {
  'first-name-column': ['firstName'],
  'last-name-column': ['lastName']
};

export function TableHeaderExampleWithFilter() {
  // Filter control state
  const [ filterTextFirstName, setFilterTextFirstName ] = useState('');
  const [ filterTextLastName, setFilterTextLastName ] = useState('');

  // Sort control state
  const [ currentSort, setCurrentSort ] = useState('');

  // Pipeline Data
  const [ filteredData, setFilteredData ] = useState(unsortedData.slice());
  const [ sortedData, setSortedData ] = useState(unsortedData);

  useEffect(() => {
    let unsubscribe;
    getSortController('filter-sort-controller').then((sortController) => {
      unsubscribe = sortController.getChangeStream().subscribe(() => {
        if (sortController.getSortDirection() == null || sortController.getCurrentSort() == null) {
          setCurrentSort('');
        } else {
          setCurrentSort(sortController.getCurrentSort() + '|' + sortController.getSortDirection());
        }
        runSort(filteredData, sortController);
      });
    });

    return () => {
      if (unsubscribe != null) {
        unsubscribe();
      }
    };
  }, [filteredData]);

  useEffect(() => {
    return () => {
      deleteSortController('filter-sort-controller');
    };
  }, []);

  function runFilterSort(firstNameFilterString, lastNameFilterString) {
    getSortController('filter-sort-controller').then((sortController) => {
      const firstNameFilterStringLc = (firstNameFilterString || '').toLowerCase();
      const lastNameFilterStringLc = (lastNameFilterString || '').toLowerCase();
      const filteredRows = unsortedData.filter((obj) => {
        return obj.firstName.toLowerCase().includes(firstNameFilterStringLc) &&
               obj.lastName.toLowerCase().includes(lastNameFilterStringLc);
      });

      setFilteredData(filteredRows);
      runSort(filteredRows, sortController);
    });
  }

  function runSort(filteredData, sortController) {
    let sortedRows = filteredData;
    if (sortController.getSortDirection() != null && sortController.getCurrentSort() != null) {
      sortedRows = naturalSort.sortObjects(
        filteredData,
        sortMap[sortController.getCurrentSort() || ''],
        sortController.getSortDirection() === 'descending'
      );
    }
    setSortedData(sortedRows);
  }

  return (
    <>
      <div className="__neon__form">
        <div className="__neon__form-row">
          <NeonTextField
            id="search-field-first-name"
            dataLabelText="First Name"
            dataShowLabel="false"
            dataPlaceholderText="First Name"
            dataIcon="search"
            dataIsClearable="true"
            modelValue={filterTextFirstName}
            modelValueChange={(value) => {
              setFilterTextFirstName(value || '');
              runFilterSort(value, filterTextLastName);
            }}
          />
          <NeonTextField
            id="search-field-last-name"
            dataLabelText="Last Name"
            dataShowLabel="false"
            dataPlaceholderText="Last Name"
            dataIcon="search"
            dataIsClearable="true"
            modelValue={filterTextLastName}
            modelValueChange={(value) => {
              setFilterTextLastName(value || '');
              runFilterSort(filterTextFirstName, value);
            }}
          />
        </div>
      </div>
      <div className="__neon__table-responsive-container-wrapper">
        <div className="__neon__table-control-container-md">
          <NeonSelectField
            id="mobile-sort-select"
            dataLabelText="Sort By"
            options={[
              {text: 'First name (ascending)', value: 'first-name-column|ascending'},
              {text: 'First name (descending)', value: 'first-name-column|descending'},
              {text: 'Last name (ascending)', value: 'last-name-column|ascending'},
              {text: 'Last name (descending)', value: 'last-name-column|descending'}
            ]}
            modelValue={currentSort}
            modelValueChange={(value) => {
              const valueToSet = value || '';
              setCurrentSort(valueToSet);
              getSortController('filter-sort-controller').then((sortController) => {
                sortController.setSortAndDirection(...valueToSet.split('|'));
              });
            }}
          />
        </div>
        <table className="__neon__table-full-width __neon__table-on-white-background __neon__table-simple __neon__table-responsive-container-md">
          <thead>
            <tr>
              <th>
                <NeonTableHeader
                  id="first-name-column"
                  dataSortControllerId="filter-sort-controller"
                  dataText="First name"
                />
              </th>
              <th>
                <NeonTableHeader
                  id="last-name-column"
                  dataSortControllerId="filter-sort-controller"
                  dataText="Last name"
                />
              </th>
            </tr>
          </thead>
          <tbody>
            {sortedData.map((row, index) => (
              <tr key={index}>
                <td data-label="First name">{row.firstName}</td>
                <td data-label="Last name">{row.lastName}</td>
              </tr>
            ))}
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>
    </>
  );
}
```


# NeonTabsVertical

A vertical navigation component for switching between related content sections displayed along the side of content.

## When To Use

Use the NeonTabsVertical component when you need to:

- Create vertical navigation instead of horizontal tabs for space efficiency
- Navigate through related content sections within a confined space
- Implement navigation for settings pages, multi-step forms, or detailed content
- Make efficient use of vertical space when horizontal space is limited
- Provide a navigation menu that remains visible while content changes
- Display complex navigation options that need to be visible all at once
- Create a consistent sidebar navigation pattern across your application
- Implement responsive navigation that works well on both desktop and mobile screens

NeonTabsVertical offers a vertical alternative to the standard NeonTabs component. While standard tabs are displayed horizontally and are ideal for simpler navigation needs, vertical tabs provide better scalability for more complex navigation requirements, especially when you have many tabs or when the tab text might be longer.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the tabs component |
| tabs | Array<Tab> | Yes | - | Array of tab objects to display |
| currentTab | string | Yes | - | ID of the currently selected tab |
| dataLegend | string | Yes | - | Legend text for the fieldset (required for accessibility) |
| neonTabSelectionChanged | function | No | - | Callback fired when the selected tab changes |

### Tab Interface

Each tab in the `tabs` array requires the following properties:

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the tab |
| text | string | Yes | - | Display text for the tab |
| isDisabled | boolean | No | false | Whether the tab can be selected |
| showBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to show a badge |
| badgeCount | number | No | - | Number to display on badge |
| badgeOverflowCount | number | No | - | Maximum count to display before showing overflow |
| badgeShowZero | boolean | No | false | Whether to show badge when count is zero |
| badgeType | string | No | - | Color variant for the badge |
| onClickCallback | function | No | - | Callback when tab is clicked. Return true to prevent default tab selection behavior |

## Examples

Basic vertical tabs:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonTabsVertical } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function TabsVerticalExample() {
  const [currentTab, setCurrentTab] = useState('tab1');

  const tabs = [
    { id: 'tab1', text: 'General' },
    { id: 'tab2', text: 'Account' },
    { id: 'tab3', text: 'Security' }
  ];

  return (
    <div className="__neon__layout-tabs-vertical">
      <div className="__neon__layout-tabs-vertical-wrapper">
        <NeonTabsVertical
          id="settings-tabs"
          dataLegend="Settings Navigation"
          tabs={tabs}
          currentTab={currentTab}
          neonTabSelectionChanged={(tabId) => setCurrentTab(tabId)}
        />
      </div>
      <div className="__neon__layout-tabs-vertical-content">
        {currentTab === 'tab1' && <div>General settings content</div>}
        {currentTab === 'tab2' && <div>Account settings content</div>}
        {currentTab === 'tab3' && <div>Security settings content</div>}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Vertical tabs with badges:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonTabsVertical } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function TabsVerticalWithBadgesExample() {
  const [currentTab, setCurrentTab] = useState('tab1');

  const tabs = [
    { id: 'tab1', text: 'Messages', showBadge: true, badgeCount: 5, badgeType: 'error' },
    { id: 'tab2', text: 'Notifications', showBadge: true, badgeCount: 12, badgeType: 'warning' },
    { id: 'tab3', text: 'Settings' }
  ];

  return (
    <div className="__neon__layout-tabs-vertical">
      <div className="__neon__layout-tabs-vertical-wrapper">
        <NeonTabsVertical
          id="notification-tabs"
          dataLegend="Notification Center"
          tabs={tabs}
          currentTab={currentTab}
          neonTabSelectionChanged={(tabId) => setCurrentTab(tabId)}
        />
      </div>
      <div className="__neon__layout-tabs-vertical-content">
        {currentTab === 'tab1' && <div>Messages content</div>}
        {currentTab === 'tab2' && <div>Notifications content</div>}
        {currentTab === 'tab3' && <div>Settings content</div>}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Tabs with disabled state and custom click handler:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonTabsVertical } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function TabsVerticalAdvancedExample() {
  const [currentTab, setCurrentTab] = useState('tab1');

  const tabs = [
    { id: 'tab1', text: 'Overview' },
    { id: 'tab2', text: 'Details' },
    {
      id: 'tab3',
      text: 'Admin Settings',
      onClickCallback: () => {
        // Custom logic here, e.g., permission check
        const userHasPermission = checkUserPermission();

        if (!userHasPermission) {
          alert('You do not have permission to access this section');
          return true; // Prevent tab selection
        }
        return false; // Allow tab selection
      }
    },
    { id: 'tab4', text: 'Coming Soon', isDisabled: true }
  ];

  return (
    <div className="__neon__layout-tabs-vertical">
      <div className="__neon__layout-tabs-vertical-wrapper">
        <NeonTabsVertical
          id="advanced-tabs"
          dataLegend="Product Information"
          tabs={tabs}
          currentTab={currentTab}
          neonTabSelectionChanged={(tabId) => setCurrentTab(tabId)}
        />
      </div>
      <div className="__neon__layout-tabs-vertical-content">
        {currentTab === 'tab1' && <div>Overview content</div>}
        {currentTab === 'tab2' && <div>Details content</div>}
        {currentTab === 'tab3' && <div>Admin Settings content</div>}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Using vertical tabs with a card layout:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';

export function TabsVerticalInCardExample() {
  const [currentTab, setCurrentTab] = useState('tab1');

  const tabs = [
    { id: 'tab1', text: 'Personal Info' },
    { id: 'tab2', text: 'Contact Info' },

  ];

    <NeonCardStandard
      id="user-profile-card"
      dataHeading="User Profile"
      dataSubheading="Manage your profile information"
    >

          <div className="__neon__layout-tabs-vertical-wrapper">
            <NeonTabsVertical
              id="profile-tabs"
              dataLegend="Profile Navigation"
              tabs={tabs}
              currentTab={currentTab}
              neonTabSelectionChanged={(tabId) => setCurrentTab(tabId)}
            />
          </div>
          <div className="__neon__layout-tabs-vertical-content">
            {currentTab === 'tab1' && <div>Personal information form</div>}
            {currentTab === 'tab2' && <div>Contact information form</div>}
            {currentTab === 'tab3' && <div>User preferences form</div>}
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </NeonCardStandard>
  );
}
```


# NeonTabs

A navigation component for organizing content into selectable tabs with corresponding panels.

## When To Use

Use the NeonTabs component when you need to:

- Organize related content into separate views without leaving the page
- Allow users to switch between different sections of content
- Create interfaces with content that can be categorized into discrete sections
- Save screen space by showing only one section at a time
- Build a navigation pattern for different views of the same type of content
- Create form sections that are logically separated but related
- Implement a UI pattern that maintains context while changing content
- Preserve user's current page context while allowing access to different content sections

NeonTabs is ideal for interfaces where users need to navigate between related sections of content without changing the overall page context. For vertical tab layouts, consider using NeonTabsVertical instead, which is better suited for longer lists of tabs or when screen width is limited.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the tabs component |
| dataTabs | Array<TabItem> | Yes | - | Array of tab configurations |
| modelValue | string \| undefined | Yes | - | ID of the currently selected tab |
| modelValueChange | function | Yes | - | Handler for tab selection changes: (tabId: string) => void |
| dataShowBorder | boolean | No | true | Whether to show a border below the tabs |
| dataFullWidth | boolean | No | false | Whether tabs should fill the full width of the container |
| dataAlign | string | No | 'left' | Alignment of the tabs. Options: 'left', 'center', 'right' |
| dataSize | string | No | 'medium' | Size of the tabs. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large' |
| dataDisabled | boolean | No | false | Whether all tabs are disabled |
| dataAriaLabel | string | No | - | Accessibility label for the tabs component |
| dataPosition | string | No | 'top' | Position of the tabs. Options: 'top', 'bottom' |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |

### TabItem Interface

```typescript
interface TabItem {
  id: string;
  label: string;
  disabled?: boolean;
  icon?: string;
  badge?: string | number;
  badgeVariant?: 'default' | 'info' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error';
  content?: React.ReactNode;
}
```

## Examples

Basic tabs:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonTabs } from '@neon/react-adapters';

function BasicTabsExample() {
  const [activeTab, setActiveTab] = useState('tab1');
  
  const tabs = [
    {
      id: 'tab1',
      label: 'Details',
      content: <div>This tab contains product details</div>
    },
    {
      id: 'tab2',
      label: 'Specifications',
      content: <div>This tab shows product specifications</div>
    },
    {
      id: 'tab3',
      label: 'Reviews',
      content: <div>This tab displays customer reviews</div>
    }
  ];
  
  return (
    <NeonTabs
      id="product-tabs"
      dataTabs={tabs}
      modelValue={activeTab}
      modelValueChange={(tabId) => setActiveTab(tabId)}
    />
  );
}
```

Tabs with icons:
```jsx
<NeonTabs
  id="profile-tabs"
  dataTabs={[
    {
      id: 'personal',
      label: 'Personal Info',
      icon: 'user',
      content: <PersonalInfoForm />
    },
    {
      id: 'security',
      label: 'Security',
      icon: 'lock',
      content: <SecuritySettings />
    },
    {
      id: 'billing',
      label: 'Billing',
      icon: 'credit-card',
      content: <BillingDetails />
    },
    {
      id: 'notifications',
      label: 'Notifications',
      icon: 'bell',
      content: <NotificationPreferences />
    }
  ]}
  modelValue={profileTab}
  modelValueChange={setProfileTab}
  dataShowBorder={true}
/>
```

Tabs with badges:
```jsx
<NeonTabs
  id="inbox-tabs"
  dataTabs={[
    {
      id: 'inbox',
      label: 'Inbox',
      badge: unreadCount,
      badgeVariant: 'info',
      content: <InboxMessages />
    },
    {
      id: 'important',
      label: 'Important',
      badge: importantCount,
      badgeVariant: 'warning',
      content: <ImportantMessages />
    },
    {
      id: 'archived',
      label: 'Archived',
      content: <ArchivedMessages />
    }
  ]}
  modelValue={inboxTab}
  modelValueChange={setInboxTab}
  dataSize="large"
/>
```

Full-width tabs:
```jsx
<NeonTabs
  id="form-wizard-tabs"
  dataTabs={[
    { id: 'step1', label: 'Step 1', content: <Step1Form /> },
    { id: 'step2', label: 'Step 2', content: <Step2Form /> },
    { id: 'step3', label: 'Step 3', content: <Step3Form /> },
    { id: 'review', label: 'Review', content: <ReviewForm /> }
  ]}
  modelValue={currentStep}
  modelValueChange={setCurrentStep}
  dataFullWidth={true}
  dataAlign="center"
/>
```

Disabled tabs:
```jsx
<NeonTabs
  id="account-tabs"
  dataTabs={[
    { id: 'profile', label: 'Profile', content: <ProfileView /> },
    { id: 'admin', label: 'Admin Settings', content: <AdminSettings />, disabled: !isAdmin },
    { id: 'developer', label: 'Developer Tools', content: <DeveloperTools />, disabled: !isDeveloper }
  ]}
  modelValue={accountTab}
  modelValueChange={setAccountTab}
/>
```

Bottom-positioned tabs:
```jsx
<NeonTabs
  id="media-tabs"
  dataTabs={[
    { id: 'images', label: 'Images', icon: 'image', content: <ImageGallery /> },
    { id: 'videos', label: 'Videos', icon: 'video', content: <VideoGallery /> },
    { id: 'audio', label: 'Audio', icon: 'music', content: <AudioPlayer /> }
  ]}
  modelValue={mediaType}
  modelValueChange={setMediaType}
  dataPosition="bottom"
/>
```




# NeonTag

A versatile tag component for displaying short, labeled information with optional icons, subtexts, and positioning options.

## When To Use

Use the NeonTag component when you need to:

- Display categorized or labeled information in a compact, visually distinct format
- Highlight status, category, or attribute information
- Show metadata associated with content
- Add visual indicators to various UI elements
- Create badges or labels with consistent styling
- Position indicators relative to other components (top, bottom, corners, etc.)
- Show short supplementary information with optional subtext
- Create visual classifications using color-coding

NeonTag is ideal for providing quick visual cues that help users identify categories, statuses, or attributes at a glance. The component supports various colors, positions, and can include icons and subtexts for enhanced information display.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | No | - | Unique identifier for the tag |
| dataText | string | Yes | - | Sets the main text that shows up on the tag |
| dataSubText | string | No | - | Sets the smaller text to the right of the \| and main text |
| dataIcon | string | No | - | Sets which icon to show. See the icons page for a list of names |
| dataType | string | No | 'gray' | Sets the overall style/color of the tag (yellow, orange, red, magenta, purple, cyan, navy, green, teal, gray, update) |
| dataPosition | string | No | - | Sets the position of the tag (top, bottom, left, right, top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right, fixed) |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles for the tag |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |

## Examples

Basic tags with different types:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonTag } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function TagExampleType() {
  return <>
    <NeonTag dataText="Default"></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataType="yellow" dataText="Yellow"></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataType="orange" dataText="Orange"></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataType="red" dataText="Red"></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataType="magenta" dataText="Magenta"></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataType="purple" dataText="Purple"></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataType="cyan" dataText="Cyan"></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataType="navy" dataText="Navy"></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataType="green" dataText="Green"></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataType="teal" dataText="Teal"></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataType="gray" dataText="Gray"></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataType="update" dataText="Update"></NeonTag>
  </>;
}
```

Tags with icons:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonTag } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function TagExampleIcon() {
  return <>
    <NeonTag dataText="Tag Icon One" dataIcon="hearing"></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataText="Tag Icon Two" dataIcon="calendar-event"></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataText="Tag Icon Three" dataIcon="star-solid"></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataText="Tag Icon Three" dataIcon="web-www"></NeonTag>
  </>;
}
```

Tag with subtext:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonTag } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function TagExampleSubText() {
  return <>
    <NeonTag dataText="Data Text" dataSubText="Sub Text"></NeonTag>
  </>;
}
```

Tags with different positioning:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonTag } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function TagExamplePosition() {
  return <>
    <NeonTag dataText="Top" dataPosition="top" style={{position: 'inherit'}}></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataText="Bottom" dataPosition="bottom" style={{position: 'inherit'}}></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataText="Left" dataPosition="left" style={{position: 'inherit'}}></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataText="Right" dataPosition="right" style={{position: 'inherit'}}></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataText="Top Left" dataPosition="top-left" style={{position: 'inherit'}}></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataText="Top Right" dataPosition="top-right" style={{position: 'inherit'}}></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataText="Bottom Left" dataPosition="bottom-left" style={{position: 'inherit'}}></NeonTag>
    <NeonTag dataText="Bottom Right" dataPosition="bottom-right" style={{position: 'inherit'}}></NeonTag>

```

Complete example with type, icon and subtext:
```jsx
import React from 'react';

export function TagCompleteExample() {
  return (
    <div style={{position: 'relative'}}>
      <NeonTag 
        dataText="Important" 
        dataSubText="New" 
        dataIcon="notification" 
        dataType="red" 
        dataPosition="top-right">
      </NeonTag>
      <p>Note: The parent element should have position: relative for positioned tags to work correctly.</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```


# NeonTextField

A text input field component that supports various validation, formatting, and display options.

## When To Use

Use the NeonTextField component when you need to:

- Collect single-line text input from users
- Implement form fields with validation requirements
- Create password fields with masked input
- Apply specific formatting or validation rules to user input
- Create search inputs or filters with clear functionality
- Implement email address inputs with built-in validation
- Create fields with character limits and constraints
- Add icon indicators to text inputs for better context

NeonTextField is the fundamental text input component for forms and should be your default choice for collecting short textual data from users. For multi-line text input, consider using NeonTextareaField instead.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the text field |
| dataLabelText | string | Yes | - | Label text for the field |
| modelValue | string \| undefined | Yes | - | Current value of the text field |
| modelValueChange | function | Yes | - | Handler for value changes: (value: string \| undefined) => void |
| dataShowLabel | boolean | No | true | Whether to show the label |
| dataPlaceholderText | string | No | - | Placeholder text when the field is empty |
| dataAriaLabel | string | No | - | Accessibility label for screen readers |
| dataHelperText | string | No | - | Helper text displayed below the field |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Text to show in a tooltip |
| dataSize | string | No | 'auto' | Width of the field. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'x-large', 'auto' |
| dataIsRequired | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is required |
| dataHideRequiredBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to hide the required indicator |
| dataShowOptionalBadge | boolean | No | false | Whether to show an optional indicator |
| dataIsReadOnly | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is read-only |
| dataIcon | string | No | - | Name of the icon to display in the field |
| dataIsClearable | boolean | No | false | Whether to show a clear button when the field has a value |
| dataRegex | string | No | - | Regular expression pattern for validation |
| dataRegexModifiers | string | No | - | Modifiers for the regex (e.g., 'i', 'g') |
| dataRegexErrorText | string | No | - | Error message to display when regex validation fails |
| dataIsRegexInverse | boolean | No | false | When true, validation passes when the input fails the regex |
| dataMinLength | number | No | - | Minimum number of characters required |
| dataMaxLength | number | No | - | Maximum number of characters allowed |
| dataExcludeChars | string | No | - | Characters that are not allowed in the input |
| dataIsEmail | boolean | No | false | Whether to validate the input as an email address |
| dataIsPassword | boolean | No | false | Whether to mask the input as a password field |
| dataShowCount | boolean | No | false | Whether to show a character count |
| dataSuccessMessage | string | No | - | Message to display when validation succeeds |
| dataLabelTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Whether to add space for label text alignment |
| dataHelperTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Whether to add space for helper text alignment |
| dataConstrainDescription | boolean | No | false | Whether to constrain description width to match the field |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is disabled |
| autocomplete | string | No | - | HTML autocomplete attribute value |
| customValidationFunction | function | No | - | Custom validation function |
| onBlur | function | No | - | Handler for blur events |
| blurInterceptor | function | No | - | Function called before blur processing |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |

## Examples

Basic text field:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonTextField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

function BasicTextFieldExample() {
  const [name, setName] = useState('');
  
  return (
    <NeonTextField
      id="user-name"
      dataLabelText="Name"
      modelValue={name}
      modelValueChange={(value) => setName(value)}
      dataPlaceholderText="Enter your name"
    />
  );
}
```

Required field with validation:
```jsx
<NeonTextField
  id="email-field"
  dataLabelText="Email Address"
  dataIsRequired={true}
  dataIsEmail={true}
  dataHelperText="Please enter a valid email address"
  modelValue={email}
  modelValueChange={setEmail}
  dataPlaceholderText="email@example.com"
/>
```

Password field:
```jsx
<NeonTextField
  id="password-field"
  dataLabelText="Password"
  dataIsPassword={true}
  dataIsRequired={true}
  dataMinLength={8}
  dataRegex="^(?=.*[a-z])(?=.*[A-Z])(?=.*\\d).*$"
  dataRegexErrorText="Password must contain at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, and one number"
  dataHelperText="Minimum 8 characters with at least 1 uppercase letter, 1 lowercase letter, and 1 number"
  modelValue={password}
  modelValueChange={setPassword}
/>
```

Field with icon and clear button:
```jsx
<NeonTextField
  id="search-field"
  dataLabelText="Search"
  dataIcon="search"
  dataIsClearable={true}
  dataPlaceholderText="Search for products..."
  modelValue={searchTerm}
  modelValueChange={setSearchTerm}
/>
```

Character-limited field with counter:
```jsx
<NeonTextField
  id="tweet-field"
  dataLabelText="Tweet"
  dataMaxLength={280}
  dataShowCount={true}
  dataHelperText="Maximum 280 characters"
  modelValue={tweetText}
  modelValueChange={setTweetText}
/>
```

Disabled field:
```jsx
<NeonTextField
  id="username-field"
  dataLabelText="Username"
  modelValue="johndoe123"
  modelValueChange={() => {}} // No-op since field is disabled
  disabled={true}
/>
```

Custom field size:
```jsx
<NeonTextField
  id="short-code-field"
  dataLabelText="Verification Code"
  dataSize="small"
  modelValue={verificationCode}
  modelValueChange={setVerificationCode}
  dataPlaceholderText="Enter code"
/>
```




# NeonTextareaField

A flexible textarea component for capturing multi-line text input with built-in validation and formatting options.

## When To Use

Use the NeonTextareaField component when you need to:

- Collect longer text responses from users that might span multiple lines
- Allow users to enter descriptions, comments, feedback, or other free-form text
- Create form fields where users need more space than a standard text field provides
- Implement text areas with character counts, validation rules, or formatting requirements
- Display multi-line text input with consistent styling and behavior across your application
- Capture text input that requires validation (minimum/maximum length, regex patterns)
- Provide users with a resizable text area for variable-length content

NeonTextareaField is the primary multi-line text input component in the Neon Design System. It extends the functionality of standard text inputs with additional features like character counting, validation, and integration with the form system.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the textarea field |
| modelValue | string \| undefined | Yes | - | A string that represents the value entered. Undefined if not set or invalid |
| modelValueChange | (value: string \| undefined) => void | Yes | - | The callback is called whenever the user changes the textarea |
| dataLabelText | string | Yes | - | Text label for the textarea field |
| dataHelperText | string | No | - | Helper text displayed below the textarea |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Tooltip text displayed on hover of the info icon |
| dataIsRequired | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is required |
| dataHideRequiredBadge | boolean | No | false | Hide the required indicator even if the field is required |
| dataShowOptionalBadge | boolean | No | false | Show an optional indicator if the field is not required |
| dataShowLabel | boolean | No | true | Whether to show the field label |
| dataShowCount | boolean | No | false | Whether to show character count in the UI |
| dataLabelTextSpace | string | No | - | Controls the spacing between the label and textarea |
| dataHelperTextSpace | string | No | - | Controls the spacing between the textarea and helper text |
| dataConstrainDescription | boolean | No | false | Whether to constrain the helper text width |
| dataSize | string | No | - | Size of the textarea ('small', 'medium', or 'large') |
| dataAriaLabel | string | No | - | Accessibility label for screen readers |
| dataIsReadOnly | boolean | No | false | Makes the field read-only when set to true |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Disables interactions with the textarea when true |
| autocomplete | string | No | - | HTML autocomplete attribute value |
| dataPlaceholderText | string | No | - | Placeholder text shown when the textarea is empty |
| dataRegex | string | No | - | Regex pattern to validate the input against |
| dataRegexModifiers | string | No | - | Modifiers for the regex pattern (e.g., 'i', 'g') |
| dataRegexErrorText | string | No | - | Error message shown when the regex validation fails |
| dataIsRegexInverse | boolean | No | false | Inverts the regex validation logic when true |
| dataMinLength | number | No | - | Minimum number of characters required |
| dataMaxLength | number | No | - | Maximum number of characters allowed |
| dataExcludeChars | string | No | - | Characters that are not allowed in the input |
| dataSuccessMessage | string | No | - | Message displayed when validation succeeds |
| customValidationFunction | function | No | - | Custom validation function for complex validations |
| blurInterceptor | function | No | - | Function called when the field loses focus |
| onBlur | function | No | - | Event handler for blur events |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |

## Examples

Simple textarea:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonTextareaField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function TextareaFieldExampleSimple() {
  const [description, setDescription] = useState();

  return (
    <NeonTextareaField
      id="description"
      dataLabelText="Description"
      dataShowLabel="false"
      modelValue={description}
      modelValueChange={(desc) => { setDescription(desc); }}
    />
  );
}
```

Form field with validation:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonTextareaField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function TextareaFieldExampleFormField() {
  const [message, setMessage] = useState();

  return (
    <NeonTextareaField
      id="message"
      dataLabelText="Message"
      dataShowLabel="true"
      dataIsRequired="true"
      dataHelperText="Please provide a message."
      dataTooltipText="Write something about you here."
      modelValue={message}
      modelValueChange={(msg) => { setMessage(msg); }}
    />
  );
}
```

Textarea with character limit and count:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonTextareaField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function TextareaFieldExampleWithCharCount() {
  const [feedback, setFeedback] = useState();

  return (
    <NeonTextareaField
      id="feedback"
      dataLabelText="Feedback"
      dataHelperText="Maximum 500 characters"
      dataShowCount={true}
      dataMaxLength={500}
      modelValue={feedback}
      modelValueChange={(value) => { setFeedback(value); }}
    />
  );
}
```

Textarea with regex validation:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonTextareaField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function TextareaFieldExampleWithRegex() {
  const [code, setCode] = useState();

  return (
    <NeonTextareaField
      id="code"
      dataLabelText="Code Sample"
      dataRegex="^[A-Za-z0-9\s]+$"
      dataRegexErrorText="Only letters, numbers and spaces are allowed"
      dataHelperText="Enter a code sample using only alphanumeric characters"
      modelValue={code}
      modelValueChange={(value) => { setCode(value); }}
    />
  );
}
```

Disabled textarea:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonTextareaField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function TextareaFieldExampleDisabled() {
  return (
    <NeonTextareaField
      id="disabled-textarea"
      dataLabelText="Comments (disabled)"
      disabled={true}
      modelValue="This textarea field is disabled and cannot be edited."
      modelValueChange={() => {}}
    />
  );
}
```


# NeonTimeField

A form input component that allows users to select or enter time values in a standardized format.

## When To Use

Use the NeonTimeField component when you need to:

- Collect time input from users in a consistent format
- Allow users to select a time value from a dropdown picker
- Capture appointment times, meeting times, or schedule information
- Enforce time format validation automatically
- Set minimum or maximum time constraints for inputs
- Implement accessible time selection in forms
- Create time-based filtering or search inputs

NeonTimeField is designed to handle time data specifically, ensuring proper formatting and validation while providing an intuitive user experience. It integrates with the Time type from the MFE utils library to handle time values consistently.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the field |
| dataLabelText | string | Yes | - | Label text for the field |
| modelValue | Time \| undefined | Yes | - | The current time value |
| modelValueChange | function | Yes | - | Callback fired when the time value changes |
| dataShowLabel | boolean | No | true | Whether to show the label |
| dataAriaLabel | string | No | - | Accessible label for screen readers |
| dataTooltipText | string | No | - | Text to display in tooltip |
| dataHelperText | string | No | - | Helper text displayed below the field |
| dataSize | string | No | 'auto' | Width of the field. Options: 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'x-large', 'auto' |
| dataSuccessMessage | string | No | - | Message to display when validation passes |
| dataIsRequired | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is required |
| dataHideRequiredBadge | boolean | No | false | Hide the required indicator badge |
| dataShowOptionalBadge | boolean | No | false | Show an optional indicator badge |
| dataLabelTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Add extra space after the label |
| dataHelperTextSpace | boolean | No | false | Add extra space after helper text |
| dataConstrainDescription | boolean | No | false | Constrain the description text width |
| dataIsReadOnly | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is read-only |
| disabled | boolean | No | false | Whether the field is disabled |
| autocomplete | string | No | - | HTML autocomplete attribute value |
| dataPlaceholderText | string | No | - | Placeholder text shown when field is empty |
| dataMinValue | string | No | - | Minimum time value allowed (format: HH:MM) |
| dataMaxValue | string | No | - | Maximum time value allowed (format: HH:MM) |
| customValidationFunction | function | No | - | Custom validation function |
| blurInterceptor | function | No | - | Function called when field loses focus |
| onBlur | function | No | - | Event handler for blur events |

## Examples

Simple time field:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonTimeField } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { type Time } from '@ps-refarch-ux/mfe-utils';

export function TimeFieldExampleSimple() {
  const [endTime, setEndTime] = useState<Time | undefined>();

  return (
    <NeonTimeField
      id="__mfe__end-time"
      dataLabelText="End Time"
      dataShowLabel="false"
      modelValue={endTime}
      modelValueChange={(time: Time | undefined): void => { setEndTime(time); }}
    />
  );
}
```

Form field with validation:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonTimeField } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { type Time } from '@ps-refarch-ux/mfe-utils';

export function TimeFieldExampleFormField() {
  const [time, setTime] = useState<Time | undefined>();

  return (
    <NeonTimeField
      id="__mfe__start-time"
      dataLabelText="Start Time"
      dataHelperText="Make sure you check the clock."
      dataIsRequired="true"
      dataShowLabel="true"
      dataTooltipText="What time is it?"
      modelValue={time}
      modelValueChange={(time: Time | undefined): void => { setTime(time); }}
    />
  );
}
```

Time field with min/max constraints:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonTimeField } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { SimpleTime, type Time } from '@ps-refarch-ux/mfe-utils';

export function TimeFieldExampleWithConstraints() {
  const [appointmentTime, setAppointmentTime] = useState<Time | undefined>(new SimpleTime(9, 0));
  const minTime = new SimpleTime(8, 30).to24HourTime(); // Earliest: 8:30 AM
  const maxTime = new SimpleTime(17, 0).to24HourTime(); // Latest: 5:00 PM

  return (
    <NeonTimeField
      id="appointment-time"
      dataLabelText="Appointment Time"
      dataHelperText="Business hours: 8:30 AM - 5:00 PM"
      dataIsRequired="true"
      dataMinValue={minTime}
      dataMaxValue={maxTime}
      modelValue={appointmentTime}
      modelValueChange={(time: Time | undefined): void => { setAppointmentTime(time); }}
    />
  );
}
```


# NeonTimePicker

A component that allows users to select a time using an interactive time picker interface.

## When To Use

Use the NeonTimePicker component when you need to:

- Allow users to select a specific time
- Provide an intuitive interface for time selection
- Standardize time input across your application
- Include time selection in forms or data entry interfaces
- Ensure consistent time format handling
- Enable precise time selection with hours and minutes
- Create accessible time selection interfaces

NeonTimePicker is the standard time selection component in the Neon Design System. For simpler time input needs or when you need a form field with a label, consider using NeonTimeField which incorporates this time picker with additional field capabilities.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the time picker |
| dataShowTimeDisplay | boolean | No | true | When set to false, removes the time display from the time picker |
| value | Time | No | Current time (rounded to nearest 5 minute interval) | The time that is shown in the time picker |
| neonValueChange | function | No | - | Callback function triggered when the selected time changes |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles |
| dataTestId | string | No | - | ID for testing purposes |
| ariaLabel | string | No | - | Accessible label for the time picker |

## Examples

Simple time picker:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonTimePicker } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { SimpleTime, type Time, formatTime } from '@ps-refarch-ux/mfe-utils';

export function TimePickerExampleSimple() {
  const [time, setTime] = useState<Time>(new SimpleTime(0, 30));

  return <>
    <NeonTimePicker
      id="time-picker-example"
      value={time}
      neonValueChange={(time: Time): void => {
        setTime(time);
      }}
    />
    <p className="__neon__text">
      Current Time: {formatTime(time, 'TIME')}
    </p>
  </>;
}
```

Time picker without time display:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonTimePicker } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { SimpleTime, type Time } from '@ps-refarch-ux/mfe-utils';

export function TimePickerExampleNoDisplay() {
  const [time, setTime] = useState<Time>(new SimpleTime(14, 30));

  return (
    <NeonTimePicker
      id="time-picker-no-display"
      dataShowTimeDisplay={false}
      value={time}
      neonValueChange={(time: Time): void => {
        setTime(time);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Time picker with default value:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonTimePicker } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { SimpleTime, type Time } from '@ps-refarch-ux/mfe-utils';

export function TimePickerExampleDefaultValue() {
  // Create a Time object for 2:45 PM
  const defaultTime = new SimpleTime(14, 45);

  return (
    <NeonTimePicker
      id="time-picker-default-value"
      value={defaultTime}
      neonValueChange={(time: Time): void => {
        console.log('Selected time:', time);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```


# NeonToast

A toast notification component for displaying brief, non-disruptive messages to users with optional actions and automatic dismissal.

## When To Use

Use the NeonToast component when you need to:

- Provide brief, non-blocking feedback to users about an action or state change
- Display notifications that don't require immediate user attention
- Show success, warning, error, or informational messages
- Present timely information that can be auto-dismissed after a period of time
- Provide quick actions related to the notification content
- Communicate status updates without disrupting the user's workflow
- Display transient messages that should appear temporarily and then disappear
- Show notifications with consistent styling across your application

NeonToast is designed for lightweight, temporary messaging that doesn't interrupt the user's current task. For more critical messages that require immediate attention, consider using NeonSystemMessage instead.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the toast |
| dataHeading | string | Yes | - | The heading text for the toast |
| dataSubheading | string | No | - | Additional descriptive text for the toast |
| dataType | string | No | 'info' | The type of toast notification. Options: 'success', 'error', 'warning', 'info' |
| datetime | Date | No | - | Timestamp for the toast notification |
| neonToastCloseButtonClick | function | Yes | - | Callback function triggered when the close button is clicked |
| children | React.ReactNode | No | - | Child elements to render within the toast |

## Slots

| Name | Required | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| toast-buttons | No | Area for action buttons related to the notification |

## Examples

Basic toast with required properties:

```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonToast } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ToastExampleRequired() {
  return (
    <NeonToast
      id="toast-required-example"
      dataHeading="This is a toast with required fields only"
      neonToastCloseButtonClick={() => { console.log('Toast closed'); }}
    />
  );
}
```

Toast with all properties:

```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonToast, NeonButton } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ToastExampleComplete() {
  return (
    <NeonToast
      id="toast-complete-example"
      dataType="info"
      dataHeading="This Toast shows all available fields"
      dataSubheading="This toast contains all the attributes that can be configured"
      neonToastCloseButtonClick={() => { console.log('Toast closed'); }}
      datetime={new Date()}
    >
      <div data-slot="toast-buttons">
        <NeonButton id="action-button" dataType="primary" dataText="Action" />
        <NeonButton id="cancel-button" dataText="Cancel" />
      </div>
    </NeonToast>
  );
}
```

Using the showToastMessage utility function:

```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonButton } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import {
  DEFAULT_TOAST_MESSAGE_FLOATING_ID,
  showToastMessage,
} from '@neon/exported-utils';

export function ToastMessageExample() {
  return (
    <NeonButton
      id="show-toast-button"
      dataType="primary"
      dataText="Show Success Toast"
      onClick={() => {
        showToastMessage(
          {
            heading: 'Operation Successful',
            subheading: 'Your changes have been saved',
            buttons: [],
            type: 'success'
          },
          {
            sendTo: DEFAULT_TOAST_MESSAGE_FLOATING_ID,
            autoDismiss: true,
            autoDismissTime: 5000,
            messageType: 'success',
          }
        );
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

Toast with custom buttons:

```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonToast, NeonButton } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function ToastExampleWithButtons() {
  return (
    <NeonToast
      id="toast-with-buttons"
      dataType="warning"
      dataHeading="Changes not saved"
      dataSubheading="Your recent changes have not been saved"
      neonToastCloseButtonClick={() => { console.log('Toast closed'); }}
    >
      <div data-slot="toast-buttons">
        <NeonButton
          id="discard-button"
          dataText="Discard"
          onClick={() => { console.log('Discarded changes'); }}
        />
        <NeonButton
          id="save-button"
          dataType="primary"
          dataText="Save Now"
          onClick={() => { console.log('Saving changes'); }}
        />
      </div>
    </NeonToast>
  );
}
```


# NeonTooltip

A lightweight tooltip component that displays helpful text or content when users hover over or focus on an element.

## When To Use

Use the NeonTooltip component when you need to:

- Provide additional context or explanation for UI elements without cluttering the interface
- Explain the function of icons, buttons, or other interactive elements
- Display supplementary information that doesn't require constant visibility
- Enhance accessibility by providing text descriptions for visual elements
- Show keyboard shortcuts or hints for power users
- Provide definitions or clarifications for abbreviated terms or technical concepts
- Display warnings or important notes about specific functionality
- Label elements that don't have visible text labels to improve usability

NeonTooltip is designed for brief, contextual information. For more complex interactions or content that users need to interact with, consider using NeonPopover or NeonModalDialog components instead.

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | No | - | Unique identifier for the tooltip |
| dataTargetId | string | Yes | - | The ID of the element that triggers the tooltip on hover/focus |
| dataPlacement | string | No | 'top' | Position of the tooltip relative to the target element. Options: 'top', 'top-start', 'top-end', 'right', 'right-start', 'right-end', 'bottom', 'bottom-start', 'bottom-end', 'left', 'left-start', 'left-end' |
| children | React.ReactNode | No | - | Content to display inside the tooltip |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS class name |
| style | object | No | - | Additional inline styles for the tooltip |

## Examples

Basic tooltip on a button:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonTooltip } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function BasicTooltipExample() {
  return (
    <div>
      <NeonButton id="example-button" dataText="Hover over me"/>
      <NeonTooltip dataTargetId="example-button">
        This is tooltip text that appears on hover or focus
      </NeonTooltip>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Tooltip with custom placement:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonTooltip } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function PlacementExample() {
  return (
    <div>
      <NeonButton id="top-start-button" dataText="Top Start Placement"/>
      <NeonTooltip dataPlacement="top-start" dataTargetId="top-start-button">
        Left justified tooltip (start)
      </NeonTooltip>

      <NeonButton id="right-button" dataText="Right Placement"/>
      <NeonTooltip dataPlacement="right" dataTargetId="right-button">
        Tooltip appears to the right
      </NeonTooltip>

      <NeonButton id="bottom-end-button" dataText="Bottom End Placement"/>
      <NeonTooltip dataPlacement="bottom-end" dataTargetId="bottom-end-button">
        Right justified tooltip at bottom (end)
      </NeonTooltip>
    </div>
  );
}
```

Tooltip with dynamic content:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonButton, NeonTooltip, NeonTextField } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function DynamicTooltipExample() {
  const [dynamicText, setDynamicText] = useState('Dynamic tooltip content');

  return (
    <>
      <div>
        <NeonTextField
          id="dynamic-content"
          dataLabelText="Dynamic Text Content"
          modelValue={dynamicText}
          modelValueChange={(value) => setDynamicText(value)}
        />
      </div>
      <div>
        <NeonButton id="dynamic-button" dataText="Hover for dynamic content"/>
        <NeonTooltip dataTargetId="dynamic-button">
          <span>{dynamicText}</span>
        </NeonTooltip>
      </div>
    </>
  );
}
```

Tooltip on non-focusable components:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonTooltip, NeonIcon, NeonIconStack } from '@neon/react-adapters';

export function NonFocusableExample() {
  return (
    <div>
      <NeonIconStack id="example-icon-stack" dataIcon="class-book" dataShape="hexagon" dataSize="large" dataColor="cyan"/>
      <NeonTooltip dataTargetId="example-icon-stack">
        Did you know? Books are just dead trees with stories inside!
      </NeonTooltip>

      <NeonIcon id="example-icon" dataIcon="volunteer-activism" dataSize="x-large"/>
      <NeonTooltip dataTargetId="example-icon">
        Volunteer activism is the practice of volunteering time and resources for the benefit of others.
      </NeonTooltip>
    </div>
  );
}
```


# NeonTree

A hierarchical tree component for displaying structured data with support for navigation, selection, and expandable/collapsible nodes.

## When To Use

Use the NeonTree component when you need to:

- Display hierarchical data with parent-child relationships
- Create a file/folder structure interface with expandable folders
- Implement a navigational tree menu with clickable links
- Create a multi-level selection interface with checkboxes
- Show organization charts or other nested data structures
- Present categories and subcategories in a collapsible format
- Create an expandable table of contents
- Implement a site navigation with expandable sections
- Visualize nested data structures like file systems, taxonomies, or organization charts
- Support lazy loading of large hierarchical datasets

NeonTree is versatile and can be configured in three primary modes: basic (for display only), navigation (for clickable links), and selectable (for checkbox selection).

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| id | string | Yes | - | Unique identifier for the tree |
| treeItems | Array<TreeItem> | Yes | - | The tree items that determine what elements show up in the tree |
| dataType | string | No | 'basic' | Type of tree to display. Options: 'basic', 'navigation', 'selectable' |
| expandedItems | Record<string, boolean> | No | {} | Object tracking which items are expanded |
| leafItemSelectionStatus | Record<string, boolean> | No | {} | Object tracking which leaf items are selected |
| disabledItems | Record<string, boolean> | No | {} | Object tracking which items are disabled |
| dataActiveItemId | string | No | - | ID of a TreeItem that will be highlighted as active (mainly used in navigation mode) |
| className | string | No | - | Additional CSS classes |

## Event Handlers

| Name | Parameters | Description |
|------|------------|-------------|
| neonTreeExpandedItemChange | (newValue: Record<string, boolean>, targetItem: TreeItem) => void | Fires when the user expands or collapses a tree item with children |
| neonTreeSelectedItemChange | (targetItem: TreeItem, leafItemSelectionStatus: Record<string, boolean>, parentItemSelectionStatus: Record<string, boolean \| 'indeterminate'>, e: Event) => void | Fires when the user checks or unchecks one of the checkboxes |
| neonActiveItemChange | (targetItem: TreeItem) => void | Fires when the user clicks on one of the links in navigation mode |

## TreeItem Interface

Each tree item supports the following properties:

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| id | string | Unique identifier for the tree item |
| text | string | The main text that shows up for the item |
| subtext | string | Secondary text that shows up for the item |
| icon | string | Main icon for the tree item |
| iconColor | string | Color for the tree item's icon (e.g., 'yellow', 'red', 'teal') |
| tagText | string | Text for a tag |
| tagSubtext | string | Subtext for a tag |
| tagType | string | Type for a tag (defaults to gray) |
| tagIcon | string | Icon for a tag |
| statusIcon | string | Status icon (always shows in gray) |
| url | string | URL for navigation links (only used when dataType="navigation") |
| onUserClick | function | Callback when a link is clicked (only used when dataType="navigation") |
| isParent | boolean | Set to true for parent nodes without immediate children (for lazy loading) |
| children | Array<TreeItem> | Child tree items |

## Examples

Basic tree with icons:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonTree } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { TreeItem } from '@neon/interfaces';

export function BasicTreeExample() {
  const treeItems = [
    {
      id: 'basic-item-1',
      text: 'Basic 1',
      icon: 'folder',
      iconColor: 'yellow',
      children: [
        {id: 'basic-item-1-1', text: 'Basic 1 - 1', icon: 'file-draw', iconColor: 'red'},
        {id: 'basic-item-1-2', text: 'Basic 1 - 2', icon: 'file-document', iconColor: 'orange'},
      ]
    },
    {
      id: 'basic-item-2',
      text: 'Basic 2',
      icon: 'folder',
      iconColor: 'yellow',
      children: [
        {
          id: 'basic-item-2-1',
          text: 'Basic 2 - 1',
          icon: 'folder',
          iconColor: 'yellow',
          children: [
            {id: 'basic-item-2-1-1', text: 'Basic 2 - 1 - 1', icon: 'file-media', iconColor: 'green'},
            {id: 'basic-item-2-1-2', text: 'Basic 2 - 1 - 2', icon: 'file-data', iconColor: 'teal'},
          ]
        },
        {id: 'basic-item-2-2', text: 'Basic 2 - 2', icon: 'file-music', iconColor: 'cyan'},
      ]
    },
    {id: 'basic-item-3', text: 'Basic 3', icon: 'file-image', iconColor: 'purple'},
  ];

  return <NeonTree
    id="basic-tree"
    treeItems={treeItems}
  />;
}
```

Navigation tree with active item:
```jsx
import React from 'react';
import { NeonTree } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { TreeItem } from '@neon/interfaces';

export function NavigationTreeExample() {
  function onUserClick(item, event) {
    event.preventDefault();
    alert('You clicked on tree item: ' + item.id);
  }

  const treeItems = [
    {
      id: 'navigation-item-1',
      text: 'Navigation 1',
      icon: 'folder',
      iconColor: 'yellow',
      url: 'https://example.com',
      onUserClick,
      children: [
        {id: 'navigation-item-1-1', text: 'Navigation 1 - 1', icon: 'file-draw', iconColor: 'red', url: 'https://example.com', onUserClick},
        {id: 'navigation-item-1-2', text: 'Navigation 1 - 2', icon: 'file-document', iconColor: 'orange', url: 'https://example.com', onUserClick},
      ]
    },
    {id: 'navigation-item-2', text: 'Navigation 2', icon: 'file-image', iconColor: 'purple', url: 'https://example.com', onUserClick},
  ];

  return <NeonTree
    id="navigation-tree"
    dataType="navigation"
    treeItems={treeItems}
    dataActiveItemId="navigation-item-1"
    neonActiveItemChange={(targetItem) => {
      console.log(`Navigating to ${targetItem.text}`);
    }}
  />;
}
```

Selectable tree with checkboxes:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonTree, NeonTag } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { TreeItem } from '@neon/interfaces';
import { getNodeFromTree } from '@neon/exported-utils';

export function SelectableTreeExample() {
  const [selectedItemsArray, setSelectedItemsArray] = useState([]);

  const treeItems = [
    {
      id: 'selectable-item-1',
      text: 'Selectable 1',
      icon: 'folder',
      iconColor: 'yellow',
      children: [
        {id: 'selectable-item-1-1', text: 'Selectable 1 - 1', icon: 'file-draw', iconColor: 'red'},
        {id: 'selectable-item-1-2', text: 'Selectable 1 - 2', icon: 'file-document', iconColor: 'orange'},
      ]
    },
    {id: 'selectable-item-2', text: 'Selectable 2', icon: 'file-image', iconColor: 'purple'},
  ];

  return <div>
    <NeonTree
      id="selectable-tree"
      dataType="selectable"
      treeItems={treeItems}
      neonTreeSelectedItemChange={(targetItem, leafItemSelectionStatus, parentItemSelectionStatus) => {
        const selectedItemsArray = Object.keys(leafItemSelectionStatus)
          .filter(id => leafItemSelectionStatus[id])
          .map(id => getNodeFromTree(treeItems, id))
          .filter(item => item !== null);

        setSelectedItemsArray(selectedItemsArray);
      }}
    />
    <div>
      {
        selectedItemsArray.map(item => (
          <NeonTag key={item.id} dataText={item.text}/>
        ))
      }
    </div>
  </div>;
}
```

Lazy loading tree example:
```jsx
import React, { useState } from 'react';
import { NeonTree } from '@neon/react-adapters';
import { TreeItem } from '@neon/interfaces';

export function LazyLoadingTreeExample() {
  const [treeItems, setTreeItems] = useState([
    {
      id: 'lazy-item-1',
      text: 'Lazy Loading Folder',
      icon: 'folder',
      iconColor: 'yellow',
      isParent: true  // This flag indicates the item has children that will be loaded later
    },
    {id: 'lazy-item-2', text: 'Standard Item', icon: 'file-image', iconColor: 'purple'},
  ]);

  const serverMap = {
    'lazy-item-1': [
      {id: 'lazy-item-1-1', text: 'Lazy Loaded Item 1', icon: 'file-data', iconColor: 'navy'},
      {id: 'lazy-item-1-2', text: 'Lazy Loaded Item 2', icon: 'file-data', iconColor: 'navy'}
    ]
  };

  return <NeonTree
    id="lazy-load-tree"
    treeItems={treeItems}
    neonTreeExpandedItemChange={(newValue, targetItem) => {
      if (targetItem.isParent === true && targetItem.children == null) {
        // Simulate network call with setTimeout
        setTimeout(() => {
          setTreeItems(prevTreeItems => {
            const newTreeItems = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(prevTreeItems)); // deep copy
            const updateTreeItems = (items) => {
              for (const item of items) {
                if (item.id === targetItem.id) {
                  // Load children from server data
                  item.children = serverMap[targetItem.id] || [{
                    id: targetItem.id + '-empty',
                    text: 'No items found'
                  }];
                  return true;
                }
                if (item.children) {
                  if (updateTreeItems(item.children)) {
                    return true;
                  }
                }
              }
              return false;
            };

            updateTreeItems(newTreeItems);
            return newTreeItems;
          });
        }, 500);
      }
    }}
  />;
}
```
